myopia.title: Current Optical Correction and Presenting Vision Among Schoolchildren With Vision Screening-identified Myopia in Yangzhou, China.
myopia.summary: Approximately one-third of students with vision screening-identified myopia had no recorded correction. Screening reports should identify both the use of correction and the presenting visual outcomes. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the current optical correction and present visual outcomes of schoolchildren identified with myopia during vision screening. METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis was conducted of data from 12,106 students aged 6.0-18.99 years in 36 schools in Yangzhou, China. Vision screening-identified myopia was defined using visual acuity (VA) and noncycloplegic refraction; current orthokeratology users were also included. VA is reported in five-mark notation with logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution (logMAR) equivalents. The primary and secondary outcomes were having a current optical correction and presenting corrected bilateral visual acuity (PCVA) ≥ 5.0 (≤0.00 logMAR) in both eyes amongst spectacle users, respectively. myopia.summary: Health advocacy, through multisectoral engagement, can help to contain the myopia epidemic. myopia.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Myopia is becoming an epidemic among children globally, due to increased near screen exposure and reduced outdoor activity. Health advocacy-actions designed to gain political commitment, policy support, and social acceptance for health goals-can help to address this public health challenge. This paper reflects on health advocacy activities undertaken to contain the myopia epidemic and on potential future directions. METHODS: We mapped activities using the American Heart Association (AHA) advocacy framework undertaken in the Netherlands from 2018 to 2026 via the innovative multidisciplinary network 'View Outdoors' (2018), targeting professionals, policymakers, and the public. We used the University of British Columbia (UBC) health advocacy framework perspective to assess the approaches, gaps, and opportunities for the next phase of the movement. myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: The prevalence of myopia is postulated to be rising worldwide, along with the risk of secondary complications, such as maculopathy; however, the evidence for this remains inconclusive, particularly for Europe. The focus is on reducing the increased axial length growth in childhood. To this end, myopia control spectacles (MCS) with peripheral myopic defocus have been developed. METHODS: Review of randomized controlled trials (RCT, ≥ 12 months) reporting axial length (AL) and spherical equivalent refraction (SER) for the MCS technologies currently available in Germany (July 2026): DIMS, HALT, CARE, HAPD. Only absolute effect sizes were considered. RESULTS: A meta-analysis (17 studies, n = 6175) confirmed significant effects at 12 months, which in some cases were no longer significant at 24 months. myopia.summary: Maternal GDM, elevated FPG levels in the third trimester, and poorly-controlled glucose were associated with an increased risk of myopia in offspring.
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between maternal glycemic status and offspring vision remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the longitudinal associations between maternal glucose concentrations during different pregnancies, glycemic control, and myopia in preschool offspring. METHODS: This cohort study enrolled 4227 mother-child pairs with children aged 3-6 years, and incorporated both a prospective analysis and a nested case-control analysis as its sub-studies. In the prospective cohort, suspected myopia was defined as non-cycloplegic spherical equivalent (SE)  ≤ 0.75 D; a stricter SE  ≤ 1.00 D cut-off was used for sensitivity analysis. Clinically-diagnosed myopia cases were extracted from electronic medical information in nested case control analysis. myopia.summary: From a QALY perspective, outdoor activity, 0.01% atropine and myopia-control spectacle lenses, excluding contact lenses and those with volatile results, were cost-effective, with outdoor activity being dominant and HALs being the most favourable alternative. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of multiple myopia control interventions in managing myopia progression from a quality-of-life perspective. METHODS: A Markov cohort model simulated myopia progression over 10 years in children starting treatment at 8 years of age. Cost-effectiveness was evaluated using the incremental cost-utility ratio (ICUR) and incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER), measured as cost per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) gained and cost per disability-adjusted life year (DALY) averted, respectively. Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses assessed model robustness. If an intervention exhibited sensitivity or instability, its cost-effectiveness cannot be determined conclusively within the range of parameter variations. myopia.title: Clinical outcomes and baseline factors associated with one-year axial elongation during orthokeratology wear in children: a retrospective study.
myopia.summary: Children undergoing orthokeratology showed a mean one-year axial elongation of 0.23 mm. Older age, higher baseline myopia, larger pupil diameter and BMI were associated with axial elongation during treatment, with notable sex differences. These findings may help inform individualized orthokeratology management in pediatric myopia.
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myopia has emerged as a major global public health concern, especially in Asia, with high myopia substantially increasing the risk of complications such as retinal degeneration and glaucoma. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of orthokeratology (Ortho-K) in controlling axial length (AL) elongation in myopic children over a one-year period and to identify baseline predictors of treatment response. METHODS: This retrospective, single-group, pre-post control study included 122 children (244 eyes) with myopia who were fitted with orthokeratology lenses at Jiangyin People's Hospital between January 2024 and December 2025 and completed one year of follow-up. Baseline data, including age, body mass index (BMI), spherical equivalent (SE), pupil diameter (PD), and axial length (AL) were collected. myopia.title: Effectiveness of spectacle lenses with highly aspherical lenslets (HAL) in slowing axial elongation and spherical equivalent refraction progression in myopic and pre-myopic children: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
myopia.summary: Current evidence suggests that HAL spectacle lenses may slow axial elongation and SER progression in myopic children. In pre-myopic children, HAL lenses may offer a smaller benefit, particularly with high adherence, but the evidence is limited and of low quality, precluding a strong recommendation for routine myopia prevention. …
myopia.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the efficacy of highly aspherical lenslet (HAL) spectacle lenses on axial length (AL) elongation and spherical equivalent refraction (SER) progression in myopic and pre-myopic Children. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, VIP, and WanFang databases were systematically searched from inception to June 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCT) and prospective cohort studies comparing HAL lenses with single-vision lenses (SVL) for myopia control or prevention were included. Two investigators independently screened literature, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias. Meta-analysis was performed using RevMan 5.4 software. myopia.title: Trends in real-world atropine prescribing for myopia control across evidence eras.
myopia.summary: A clear shift in atropine prescribing patterns for pediatric myopia management was identified over the course of the study period. During the Early Low-Dose Atropine Era, clinicians exclusively prescribed the lowest concentration of atropine (0.01%), and only a small proportion of patients were escalated to a higher concentration at 12 mo …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Identify trends in atropine prescribing and concentration adjustments for pediatric myopia control across multiple U.S. academic eye centers. METHODS: A multicenter, retrospective chart review was conducted of children (ages 3-17 years) prescribed low-concentration atropine for myopia management at three academic medical centers in the United States: the Casey Eye Institute, Oregon Health & Science University, the Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago, and the Rady Children's Hospital Orange County. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize the data and summarize prescribing patterns, concentration changes, and follow-up rates by enrollment period and initial atropine concentration. myopia.title: Variations in Corneal Refractive Change Region After Orthokeratology Lens Wear.
myopia.summary: Orthokeratology induces measurable changes in the height and volume of the CRC region. Both parameters are important for evaluating myopia control outcomes, and our findings provide guidance for clinical lens selection.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: This study analyzed 1-year longitudinal variations in the corneal refractive change (CRC) region after orthokeratology (Ortho-K) lens wear between vision shaping treatment (VST) and corneal refractive therapy (CRT) designs. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 148 patients with myopia (148 eyes) treated with Ortho-K lenses for 12 months at Beijing Tongren Hospital's myopia clinic from June 2020 to December 2022. Participants were divided into two groups: group A (74 eyes) who wore VST design Ortho-K lens, and group B (74 eyes) who wore CRT design lens. Data from the right eyes were collected. Measurements included tangential corneal topography maps, which were converted into refractive power maps to calculate the area, height, and volume of the CRC region. myopia.title: Short-term visual and ocular responses to a myopia control contact lens: influence of optical zones and hydration techniques.
myopia.summary: The evaluated contact lenses showed good short-term performance and tolerance. A smaller central optical zone was associated with modest reductions in contrast sensitivity and perceived visual quality, without clear advantages in other outcomes. Hydration modality did not influence performance.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the short-term visual performance, subjective acceptance, tear film stability, and ocular physiological response after 1 h of wear of a monthly replacement soft contact lens for myopia control with different central optical zone diameters and hydration modalities. METHODS: Thirty myopic young adults (21 ± 1 years) were fitted monocularly with three centre-distance multifocal designs: 3.9 mm optical zone with bulk hydration, 3.9 mm with blister hydration, and 3.6 mm with bulk hydration. A no-contact lens condition served as baseline. High-contrast visual acuity (CDVA) and contrast sensitivity function (CSF) under photopic and mesopic conditions, tear film parameters (tear meniscus heigh, non-invasive tear break-up time), and Likert scales (visual quality, comfort, satisfaction) were assessed using a repeated-measures design. myopia.title: Systematic review of atropine cost-effectiveness in childhood myopia management.
myopia.summary: Studies demonstrate favourable economic value using diverse metrics, including cost per diopter reduction, cost ratios, and cost-utility estimates, rather than uniformly reported ICERs. …
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood myopia is a global public health concern, with rising prevalence and a significant economic burden due to complications like retinal detachment and macular degeneration. Low-dose atropine (LDA) range 0.01%-0.05% is a clinically effective intervention for slowing myopia progression. However, its economic value remains under-evaluated across diverse settings. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251009680) to assess the cost-effectiveness of atropine for myopia management in children. Four model-based economic evaluations met the inclusion criteria, from Hong Kong, New Zealand, Australia/China and France/United Kingdom. myopia.title: Twelve-Month Efficacy and Visual Tolerability of MyoPi Spectacle Lenses in Childhood Myopia: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
myopia.summary: In children with myopia, MyoPi continuous free-form defocus spectacle lenses slowed 12-month axial elongation and cycloplegic refractive progression compared with single-vision spectacles, with acceptable overall safety and visual tolerability.
myopia.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the 12-month efficacy, safety, and visual tolerability of MyoPi continuous free-form defocus spectacle lenses compared with conventional single-vision spectacle lenses (SVLs) in children with myopia. DESIGN: Prospective, multicenter, randomized, single-masked, parallel-group clinical trial. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 116 eligible children were randomized 1:1 to MyoPi or SVLs. Eligible participants were 8 to 13 years of age with bilateral cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction (SER) from -0.75 to -5.00 diopters (D). METHODS: Participants were randomized 1:1 to MyoPi or single-vision spectacle lenses and were followed at baseline, week 1, month 3, month 6, and month 12. myopia.title: A novel progressive defocus rigid gas permeable contact lenses for controlling axial elongation in myopic children: a retrospective study.
myopia.summary: Daily wearing of the DRGP lenses significantly curbs axial elongation in children when compared with SV lenses.
myopia.abstract: AIM: To evaluate the efficacy of progressive defocus rigid gas permeable (DRGP) contact lenses in slowing down myopic progression and analyze the factors may influence axial length (AL) elongation in myopic children. METHODS: This was a retrospective study conducted on school-age children with myopia of -5.00 D or higher who were fitted with DRGP lenses. A matched control group wearing single-vision (SV) spectacles was selected based on comparable baseline age and refractive error. The AL was measured at baseline and at 6-month intervals thereafter. Changes in AL were compared between the groups. RESULTS: The DRGP lenses group comprised 56 subjects (39 females, mean age 11.96±2.32y), the SV spectacle group comprised 53 subjects (29 females, mean age 11.09±2.33y). myopia.title: Development and external validation of a prediction model for suboptimal orthokeratology control in adolescents.
myopia.summary: The study constructs a risk prediction model to forecast the likelihood that myopic adolescents will not achieve the ideal control effect after wearing OK lenses, offering proactive and effective guidance for frontline clinical practitioners in devising diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
myopia.abstract: AIM: To develop and externally validate a risk prediction model for adolescents wearing orthokeratology (OK) lenses to predict the probability of suboptimal control effects. METHODS: A retrospective analysis of myopic children who used OK lenses consistently for at least 18mo between January 2021 and March 2023 were conducted. Various ophthalmic examinations and recorded baseline parameters were performed. A risk prediction model was developed using multifactorial logistic regression analysis, and the model's discrimination and calibration were assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and Brier score. RESULTS: The modeling group included 228 eyes (mean age, 10.46±1.99y; 55.7% males), with 120 right eyes (52.6%) and 108 left eyes (47.4%), and the validation group included 100 eyes. myopia.abstract: High myopia in children risks irreversible visual impairment, yet optimal interventions remain debated. This multicenter double-blind, randomized-controlled trial aims to evaluate the effect and safety of different atropine eyedrops for myopia control in children with high myopia, conducted in Shanghai Eye Diseases Prevention and Treatment Center, Shanghai General Hospital and Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital. Recruitment started on July 4th, 2021 and final follow-up was August, 21st, 2024. 219 children aged 6-12 years with myopia of at least -5.0 diopter (D) were recruited and randomly assigned to use either 0.01%(N = 76), 0.04%(N = 72), or 0.10%(N = 71) atropine eyedrops once nightly for both eyes over 24 months, and 182 participants completed trial; 219 (76:72:71) randomized cases were analyzed. myopia.summary: Vergence and accommodation of young myopic adults following the cessation of long-term atropine therapy for myopia progression differed from that of young myopic adults with no prior atropine use. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Myopia is a worldwide health concern due to its increasing prevalence and associated pathology, visual dysfunction, societal and quality of life impacts. Despite widespread use of atropine in Taiwan to manage myopia, its prevalence has increased. It has been suggested that the efficacy of atropine in slowing myopia progression may be limited by binocular vision (BV) function. Furthermore, the long-term impacts of atropine are unknown. This study aimed to contrast the BV profile of young myopic adults following cessation of atropine therapy for myopia control, relative to myopic adults without this history. METHODS: From a pool of young myopic adults attending a vision screening (n = 1320), 204 myopic (≤-0.50 dioptres, D) adults were invited for further clinical evaluation. myopia.summary: Myopia prevalence and visual behavior patterns in preschool children in Shunyi District are homogenized between urban and rural areas. In this age group, parental myopia is the only statistically significant independent predictor of childhood myopia (OR = 4.87). …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate urban-rural differences in refractive status among children aged 3-6 years in Shunyi District, Beijing, and their associations with daily visual behaviors, as well as to ascertain the relative contributions of familial risk and environmental factors in this population. METHODS: A total of 1,142 children (527 in urban areas and 615 in townships) from 11 kindergartens in Shunyi District were selected through stratified cluster random sampling. After fully paralyzing the ciliary muscle with 1% cyclopentolate, computerized refraction was performed to calculate the spherical equivalent (SE). Standardized questionnaires were used to obtain eye-use duration, eye-use distance, outdoor activity time and parental myopia history. myopia.summary: Compared with SV, OK lenses suppress AL elongation and SE progression. There are increases in ChT and 3D-CVI associated with this suppression, suggesting that ChT and 3D-CVI may serve as biomarkers for evaluating the efficacy of myopia-control interventions and supporting further investigation of their role in mechanism of myopia control.
myopia.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the longitudinal effects of single-vision spectacles (SV) and orthokeratology (OK) lenses on choroidal structure and microcirculation in adolescents with myopia, and to analyze differences in responses between the two correction modalities. METHODS: This prospective, nonrandomized cohort study enrolled myopic patients aged 8 to 15 years. Axial length (AL), spherical equivalent refraction (SE), choroidal thickness (ChT), and three-dimensional choroidal vascularity index (3D-CVI) in nine macular sectors within concentric rings of 1, 3, and 6 mm in diameter were measured at baseline and at 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year after lens wear. myopia.summary: This prospective cohort study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of modified posterior scleral reinforcement (PSR) combined with comprehensive therapy versus conventional optical correction for controlling myopia progression in patients with high and pathologic myopia. …
myopia.abstract: This prospective cohort study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of modified posterior scleral reinforcement (PSR) combined with comprehensive therapy versus conventional optical correction for controlling myopia progression in patients with high and pathologic myopia. A total of 203 patients aged 8-18 years were allocated, based on preference, to either the combination therapy group (n = 111; receiving modified PSR plus low-concentration atropine and/or peripheral defocus optical correction) or the conventional control group (n = 92; fitted with rigid gas-permeable contact lenses only). After accounting for 10 withdrawals during the study period, 193 patients completed the 24-month follow-up (combination group, n = 102; control group, n = 91) and were included in the final analysis. myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To computationally evaluate how single vision (SV), concentric bifocal (BF), and a contact lens with non-refractive opaque elements (AR) lens designs modulate retinal ganglion cell (RGC) activity. METHODS: Wide-field retinal simulations were generated using a schematic myopic eye corrected with SV, BF, and AR designs across three stimuli (Lena image, logMAR chart, dynamic gratings), three pupil diameters, and three residual accommodative error configurations. For each configuration, retinal image montages emulating blink-induced on-eye lens movement over one second were processed through a multilayer biomimetic virtual retina model to simulate RGC spike trains, quantified using median absolute deviation (MAD) and up-crossing rate (UCR). myopia.title: Atropine, red-light therapy, and lenslet spectacles for premyopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
myopia.summary: Available randomized evidence suggests that some interventions may reduce early refractive change in children classified as premyopic, while effects on axial elongation remain less certain. Atropine had the largest evidence base, but certainty was low for SE and very low for AL. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Earlier onset of childhood myopia is associated with greater subsequent progression and a higher risk of high myopia and related ocular complications. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether low-concentration atropine, repeated low-level red-light therapy (RLRL), and study-specific lenslet-array spectacle designs reduce refractive change and axial elongation in non-myopic children classified as premyopic. METHODS: This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251252431) and conducted according to PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception to 17 July 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials with follow-up ranging from 3 to 24 months that included children meeting study-specific criteria for premyopia and reported cycloplegic spherical equivalent (SE) and/or axial length (AL). myopia.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the 24-month efficacy of combining highly aspherical lenslet target (HALT) spectacle lenses with low-dose atropine (LDA) in children with poor response to atropine monotherapy. Methods: This prospective interventional cohort study included myopic children aged 6-11 years who continued to progress despite LDA (0.01-0.025%). Fifty children completed 12 months of follow-up and 48 completed 24 months. At 12 months, atropine dosage was maintained, reduced, or increased according to clinical discretion. Cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction (SER) and axial length (AL) were measured at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. myopia.abstract: Background/Objectives: Repeated low-level red-light (RLRL) therapy has recently emerged as a promising treatment for childhood myopia. Choroidal thickening has been proposed as a key biological mechanism underlying its therapeutic efficacy; however, evidence regarding its effects on subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT), particularly in children with premyopia, remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to comprehensively evaluate the effects of RLRL therapy on SFCT in pediatric patients with myopia and premyopia. Methods: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were systematically searched from database inception through 29 September 2026. Methods: A total of 39 eyes from 39 participants (mean age: 11.1 ± 1.54 years, ranging from 6 to 13 years) were included. Participants underwent an eye examination and were assigned to one of three studied lenses: multifocal contact lenses with either non-adjustable (Biofinity Multifocal) or adjustable parameters (Gentle 80 Multifocal), or a contact lens designed for myopia control (MYLO). After six months of lens wear, a refractive assessment was performed and topographic images of the eye with the contact lens fitted were taken. myopia.title: The economic burden of myopia diagnosis and treatment: A cross-sectional cost-of-illness study in Yantai, China.
myopia.summary: Myopia imposes a substantial economic burden in Yantai, especially among younger individuals, those with early-onset myopia, individuals with lower educational attainment, and those using expensive correction methods.
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myopia has become a major global public health and economic issue. Population-based cost-of-illness evidence from prefecture-level cities in China remains limited. This study aimed to quantify the direct economic burden of myopia diagnosis and treatment among individuals aged 6 to 55 years in Yantai, China, and to identify factors associated with per-capita direct myopia expenditure. METHODS: A cross-sectional cost-of-illness study was conducted between September and November 2021 in Yantai. A multistage sampling strategy was used to recruit students and their parents from primary schools, middle schools, high schools/vocational schools, and universities. Questionnaire data on demographic characteristics, myopia status, correction methods, healthcare utilization, and costs were collected. myopia.abstract: The global myopia epidemic, especially among children, poses a major public health burden. Orthokeratology (OK) is an established intervention for slowing myopia progression, yet its conventional practice is constrained by variable treatment responses, an experience-dependent fitting process, and the need for vigilant long-term safety monitoring. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers an approach to enhance precision, efficiency, and accessibility across the entire OK care cycle. This review assesses AI applications in OK, encompassing pre-treatment efficacy prediction, AI-assisted lens fitting and automated fit assessment during treatment, and post-treatment safety monitoring with complication risk alert. myopia.title: Retinal Sensitive Areas in Myopia Control: Identifying the Potential Retinal 'Sweet Spot'-A Scoping Review.

myopia.abstract: Myopia control may involve targeting the peripheral retina to slow eye growth; however, there is no consensus on the optimal lens design, and treatment effects remain variable. This scoping review explored whether a specific retinal region is sensitive to visual manipulation, which could inform more effective treatments. A literature search was conducted in December 2025, with updates in March and June 2026 using PubMed, MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Library. Full manuscripts in English in animals and humans were included and screened by title, abstract, and full text for relevance. A total of 134 studies were identified, with 22 meeting inclusion criteria (13 human, 9 animal studies). Evidence across studies suggests that both the extent and location of defocus influence axial elongation. myopia.abstract: An 18-month prospective, non-randomized comparative observational study evaluated the effects of different optical corrections on myopia progression, binocular vision, and visual performance in Spanish children. Forty-five myopic participants aged 9-14 years were allocated to single-vision lenses (SV), low-addition progressive addition lenses (PALs), or defocus-incorporated multiple segments lenses (DIMS). Assessments included spherical equivalent (SE) and axial length (AL), comprehensive accommodative function evaluated by measuring amplitude of accommodation, positive and negative relative accommodation, accommodative facility, and accommodative response, and binocular function evaluated by measuring phorias, fusional vergences, and stereopsis. myopia.abstract: The rising comorbidity of myopia and overweight/obesity (OWOB) in children shares modifiable behavioral pathways, yet evidence for integrated prevention remains limited. We conducted a cluster-randomized, hybrid type I effectiveness-implementation trial in 36 pair-matched Beijing schools. Of 4991 enrolled students in Grades 1-4 and 7, 3426 (68.6%) completed the 12-month follow-up. The school-centered "22510SS" intervention targeted outdoor activity, screen time, diet, sleep, and health monitoring. No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in spherical equivalent or BMI change, or in the prevalence of myopia, OWOB, or their comorbidity. The intervention improved the overall behavior-improvement rate (39.7% vs. 33.7%; OR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.00-1.80). myopia.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Intermittent exotropia frequently coexists with childhood myopia. Myopia-control interventions may affect accommodation, convergence or binocular function but evidence specific to children with intermittent exotropia has not been synthesised. This review will assess efficacy in randomised trials and comparative effectiveness and safety in non-randomised studies considering both myopia progression and strabismus-related outcomes. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This protocol follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) 2015 statement. myopia.title: Early Axial Length Response Predicts Long-Term Myopia Control in Children Undergoing Orthokeratology.
myopia.summary: Early AL change after 6 months of OK wear is a useful biomarker for risk‑stratifying long‑term myopia control response. Children with ΔAL₆m ≤ 0.07 mm were much more likely to achieve a favourable AL response, whereas those with ΔAL₆m ≥ 0.09 mm had an elevated risk of poor AL response.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether early axial length (AL) change after 6 months of orthokeratology (OK) wear serves as a clinically meaningful biomarker for predicting long-term myopia control after 2 years. METHODS: This retrospective analysis included 101 children from a multicentre OK cohort who completed 24 months of follow‑up, with AL measured at baseline and at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months. Early AL shortening was defined as a ≥0.01 mm reduction after 6 months. Longitudinal AL change was assessed using linear mixed‑effects models. To evaluate predictive utility, separate logistic regression models were fitted using the 6-month AL change (ΔAL₆m) as a continuous predictor for two predefined AL outcome categories: favourable AL response (ΔAL₂₄m ≤ 0.30 mm) and poor AL response (>0.59 mm). myopia.title: Effect of 0.01%, 0.02% and 0.04% atropine eyedrops vs placebo on myopia incidence in pre-myopic children: A randomized clinical trial.
myopia.summary: Low-concentration atropine demonstrated a dose-response relationship for reducing cumulative myopia incidence and slowing refractive progression in pre-myopic children, but no such relationship on axial length. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the dose-response relationship and individual efficacy of 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.04% atropine eye drops for preventing myopia onset in pre-myopic children. DESIGN: Twelve-month randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial conducted in Shanghai primary schools (March 2023-December 2024). METHODS: Children aged 6-10 years with cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction of -0.50 to + 0.75 diopters (D) were randomized 1:1:1:1 to placebo or 0.01%, 0.02%, or 0.04% atropine once daily. Primary outcome was 12-month cumulative myopia incidence (SER ≤ -0.50 D in the worse eye); secondary outcomes were changes in SER and axial length of the worse eye. Children with ocular or systemic diseases, prior orthokeratology use, or other myopia control interventions were excluded. myopia.title: Axial Length Stabilization and Scleral Curvature Changes following Repeated Low-level Red-light Therapy in Children with High Myopia.
myopia.summary: RLRL therapy was associated with AL stabilization in highly myopic eyes. Although apparent scleral curvature change was observed, it was a post hoc analysis in a small number of eyes and its association with choroidal thickness and the shortening of the AL needs further investigation.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine the incidence and extent of axial length (AL) shortening after 12 months of repeated low-level red-light (RLRL) therapy in highly myopic eyes. In addition, to investigate the relationship between the AL shortening and changes in the posterior scleral curvature in the swept-source optical coherence tomographic (SS-OCT) images. METHODS: Thirty participants aged 8 to 18 years with high myopia were studied. The spherical equivalent of refractive error (SER) and AL were measured, and SS-OCT images were recorded at baseline, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after beginning RLRL therapy. RESULTS: Twelve months of RLRL therapy led to an average reduction in myopic SER by 0.29 D (95% CI, 0.10 to 0.49 D; P < 0.05) and stabilization of AL, with a mean change of -0.03 mm (95% CI, -0.09 to 0.04 mm; P = 1.00). myopia.title: From Corneal Epithelium to Endothelium: Long-Term Corneal Changes in Myopic Children Wearing Daily Disposable Hydrogel Soft Contact Lenses.
myopia.summary: Long-term wear of daily disposable hydrogel SCLs in children did not alter CET and CST significantly over a minimum 10-year period. Corneal endothelial integrity and pleomorphism were maintained, with higher polymegethism observed only in two peripheral regions. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aims to investigate the long-term impact of soft contact lens (SCL) wear on the cornea in children. METHODS: Twenty-one participants who had worn daily disposable hydrogel SCLs for over 10 years (≥10 h/day, 6 days/week) since ages 8-12 years were recruited, together with age-matched controls without contact lens wear. Corneal epithelial (CET) and stromal thickness (CST) were measured using anterior segment optical coherence tomography in central (2 mm), mid-peripheral (2-5 mm) and peripheral (5-6 mm) annular regions. Corneal endothelium was imaged with a non-contact specular microscope to calculate corneal endothelial cell density (ECD), coefficients of variation of cell size (polymegethism, CV,%) and percentage of hexagonal cells (pleomorphism, HEX,%) in the central and six peripheral regions. myopia.title: Diffractive Soft Contact Lenses for Modifying Ocular Longitudinal Chromatic Aberration.
myopia.summary: This study presents the first demonstration of a soft contact lens capable of manipulating ocular LCA, including sign reversal. LIRIC diffractive contact lenses offer a practical platform for tuning the eye's chromatic defocus cues and warrant further investigation as a novel myopia control strategy.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Childhood myopia prevalence is increasing rapidly worldwide, underscoring the need for effective strategies to slow its progression. Longitudinal chromatic aberration (LCA) has been identified as an optical cue for the sign of defocus that may guide childhood eye growth and emmetropisation. Reversing the sign of ocular LCA has been proposed as a myopia control strategy, yet no wearable devices have demonstrated this capability. Here, diffractive soft contact lenses fabricated using laser-induced refractive index change (LIRIC) are introduced to modify ocular LCA. METHODS: Contact lenses were made with four diffractive powers (1.5, 2.0, 3.0 and 6.0 D) using LIRIC, a femtosecond laser writing technique that modifies the internal refractive index of a soft contact lens without altering external geometry. Lens LCA was characterised using a custom multi-wavelength Badal optical bench

myopia.title: Cost-effectiveness of monotherapy and combination therapy for myopia control in Chinese children.
myopia.summary: Under limited budget conditions, outdoor activities and defocus spectacles represent advantageous cost-effective treatment options. When the budget is sufficient, RLRL may be considered a promising option pending confirmation of its long-term safety and effectiveness, and 0.01% atropine combined with DIMS is the preferred cost-effective o …
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myopia poses a major public health and economic burden in China, necessitating cost-effectiveness evaluations of control strategies. We aimed to assess cost-effectiveness of single/combined myopia control in children and adolescents to optimise strategies. METHODS: We conducted a network meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy of myopia control interventions in Chinese children (aged 6-18 years). Annual changes in axial length (AL) and spherical equivalent refraction (SER) were the primary outcomes. Additionally, we used a decision-analytic Markov model with clinical and cost data from China to evaluate 16 myopia control strategies for eight-year-old children over eight years from a patient perspective, with 3% discounting. myopia.title: Combination therapy for myopia control using defocus incorporated multiple segments spectacles in children refractory to higher-dose atropine.
myopia.summary: Combination therapy of atropine and DIMS was effective in myopia control in children with poor response to atropine treatment alone. Further large-scale and long-term studies are needed to confirm these observations.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To explore the efficacy of myopia control by adding defocus incorporated multiple segments (DIMS) spectacles in children who are refractory to higher-dose atropine control. METHODS: This prospective cohort study included children aged 6-14 who had previously used ≥0.125% atropine for at least one year and were later treated with DIMS plus atropine for over six months. Annual axial length (AL) changes during monotherapy and combination therapy were compared using paired t-tests. Generalized estimating equations were used to analyze correlations with outcome variables. RESULTS: In total, 57 eyes from 29 patients (mean age 9.8 years) were included in our final analysis. myopia.summary: Uncorrected astigmatism had an almost identical impact on visual acuity and vision quality in eyes fitted with DF myopia control and SV contact lenses.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To quantify the impact of uncorrected astigmatism in myopic eyes fitted with dual focus (DF) myopia control contact lenses. METHODS: The right eyes of 10 young adult myopes were corrected with standard single vision (SV, Proclear 1 day, CooperVision, Inc.) and DF (MiSight 1 day, CooperVision, Inc.) contact lenses. SV and DF contact lens powers were determined from SV over-refractions and any ocular astigmatism was corrected using cylindrical trial lenses. Visual acuity and subjective vision were measured through added cylindrical trial lenses (0.00DC, 0.75DC, 1.25DC, 1.75DC and 2.25DC) with spherical equivalent adjustments. With the 2.25D astigmatic lenses, spherical trial lenses were also used to focus the front edge, centre and back edge of the interval of Sturm. myopia.summary: These results suggest that 0.125% atropine might induce changes in the retina vasculature in children with myopia and that these changes might correlate with myopia progression. Nevertheless, as a pilot study, this result may need to be confirmed in larger studies.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: The study assessed the microvascular changes in the retina after the use of 0.125% atropine in children with myopia and the association between retinal microvascular changes and the effects of myopia treatment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This is a prospective cohort study. Children with myopia aged 5-18 years old were included in the study. Retina microvascular parameters were measured with spectral domain optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography devices during the follow-up. The main outcome measurements include vessel density of the superficial vascular plexus (SVP), deep vascular plexus, and axial length (AL). RESULTS: A total of 64 eyes of 36 patients were included. A significant decrease in parafoveal vessel density of the SVP was observed in the first 3 months (P = 0.032). myopia.title: Optical Dynamics of Violet and Blue Light in Myopia Development: A Comparative and Historical Analysis.
myopia.summary: The rising prevalence of myopia in children has become a major concern due to its long-term effects on eye health and vision. This increase has prompted extensive research into the environmental and biological factors influencing eye development. …
myopia.abstract: The rising prevalence of myopia in children has become a major concern due to its long-term effects on eye health and vision. This increase has prompted extensive research into the environmental and biological factors influencing eye development. Recent studies highlight the critical role of specific light wavelengths, particularly violet (360-400 nm) and blue (400-500 nm), in regulating eye growth. Violet light is thought to support choroidal health by activating photopigments in the retina, helping to maintain proper eye growth and reduce the risk of myopia. Conversely, the elimination of blue light through blue-blocking lenses has been linked to changes in the refractive dynamics of the eye, potentially contributing to excessive axial elongation a key characteristic of myopia. myopia.summary: Axial elongation during D.S.D.O. spectacle lens wear averaged approximately 0.17 mm/year in this large routine care cohort. Observed changes were lower than both historical external expectations, but these benchmark contrasts are descriptive associations and should not be interpreted as causal efficacy estimates. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe longitudinal axial elongation in children wearing spectacle lenses incorporating Diversified Segmental Defocus Optimization (D.S.D.O.) technology in routine clinical practice and to place the observed change in context using two historical external benchmarks. METHODS: This retrospective cohort included first time D.S.D.O. spectacle lens users with no documented prior myopia control lens wear and bilateral follow up of at least 12 months. Repeated axial length measurements from March 2022 through July 2026 underwent prespecified longitudinal quality control. The primary mixed effects model adjusted for age, sex, baseline axial length, baseline spherical equivalent, and any recorded atropine use. myopia.title: Multipoint Defocus Optics Technology Spectacle Lenses for Myopia Control in Children: A One-Year Interim Analysis of a Randomized Trial.
myopia.summary: PMDOT lenses were not inferior to HAL lenses in controlling myopia progression.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the one-year efficacy of novel partition multipoint defocus optics technology (PMDOT) lenses in slowing myopia progression, compared to lenses with highly aspherical lenslets (HAL). METHODS: This is a 1-year interim analysis of an ongoing 2-year, non-inferiority randomized controlled trial, in which 194 children ages 8 to 13 years with spherical equivalent refraction (SER) of -0.75 to -4.5 diopters (D) were randomized to either the PMDOT or HAL group. The primary outcome of the full trial was the mean between-group difference in SER change at 2 years, and the non-inferiority margin was -0.3 D. Secondary outcomes included changes in axial length (AL), choroidal thickness (ChT), and other biometric parameters, as well as best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) at 2 years and subjective visual experience. myopia.abstract: Myopia is a refractive anomaly, a global public health issue, mainly due to an increase in axial length of the eyeball. Myopia is increasing worldwide with the appearance of a "myopia global growing epidemic". In children under 6 years old, 20 % have abnormalities, the most common of which are primarily refractive abnormalities, followed by strabismus and amblyopia. Myopia presents a major risk of complications, correlated with its severity, such as retinal detachment, retinal neovascularization, early cataracts and glaucoma. In children with high myopia, syndromic myopia must be explored. Early detection of myopia onset and progression is essential to myopia control strategies. The most promising treatments include outdoor activities, defocusing corrective lenses, defocusing contact lenses, orthokeratology and pharmacological treatments with low-dose atropine.

myopia.title: Overnight orthokeratology.
myopia.summary: Overnight orthokeratology lenses are approved in countries all over the world for the temporary reduction in myopia, and recently, one lens design has received regulatory approval for myopia control in Europe. …
myopia.abstract: Overnight orthokeratology lenses are approved in countries all over the world for the temporary reduction in myopia, and recently, one lens design has received regulatory approval for myopia control in Europe. The modern orthokeratology lens has a substantial history from its origins of attempting to flatten the corneal curvature with a spherical rigid contact lens to sophisticated gas permeable lenses, designed to reshape the cornea. These lenses are predominantly prescribed for children to slow myopia progression and limit axial elongation of the eye. This article reviews the peer-reviewed literature on the efficacy of orthokeratology for myopia control, sustainability after treatment is discontinued, and the safety concerns of overnight contact lens wear. Future avenues of research are discussed.

myopia.title: The epidemics of myopia: Aetiology and prevention.
myopia.summary: There is an epidemic of myopia in East and Southeast Asia, with the prevalence of myopia in young adults around 80-90%, and an accompanying high prevalence of high myopia in young adults (10-20%). This may foreshadow an increase in low vision and blindness due to pathological myopia. …
myopia.abstract: There is an epidemic of myopia in East and Southeast Asia, with the prevalence of myopia in young adults around 80-90%, and an accompanying high prevalence of high myopia in young adults (10-20%). This may foreshadow an increase in low vision and blindness due to pathological myopia. These two epidemics are linked, since the increasingly early onset of myopia, combined with high progression rates, naturally generates an epidemic of high myopia, with high prevalences of "acquired" high myopia appearing around the age of 11-13. The major risk factors identified are intensive education, and limited time outdoors. The localization of the epidemic appears to be due to the high educational pressures and limited time outdoors in the region, rather than to genetically elevated sensitivity to these factors. myopia.title: Myopia and orthokeratology for myopia control.
myopia.summary: The prevalence of myopia in children is increasing worldwide and is viewed as a major public health concern. This increase has driven interest in research into myopia prevention and control in children. …
myopia.abstract: The prevalence of myopia in children is increasing worldwide and is viewed as a major public health concern. This increase has driven interest in research into myopia prevention and control in children. Although there is still uncertainty in the risk factors underlying differences in myopia prevalence between ethnic groups, rates in children of East Asian descent are typically higher regardless of where they live. Mounting evidence also suggests that myopia prevalence in children increases with age. Earlier commencement and more rigorous education systems in these countries, resulting in more time spent on near-work activities and less time on outdoor activities, may be responsible for the earlier age of myopia onset. myopia.title: Efficacy in myopia control.
myopia.summary: There is rapidly expanding interest in interventions to slow myopia progression in children and teenagers, with the intent of reducing risk of myopia-associated complications later in life. …
myopia.abstract: There is rapidly expanding interest in interventions to slow myopia progression in children and teenagers, with the intent of reducing risk of myopia-associated complications later in life. Despite many publications dedicated to the topic, little attention has been devoted to understanding 'efficacy' in myopia control and its application. Treatment effect has been expressed in multiple ways, making comparison between therapies and prognosis for an individual patient difficult. Available efficacy data are generally limited to two to three years making long-term treatment effect uncertain. From an evidence-based perspective, efficacy projection should be conservative and not extend beyond that which has been empirically established. myopia.title: Defocus Incorporated Multiple Segments (DIMS) spectacle lenses slow myopia progression: a 2-year randomised clinical trial.
myopia.summary: Daily wear of the DIMS lens significantly retarded myopia progression and axial elongation in myopic children. Our results demonstrated simultaneous clear vision with constant myopic defocus can slow myopia progression.
myopia.abstract: AIM: To determine if 'Defocus Incorporated Multiple Segments' (DIMS) spectacle lenses slow childhood myopia progression. METHODS: A 2-year double-masked randomised controlled trial was carried out in 183 Chinese children aged 8-13 years, with myopia between -1.00 and -5.00 D and astigmatism ≤1.50 D. Children were randomly assigned to wear DIMS (n=93) or single vision (SV) spectacle lenses (n=90). DIMS lens incorporated multiple segments with myopic defocus of +3.50 D. Refractive error (cycloplegic autorefraction) and axial length were measured at 6month intervals. RESULTS: 160 children completed the study, n=79 in the DIMS group and n=81 in the SV group. Average (SE) myopic progressions over 2 years were -0.41±0.06 D in the DIMS group and -0.85±0.08 D in the SV group. myopia.title: Low-Concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression (LAMP) Study: A Randomized, Double-Blinded, Placebo-Controlled Trial of 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% Atropine Eye Drops in Myopia Control.
myopia.summary: The 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% atropine eye drops reduced myopia progression along a concentration-dependent response. All concentrations were well tolerated without an adverse effect on vision-related quality of life. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Low-concentration atropine is an emerging therapy for myopia progression, but its efficacy and optimal concentration remain uncertain. Our study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of low-concentration atropine eye drops at 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% compared with placebo over a 1-year period. DESIGN: Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-masked trial. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 438 children aged 4 to 12 years with myopia of at least -1.0 diopter (D) and astigmatism of -2.5 D or less. METHODS: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% atropine eye drops, or placebo eye drop, respectively, once nightly to both eyes for 1 year. Cycloplegic refraction, axial length (AL), accommodation amplitude, pupil diameter, and best-corrected visual acuity were measured at baseline, 2 weeks, 4 months, 8 months, and 12 months. There is a high prevalence of myopia, 80% to 90%, in young adults in East Asia; myopia has become the leading cause of blindness in this area. As the myopic population increases globally, the severity of its impact is predicted. …
myopia.abstract: Myopia is not a simple refractive error, but an eyesight-threatening disease. There is a high prevalence of myopia, 80% to 90%, in young adults in East Asia; myopia has become the leading cause of blindness in this area. As the myopic population increases globally, the severity of its impact is predicted. Approximately one fifth of the myopic population has high myopia (≥-6 diopters), which results in irreversible vision loss such as retinal detachment, choroidal neovascularization, cataracts, glaucoma, and macular atrophy. The increasing prevalence of school myopia in the past few decades may be a result of gene-environment interactions. However, earlier school myopia onset would accompany faster myopia progression and greater risk of high myopia later in life. myopia.title: Biological Mechanisms of Atropine Control of Myopia.
myopia.summary: Myopia is a global problem that is increasing at an epidemic rate in the world. Although the refractive error can be corrected easily, myopes, particularly those with high myopia, are susceptible to potentially blinding eye diseases later in life. …
myopia.abstract: Myopia is a global problem that is increasing at an epidemic rate in the world. Although the refractive error can be corrected easily, myopes, particularly those with high myopia, are susceptible to potentially blinding eye diseases later in life. Despite a plethora of myopia research, the molecular/cellular mechanisms underlying the development of myopia are not well understood, preventing the search for the most effective pharmacological control. Consequently, several approaches to slowing down myopia progression in the actively growing eyes of children have been underway. So far, atropine, an anticholinergic blocking agent, has been most effective and is used by clinicians in off-label ways for myopia control. Although the exact mechanisms of its action remain elusive and debatable, atropine encompasses a complex interplay with receptors on different ocular tissues at multiple levels

myopia.title: Preventing Myopia.
myopia.summary: Effective pharmacological and optical measures are now available to lessen the progression of myopia. The increasing prevalence of myopia should motivate pediatricians, parents, and schools to pay attention to risk factors such as close-up work and lack of daylight exposure, particularly in view of the increased use of digital media.
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nearsightedness (myopia) has become more common around the world recently, mainly because of changes in visual, educational, and recreational behavior. The question arises how the risk of myopia and its progression can be reduced. This would lessen the prevalence and severity of myopia and also lower the risk of secondary diseases that impair visual acuity. METHODS: The PubMed/Medline database was selectively searched for pertinent literature. RESULTS: The risk of myopia is lowered by exposure to daylight and increased by activities performed at short visual distances (close-up work). A person with little exposure to daylight has a fivefold risk of developing myopia, which can rise as high as a 16-fold risk if that person also performs close-up work. myopia.title: Myopia Prevention and Outdoor Light Intensity in a School-Based Cluster Randomized Trial.
myopia.summary: The school-based outdoor promotion program effectively reduced the myopia change in both nonmyopic and myopic children. Outdoor activities with strong sunlight exposure may not be necessary for myopia prevention. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the effectiveness of a school-based program promoting outdoor activities in Taiwan for myopia prevention and to identify protective light intensities. DESIGN: Multi-area, cluster-randomized intervention controlled trial. PARTICIPANTS: A total 693 grade 1 schoolchildren in 16 schools participated. Two hundred sixty-seven schoolchildren were in the intervention group and 426 were in the control group. METHODS: Initially, 24 schools were randomized into the intervention and control groups, but 5 and 3 schools in the intervention and control groups, respectively, withdrew before enrollment. A school-based Recess Outside Classroom Trial was implemented in the intervention group, in which schoolchildren were encouraged to go outdoors for up to 11 hours weekly. myopia.abstract: Myopia has been predicted to affect approximately 50% of the world's population based on trending myopia prevalence figures. Critical to minimizing the associated adverse visual consequences of complicating ocular pathologies are interventions to prevent or delay the onset of myopia, slow its progression, and to address the problem of mechanical instability of highly myopic eyes. Although treatment approaches are growing in number, evidence of treatment efficacy is variable. This article reviews research behind such interventions under four categories: optical, pharmacological, environmental (behavioral), and surgical. In summarizing the evidence of efficacy, results from randomized controlled trials have been given most weight, although such data are very limited for some treatments. The overall conclusion of this review is that there are multiple avenues for intervention worthy of expl

myopia.title: [Prevention of myopia].
myopia.summary: To avoid complications of high myopia the best solution would be to prevent myopia development from the very beginning. Many studies have suggested that the frequently quoted myopia boom is related to changes in visual experiences during more demanding education and not due to changes in genetic factors. …
myopia.abstract: To avoid complications of high myopia the best solution would be to prevent myopia development from the very beginning. Many studies have suggested that the frequently quoted myopia boom is related to changes in visual experiences during more demanding education and not due to changes in genetic factors. To avoid myopia development it would therefore be best to carry out a better control of visual experience of children. In this article new approaches are described to record and improve visual habits in children, e.g. new sensors attached to the spectacle frames to document brightness, reading distance and reading duration, changes in text contrast polarity during reading, potential role of smartphones and some not yet fully explored orally applied substances to inhibit myopia.

myopia.title: Interventions to slow progression of myopia in children.
myopia.summary: Antimuscarinic topical medication is effective in slowing myopia progression in children. Multifocal lenses, either spectacles or contact lenses, may also confer a small benefit. Orthokeratology contact lenses, although not intended to modify refractive error, were more effective than SVLs in slowing axial elongation. …
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nearsightedness (myopia) causes blurry vision when one is looking at distant objects. Interventions to slow the progression of myopia in children include multifocal spectacles, contact lenses, and pharmaceutical agents. OBJECTIVES: To assess the effects of interventions, including spectacles, contact lenses, and pharmaceutical agents in slowing myopia progression in children. SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL; Ovid MEDLINE; Embase.com; PubMed; the LILACS Database; and two trial registrations up to February 2018. A top up search was done in February 2019. SELECTION CRITERIA: We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs). We excluded studies when most participants were older than 18 years at baseline. myopia.title: Pharmacogenomic Approach to Antimyopia Drug Development: Pathways Lead the Way.
myopia.summary: Myopia is the most common eye disorder in the world which is caused by a mismatch between the optical power of the eye and its excessively long axial length. Recent studies revealed that the regulation of the axial length of the eye occurs via a complex signaling cascade, which originates in the retina and propagates across all ocular tis …
myopia.abstract: Myopia is the most common eye disorder in the world which is caused by a mismatch between the optical power of the eye and its excessively long axial length. Recent studies revealed that the regulation of the axial length of the eye occurs via a complex signaling cascade, which originates in the retina and propagates across all ocular tissues to the sclera. The complexity of this regulatory cascade has made it particularly difficult to develop effective antimyopia drugs. The current pharmacological treatment options for myopia are limited to atropine and 7-methylxanthine, which have either significant adverse effects or low efficacy. In this review, we focus on the recent advances in genome-wide studies of the signaling pathways underlying myopia development and discuss the potential of systems genetics and pharmacogenomic approaches for the development of antimyopia drugs.

myopia.title: Atropine for the treatment of childhood myopia: safety and efficacy of 0.5%, 0.1%, and 0.01% doses (Atropine for the Treatment of Myopia 2).
myopia.summary: Atropine 0.01% has minimal side effects compared with atropine at 0.1% and 0.5%, and retains comparable efficacy in controlling myopia progression.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Our previous study, Atropine for the Treatment of Myopia 1 (ATOM1), showed that atropine 1% eyedrops were effective in controlling myopic progression but with visual side effects resulting from cycloplegia and mydriasis. The aim of this study was to compare efficacy and visual side effects of 3 lower doses of atropine: 0.5%, 0.1%, and 0.01%. DESIGN: Single-center, double-masked, randomized study. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 400 children aged 6-12 years with myopia of at least -2.0 diopters (D) and astigmatism of -1.50 D or less. INTERVENTION: Children were randomly assigned in a 2:2:1 ratio to 0.5%, 0.1%, and 0.01% atropine to be administered once nightly to both eyes for 2 years. Cycloplegic refraction, axial length, accommodation amplitude, pupil diameter, and visual acuity were noted at baseline, 2 weeks, and then every 4 months for 2 years. myopia.title: The complex interactions of retinal, optical and environmental factors in myopia aetiology.
myopia.summary: Myopia is the commonest ocular abnormality but as a research topic remains at the margins of mainstream ophthalmology. The concept that most myopes fall into the category of 'physiological myopia' undoubtedly contributes to this position. …
myopia.abstract: Myopia is the commonest ocular abnormality but as a research topic remains at the margins of mainstream ophthalmology. The concept that most myopes fall into the category of 'physiological myopia' undoubtedly contributes to this position. Yet detailed analysis of epidemiological data linking myopia with a range of ocular pathologies from glaucoma to retinal detachment demonstrates statistically significant disease association in the 0 to -6 D range of 'physiological myopia'. The calculated risks from myopia are comparable to those between hypertension, smoking and cardiovascular disease. In the case of myopic maculopathy and retinal detachment the risks are an order of magnitude greater. This finding highlights the potential benefits of interventions that can limit or prevent myopia progression. myopia.title: Time spent in outdoor activities in relation to myopia prevention and control: a meta-analysis and systematic review.
myopia.summary: Outdoor time is considered to reduce the risk of developing myopia. The purpose is to evaluate the evidence for association between time outdoors and (1) risk of onset of myopia (incident/prevalent myopia); (2) risk of a myopic shift in refractive error and c) risk of progression in myopes only. …
myopia.abstract: Outdoor time is considered to reduce the risk of developing myopia. The purpose is to evaluate the evidence for association between time outdoors and (1) risk of onset of myopia (incident/prevalent myopia); (2) risk of a myopic shift in refractive error and c) risk of progression in myopes only. A systematic review followed by a meta-analysis and a dose-response analysis of relevant evidence from literature was conducted. PubMed, EMBASE and the Cochrane Library were searched for relevant papers. Of the 51 articles with relevant data, 25 were included in the meta-analysis and dose-response analysis. Twenty-three of the 25 articles involved children. Risk ratio (RR) for binary variables and weighted mean difference (WMD) for continuous variables were conducted. myopia.title: Myopia Control 2020: Where are we and where are we heading?
myopia.summary: PURPOSE: This review arms practitioners with the evidence-based information they need to fully manage myopia. RECENT FINDINGS: The recent peer-reviewed literature is critically evaluated to provide a comprehensive analysis of the safety and efficacy of behavioural, optical and pharmaceutical myopia management. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: This review arms practitioners with the evidence-based information they need to fully manage myopia. RECENT FINDINGS: The recent peer-reviewed literature is critically evaluated to provide a comprehensive analysis of the safety and efficacy of behavioural, optical and pharmaceutical myopia management. Importantly, the paper addresses not only who to treat, but how to treat them, and when to stop or modify treatments. Finally, the paper discusses expectations for treatment and why slowing myopia by even 1 dioptre improves long term health outcomes. SUMMARY: The management of an individual child should be underpinned by the evidence-based literature and clinicians must stay alert to ongoing myopia research that will undoubtedly result in an evolution of the standard of care for the myopic and pre-myopic child.

myopia.title: Two-Year Clinical Trial of the Low-Concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression (LAMP) Study: Phase 2 Report.
myopia.summary: Over 2 years, the efficacy of 0.05% atropine observed was double that observed with 0.01% atropine, and it remained the optimal concentration among the studied atropine concentrations in slowing myopia progression.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% atropine eye drops over 2 years to determine which is the optimal concentration for longer-term myopia control. DESIGN: Randomized, double-masked trial extended from the Low-Concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression (LAMP) Study. PARTICIPANTS: Three hundred eighty-three of 438 children (87%) aged 4 to 12 years with myopia of at least -1.0 diopter (D) originally randomized to receive atropine 0.05%, 0.025%, 0.01%, or placebo once daily in both eyes in the LAMP phase 1 study were continued in this extended trial (phase 2). METHODS: Children in the placebo group (phase 1) were switched to receive 0.05% atropine from the beginning of the second-year follow-up, whereas those in the 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% atropine groups continued with the same regimen. myopia.title: Commonly Held Beliefs About Myopia That Lack a Robust Evidence Base.
myopia.summary: There are many hypotheses proposed to explain phenomena in the myopia field. Caution should be exercised in adopting conjecture until a robust evidence base is provided in support.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To subject a number of commonly held beliefs or areas of confusion in the myopia field to scientific scrutiny. METHOD: A collection of statements about myopia are provided with references to demonstrate that a section of the research or clinical community supports the statement. The topics under discussion are reviewed critically with reference to the literature. These outcomes were classified as primary (refractive error and/or axial length), secondary (patient reported outcomes and treatment compliance), and exploratory (peripheral refraction, accommodative changes, ocular alignment, pupil size, outdoor activity/lighting levels, anterior and posterior segment imaging, and tissue biomechanics). myopia.title: The Role of Orthokeratology in Myopia Control: A Review.
myopia.summary: The prevalence of myopia and high myopia has significantly increased worldwide and in the United States. The serious implications of these trends are being recognized. Myopia is not just a minor inconvenience requiring vision correction with glasses or contact lenses, but a disease process creating significant risk of serious vision-threa …
myopia.abstract: The prevalence of myopia and high myopia has significantly increased worldwide and in the United States. The serious implications of these trends are being recognized. Myopia is not just a minor inconvenience requiring vision correction with glasses or contact lenses, but a disease process creating significant risk of serious vision-threatening eye disease. Various methods of treatment for myopia and myopic progression have been prescribed and studied in effort to find one that is effective, safe, and that patients will be compliant with. Numerous peer-reviewed studies have shown orthokeratology (OrthoK) is effective in slowing myopic progression. This review article covers the development of OrthoK, its mechanism of action, its evolution, and refinement from a refractive option to its use as a mean of slowing myopic progression. myopia.title: Retardation of myopia in Orthokeratology (ROMIO) study: a 2-year randomized clinical trial.
myopia.summary: On average, subjects wearing ortho-k lenses had a slower increase in axial elongation by 43% compared with that of subjects wearing single-vision glasses. Younger children tended to have faster axial elongation and may benefit from early ortho-k treatment. (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00962208.).
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: This single-masked randomized clinical trial aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of orthokeratology (ortho-k) for myopic control. METHODS: A total of 102 eligible subjects, ranging in age from 6 to 10 years, with myopia between 0.50 and 4.00 diopters (D) and astigmatism not more than 1.25D, were randomly assigned to wear ortho-k lenses or single-vision glasses for a period of 2 years. Axial length was measured by intraocular lens calculation by a masked examiner and was performed at the baseline and every 6 months. This study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, number NCT00962208. RESULTS: In all, 78 subjects (37 in ortho-k group and 41 in control group) completed the study. myopia.summary: This network analysis indicates that a range of interventions can significantly reduce myopia progression when compared with single vision spectacle lenses or placebo. In terms of refraction, atropine, pirenzepine, and progressive addition spectacle lenses were effective. …

METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to August 2014. We selected randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving interventions for controlling the progression of myopia in children with a treatment duration of at least 1 year for analysis. myopia.summary: Myopia is an important public health problem due to its prevalence and significant public health cost. myopia.abstract: Myopia is an important public health problem due to its prevalence and significant public health cost. Elevating levels of myopia increase the risk of vision impairment, and therefore, high myopia has become one of the main causes of untreatable vision loss throughout the world due to its irreversible complications. At present, many options for slowing progression of myopia have already been proposed and evaluated such as progressive addition of executive bifocal spectacle lenses, peripheral defocusing lenses, overnight orthokeratology, pharmacological agents such as atropine eye drops, and multifocal soft contact lenses (MFSCLs). Use of MFSCLs has especially increased in recent years due to the growing demand to slow myopia progression during patient's adolescent growth period to avoid pathological myopia in adulthood. myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: A trend that myopia is becoming gradually more common is shown in studies worldwide. Highest frequencies have been found in East Asian urban populations (96.5%) but also a study in Europe shows that nearly half of the 25-29 year olds has myopia. With the increase in prevalence, high myopia, i.e. a spherical equivalent of -6 or more and an axial length of 26 mm or more is also on the rise. High myopia particularly carries a significant risk of ocular pathology related to the long axial length. This highlights the need for myopia management in children with progressive myopia, in particular progression to high myopia. myopia.summary: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Myopia refers to a refractive state of the eye that can predispose to visually significant ocular disease. The prevalence of myopia is increasing worldwide. Researchers internationally have been investigating methods to slow down its progression to prevent sight-threatening complications. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Myopia refers to a refractive state of the eye that can predispose to visually significant ocular disease. The prevalence of myopia is increasing worldwide. Researchers internationally have been investigating methods to slow down its progression to prevent sight-threatening complications. In this article, we perform a review of the current literature discussing interventions for preventing pediatric myopic progression. RECENT FINDINGS: Various interventions, including lifestyle modification, optical methods, and pharmacologic approaches, have been proposed to help control myopic progression. myopia.title: Combined Orthokeratology with Atropine for Children with Myopia: A Meta-Analysis.
myopia.summary: Our study suggests that the combination of OK and 0.01% atropine is more effective in slowing axial elongation than OK monotherapy in children with myopia in a relatively short duration of treatment. In addition, the combination therapy has no negative influence on UCVA, CECD, and IOP.
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myopia has become a worldwide public health issue, which is occurring at a younger age, leading to an increased risk of high myopia. Ocular complications associated with high myopia can lead to irreversible vision loss. It is urgent and critical to explore effective treatment to slow down or even stop the progression of myopia in young children. OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study was to evaluate the additive effects of orthokeratology (OK) and 0.01% atropine ophthalmic solution for myopia in children. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Cochrane Library, EMBASE, MEDLINE, Web of science, Ovid, EBSCO host, CNKI, and CBM to collect eligible studies. myopia.title: Effects of orthokeratology on axial length growth in myopic anisometropes.
myopia.summary: Ortho-k treatment slows AL growth in the more myopic eye of anisometropic patients; should the contralateral eye develop myopia in the future, ortho-k is capable of slowing down AL growth in that eye as well.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the effect of orthokeratology (ortho-k) lens wear on axial length (AL) growth in juvenile myopic anisometropes. METHODS: This retrospective study consisted of two parts. In Part One, 25 anisometropic participants (mean age, 11.2 ± 1.9 years; 11 females and 14 males) were fitted with ortho-k lenses in the more myopic eye only, and the rate of AL growth was compared between the ortho-k lens wearing eye and the untreated contralateral eye over an average period of 23.1 ± 8.3 months. In Part Two, 8 participants who developed myopia in the contralateral eye received ortho-k treatment in both eyes for an average of 12 months; the rate of AL growth before and after ortho-k treatment in the newly developed myopic eye was compared. myopia.title: [Biological mechanisms of myopia].
myopia.summary: Recent studies have confirmed that the prevalence of myopia has increased in most countries, that the increase must be due to environmental factors and that myopia is closely linked to the level of education. …
myopia.abstract: Recent studies have confirmed that the prevalence of myopia has increased in most countries, that the increase must be due to environmental factors and that myopia is closely linked to the level of education. Extensive close-up work with short viewing distances, little outdoor activity and continuous exposure to low illumination are currently considered the major factors. It remains unknown how close-up work can stimulate eye growth. Animal models provide the possibility to manipulate visual experiences and to observe subsequent changes in eye growth. They have uncovered a number of unexpected aspects which have led to studies in children. myopia.summary: Over 5 years, atropine 0.01% eyedrops were more effective in slowing myopia progression with less visual side effects compared with higher doses of atropine.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the safety and efficacy of different concentrations of atropine eyedrops in controlling myopia progression over 5 years. DESIGN: Randomized, double-masked clinical trial. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 400 children originally randomized to receive atropine 0.5%, 0.1%, or 0.01% once daily in both eyes in a 2:2:1 ratio. METHODS: Children received atropine for 24 months (phase 1), after which medication was stopped for 12 months (phase 2). Children who had myopia progression (≥-0.50 diopters [D] in at least 1 eye) during phase 2 were restarted on atropine 0.01% for a further 24 months (phase 3). MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Change in spherical equivalent and axial length over 5 years. myopia.title: Strategies to Regulate Myopia Progression With Contact Lenses: A Review.
myopia.summary: CLs were reported to be well accepted, consistent, and safe methods to address myopia regulation in children. Corneal refractive therapy (orthokeratology) is so far the method with the largest demonstrated efficacy in myopia regulation across different ethnic groups. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Higher myopic refractive errors are associated with serious ocular complications that can put visual function at risk. There is respective interest in slowing and if possible stopping myopia progression before it reaches a level associated with increased risk of secondary pathology. The purpose of this report was to review our understanding of the rationale(s) and success of contact lenses (CLs) used to reduce myopia progression. METHODS: A review commenced by searching the PubMed database. The inclusion criteria stipulated publications of clinical trials evaluating the efficacy of CLs in regulating myopia progression based on the primary endpoint of changes in axial length measurements and published in peer-reviewed journals. myopia.title: Post-traumatic pseudomyopia.
myopia.summary: Pseudomyopia is one of many ocular and behavioral sequelae following TBI. By understanding the natural course and potential management options for post-traumatic pseudomyopia, the clinician will be better prepared to deal with these challenging cases. …
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Many clinicians have noted that patients demonstrate a myopic refractive change following Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI). This apparent myopic shift disappears with cycloplegia, yet stubbornly reappears as soon as the pharmaceutical effect wears off. We propose that this shift is secondary to an irritative lesion that affects the parasympathetic innervation, resulting in ciliary body contracture. The dilemma for the clinician is whether to provide the immediate relief of clear distance vision by prescribing additional minus lenses, or to work toward attempting to re-establish the baseline refractive error. myopia.summary: Topical atropine was well tolerated and effective in slowing the progression of low and moderate myopia and ocular axial elongation in Asian children.
