contactlens.title: Bacterial biofilm formation on implantable devices and approaches to its treatment and prevention
contactlens.summary: In living organisms, biofilms are defined as complex communities of bacteria residing within an exopolysaccharide matrix that adheres to a surface. In the clinic, they are typically the cause of chronic, nosocomial, and medical device-related infections. …
contactlens.abstract: In living organisms, biofilms are defined as complex communities of bacteria residing within an exopolysaccharide matrix that adheres to a surface. In the clinic, they are typically the cause of chronic, nosocomial, and medical device-related infections. Due to the antibiotic-resistant nature of biofilms, the use of antibiotics alone is ineffective for treating biofilm-related infections. In this review, we present a brief overview of concepts of bacterial biofilm formation, and current state-of-the-art therapeutic approaches for preventing and treating biofilms. Also, we have reviewed the prevalence of such infections on medical devices and discussed the future challenges that need to be overcome in order to successfully treat biofilms using the novel technologies being developed.

contactlens.title: Hydrogels: Properties and Applications in Biomedicine
contactlens.summary: Hydrogels are crosslinked polymer chains with three-dimensional (3D) network structures, which can absorb relatively large amounts of fluid. Because of the high water content, soft structure, and porosity of hydrogels, they closely resemble living tissues. …
contactlens.abstract: Hydrogels are crosslinked polymer chains with three-dimensional (3D) network structures, which can absorb relatively large amounts of fluid. Because of the high water content, soft structure, and porosity of hydrogels, they closely resemble living tissues. Research in recent years shows that hydrogels have been applied in various fields, such as agriculture, biomaterials, the food industry, drug delivery, tissue engineering, and regenerative medicine. Along with the underlying technology improvements of hydrogel development, hydrogels can be expected to be applied in more fields. contactlens.title: Wearable sensors: modalities, challenges, and prospects
contactlens.summary: Wearable sensors have recently seen a large increase in both research and commercialization. However, success in wearable sensors has been a mix of both progress and setbacks. Most of commercial progress has been in smart adaptation of existing mechanical, electrical and optical methods of measuring the body. …
contactlens.abstract: Wearable sensors have recently seen a large increase in both research and commercialization. However, success in wearable sensors has been a mix of both progress and setbacks. Most of commercial progress has been in smart adaptation of existing mechanical, electrical and optical methods of measuring the body. This adaptation has involved innovations in how to miniaturize sensing technologies, how to make them conformal and flexible, and in the development of companion software that increases the value of the measured data. However, chemical sensing modalities have experienced greater challenges in commercial adoption, especially for non-invasive chemical sensors. There have also been significant challenges in making significant fundamental improvements to existing mechanical, electrical, and optical sensing modalities, especially in improving their specificity of detection. contactlens.title: Technology Roadmap for Flexible Sensors
contactlens.summary: Humans rely increasingly on sensors to address grand challenges and to improve quality of life in the era of digitalization and big data. For ubiquitous sensing, flexible sensors are developed to overcome the limitations of conventional rigid counterparts. …
contactlens.abstract: Humans rely increasingly on sensors to address grand challenges and to improve quality of life in the era of digitalization and big data. For ubiquitous sensing, flexible sensors are developed to overcome the limitations of conventional rigid counterparts. Despite rapid advancement in bench-side research over the last decade, the market adoption of flexible sensors remains limited. To ease and to expedite their deployment, here, we identify bottlenecks hindering the maturation of flexible sensors and propose promising solutions. We first analyze challenges in achieving satisfactory sensing performance for real-world applications and then summarize issues in compatible sensor-biology interfaces, followed by brief discussions on powering and connecting sensor networks. lens.abstract: Corneal alkali burn causes persistent inflammation, fibrosis, neovascularization, and vision impairment. Although amniotic membrane (AM) transplantation and mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-based therapies have shown therapeutic potential, their combined application as a tissue-engineered construct for alkali-induced corneal injury remains insufficiently explored. Here, we developed a decellularized AM-based bone marrow-derived MSC (BMSC) composite and evaluated its therapeutic effects in a mouse model of corneal alkali burn. Compared with AM transplantation or subconjunctival BMSC injection alone, the BMSC-AM composite more effectively reduced corneal opacity and neovascularization, restored epithelial integrity and stromal architecture, and suppressed inflammatory and fibrotic responses. lens.abstract: Corneal innervation is essential for ocular surface homeostasis and protection, yet methods for selectively labeling and manipulating cornea-projecting neurons remain limited. Conventional retrograde tracers can identify cornea-projecting cell bodies in the trigeminal ganglion (TG), but they do not enable the expression of genetically encoded effector proteins, sensors, or recombinases. We describe and validate intrastromal adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery as an approach for labeling cornea-projecting TG neurons in mice. A 1-2-μL viral injection was delivered into the corneal stroma and labeling was assessed 2-12 weeks later in cleared whole TG, TG sections, corneal whole mounts, and thick brainstem sections. lens.abstract: This study compared five wearable sensors (VEET, Clouclip, Actiwatch, ActLumus, and GENEActiv) for quantification of myopia-related environmental exposures. Thirty participants (27.8 ± 7.0 years) simultaneously wore two spectacle-mounted and three wrist-worn sensors for one day while maintaining a detailed activity log. Data were binned by viewing distance (near: 15- < 60 cm, intermediate: 60- < 100 cm, far: ≥100 cm) and illumination (scotopic: <3 lux, mesopic: 3 to < 30 lux, indoor photopic: 30 to <1000 lux, outdoor photopic: ≥ 1000 lux). The VEET recorded significantly more near and intermediate time than the Clouclip (p < 0.001). Activity logs yielded significantly lower near viewing compared to the VEET (p < 0.001) and Clouclip (p = 0.048) and higher intermediate viewing time (p < 0.001). lens.title: Fluid fluctuation and visual outcomes in neovascular age-related macular degeneration: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
lens.summary: Fluctuation in retinal thickness and fluid during anti-vascular endothelial growrh factor (VEGF) therapy has emerged as a candidate prognostic biomarker in neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), but the evidence is heterogeneous and has not been quantitatively synthesized. …
lens.abstract: Fluctuation in retinal thickness and fluid during anti-vascular endothelial growrh factor (VEGF) therapy has emerged as a candidate prognostic biomarker in neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), but the evidence is heterogeneous and has not been quantitatively synthesized. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to December, 2025, for studies reporting retinal fluid or thickness fluctuation metrics and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) outcomes in eyes receiving anti-VEGF therapy for nAMD, including both observational studies and post hoc analyses of randomized trials. Between-group mean differences (MDs) in BCVA change were pooled using random-effects models, stratified by study design and OCT parameter, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. lens.title: Inactivation of microorganisms in the complex regions of transvaginal ultrasound probes by a UVC-LED light based disinfection system.
lens.summary: Endocavity ultrasound transducers, particularly transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS) probes, contain intricate structures such as notches, grooves, lens surfaces, and handle edges that are highly susceptible to microbial contamination yet difficult to disinfect using conventional high-level disinfection (HLD) methods. …
lens.abstract: Endocavity ultrasound transducers, particularly transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS) probes, contain intricate structures such as notches, grooves, lens surfaces, and handle edges that are highly susceptible to microbial contamination yet difficult to disinfect using conventional high-level disinfection (HLD) methods. This study evaluated the efficacy of a novel ultraviolet C light emitting diode (UVC-LED) HLD system in eliminating microbial contamination from these complex probe surfaces. Two TVUS probes were sampled from predefined high-risk regions before and after disinfection following clinical use. Probe A was sampled at the top and bottom notches and both sides of the handle, while Probe B was assessed at the lens, edges, and bent groove regions. Microbial contamination was quantified using swab sampling, culture on agar plates, and identification via Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Io

lens.title: Amplified MS2 labeling reveals heterogeneous dynamics of RNA granules in the live murine brain ex vivo.
lens.summary: Dynamics of messenger ribonucleic acids (mRNAs) and the complexes with associated proteins (RNPs), also known as RNA granules, provide post-transcriptional control of gene expression. This regulation is crucial for cell-type diversity and activity-dependent plasticity of the mammalian central nervous system (CNS). …
lens.abstract: Dynamics of messenger ribonucleic acids (mRNAs) and the complexes with associated proteins (RNPs), also known as RNA granules, provide post-transcriptional control of gene expression. This regulation is crucial for cell-type diversity and activity-dependent plasticity of the mammalian central nervous system (CNS). However, elucidating the physiological significance of RNA granules has been hampered by technical difficulties to probe them in live brain. Here, we describe a novel method to visualize RNA granules in native CNS tissues of mouse. To amplify the fluorescence signal from single mRNAs incorporating MS2 stem loops, MS2 capsid protein (MCP) was conjugated with 4 tandem superfolder green fluorescent proteins (sfGFPs). lens.title: Contrast Sensitivity Functions in ON and OFF Visual Pathways in Myopia.
lens.summary: High myopia exhibited reduced ordinary and ON pathway CS. The ON pathway-selective CS deficits were significantly correlated with myopia severity and predominantly observed at low SFs. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: The current study investigates the contrast sensitivity (CS) of ON and OFF visual pathways across a broad spatial frequency range in individuals with varying severities of myopia. METHODS: The CS function (CSF) was measured in 60 adults (emmetropes, low myopes, and high myopes) using a psychophysical paradigm that could selectively activate the ON and OFF pathways, combined with the quick CSF method. Stimuli included bipolar, increment, and decrement bandpass-filtered noise across 15 spatial frequency levels (0.25-25.85 cycles per degree). Tests were performed under binocular, dominant eye (DE), and non-DE (NDE) conditions. RESULTS: High myopes exhibited significant deficits in ordinary (bipolar) and ON pathway (increment) CS, primarily manifested as reduced peak sensitivity. lens.title: Evaluation of A Modified Persian Version of the Developmental Eye Movement Test in Children.
lens.summary: This study thus provides Persian-language normative data and supports the reliability of the DEM test for this population. This investigation successfully established Persian-language normative data for the DEM test and confirmed the instrument's reliability within an Iranian population. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To adapt and evaluate the Developmental Eye Movement (DEM) test in Persian for Iranian children aged 7-12 years, to evaluate developmental changes across ages, and to compare performance with the American normative sample to identify potential linguistic and cultural influences on oculomotor behavior. METHODS: The DEM test was developed by translating the original numbers into Persian numerals. Awe enrolled a sample of 720 Iranian children aged 7-12 years utilizing a stratified random sampling method from four educational districts in Shiraz. The assessment was administered in accordance with the standardized protocol detailed in the official manual, except that the numerals were read from right to left. lens.title: Mathematical foundations of artificial intelligence in healthcare: a systematic review.
lens.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare relies on diverse mathematical frameworks, yet their contributions to model development, evaluation, interpretability, and clinical translation remain fragmented. …
lens.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare relies on diverse mathematical frameworks, yet their contributions to model development, evaluation, interpretability, and clinical translation remain fragmented. This systematic review synthesized the classical and emerging mathematical foundations underpinning healthcare AI and examined major methodological and application trends. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, studies published between January 2016 and June 30, 2026, were identified through systematic searches of Scopus, Google Scholar, and PubMed/MEDLINE, with searches conducted using Harzing's Publish or Perish v8 where applicable. Bibliometric analysis was performed using VOSviewer, while methodological quality was assessed using an adapted JBI-based framework and AMSTAR-2 for systematic reviews. Of 653 records identified, 147 studies met the eligibility criteria. Non-mutually exclusive

Kolb-Based Experiential Learning: Impact of Real-Patient Integration on Refraction Skills and Course Experience Among Undergraduate Optometry Students.
lens.summary: In this single-centre pre-post study, real-patient integration was associated with better course experience and clinical performance, though not examination accuracy. Campus volunteers offer a feasible, low-cost training resource, pending confirmation in controlled studies.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: The Refraction Technique course is central to optometric education, yet traditional teaching methods often fail to prepare students for real-world clinical complexity. Following traditional instruction, students underwent an experiential learning intervention that integrated real patients into the Refraction Technique course. Kolb's experiential learning theory provided a framework through a cyclical process of concrete experience, reflection, conceptualization, and experimentation. PATIENTS AND METHODS: A longitudinal pre-post intervention study without a concurrent control group was conducted at a single-centre among 85 undergraduate optometry students in China. Following identical systematic theoretical training and supervised peer-simulation delivered by the same instructors, students participated in a Kolb-based experiential learning intervention. lens.title: Persistent sarcopenia after flare remission in experimental RA responds to dipyridamole and is associated with restoration of adenosine and A2BR signaling.
lens.summary: RA induces persistent sarcopenia that remains after inflammation resolution. Post-remission dipyridamole reverses this phenotype in association with restoration of adenosine signaling, increased A2BR expression, AMPK activation, and enhanced anabolic pathways, highlighting purinergic modulation as a promising therapeutic strategy to impro …
lens.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with systemic inflammation and sarcopenia, which often persist despite successful control of joint swelling and the mechanisms sustaining it remain unclear. METHODS: Using the K/BxN serum-transfer model, we evaluated muscle structure, metabolism, and function after inflammatory remission. Dipyridamole was administered after remission of joint swelling to assess whether enhancement of adenosine and adenosine receptor signaling restore muscle homeostasis. Histological, molecular, metabolic, and functional analyses were performed. RESULTS: RA mice exhibited persistent loss of muscle mass, fiber atrophy, fibrosis, white adipose tissue expansion, and impaired strength and endurance despite normalization of joint swelling. lens.title: A Sensitive Period for Automaticity Rather than Ability: Automatic Visuospatial Coding of Touch Requires Visual Experience in Early Life.
lens.summary: Early visual experience can profoundly shape tactile perception. Sighted and late blind but not congenitally blind humans automatically link touch to a visuospatial reference frame-evidenced by a tendency to assign tactile stimuli to the wrong hand when the hands are crossed. …
lens.abstract: Early visual experience can profoundly shape tactile perception. Sighted and late blind but not congenitally blind humans automatically link touch to a visuospatial reference frame-evidenced by a tendency to assign tactile stimuli to the wrong hand when the hands are crossed. Here, we tested for a sensitive period during which visual experience irrevocably shapes the automaticity of visuospatial coding of touch. To this aim, tactile spatiotemporal perception was measured in individuals who had been temporarily blind due to bilateral dense cataracts that were either congenital or developed in childhood. Participants reported the location of the first of two successive tactile stimuli-one on each hand-resting their arms in a crossed or uncrossed position. lens.title: The Amsler Grid Use Study (AGUS): Amsler Grid Nonadherence is Driven by Forgetfulness and Health Beliefs But Not Age.
lens.summary: Amsler grid nonadherence was primarily unintentional and mostly due to forgetfulness. Poor adherence was associated with greater concerns in Amsler grid use, indicating modifiable factors that can be addressed to improve adherence.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: The Amsler grid is a widely prescribed home-monitoring tool used to detect vision changes associated with ocular disease. Despite poor adherence being considered a major challenge in its administration, studies examining adherence rates are lacking, limiting the development of evidence-based solutions. Therefore, this study aimed to quantify current adherence levels of Amsler grid use and explore factors that may influence nonadherence. METHODS: A mail-out survey containing items adapted from validated questionnaires, collecting adherence, self-efficacy and beliefs towards Amsler grid use, was distributed via a modified Dillman's Total Design method to 300 individuals who attended a large referral-only eye clinic and were prescribed an Amsler grid. Responses scored adherence levels (high, moderate and low), determined reasons for nonadherence and behaviours of adherence/nonadher

lens.title: 3D-Printed Hydroxyapatite/Polycaprolactone Porous Scaffolds as Tarsus Substitutes for Eyelid Defects: A Preliminary Study in Rabbits.
lens.summary: The 3D‑printed HA/PCL scaffolds are promising for tarsal repair. The 84% HA scaffold offers superior mechanical compatibility, inflammatory regulation, angiogenesis, and tissue regeneration, providing an experimental basis for eyelid reconstruction biomaterials.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Reconstruction of eyelid tarsal defects remains challenging due to donor-site morbidity, insufficient autologous tissue sources, and biomechanical mismatch between grafts and native tarsal plate. This study aimed to fabricate polyethylene glycol 400-plasticized 3D-printed hydroxyapatite/polycaprolactone (HA/PCL) porous scaffolds, and to compare the repair efficacy of scaffolds with 70% and 84% HA mass fractions in a rabbit eyelid tarsal defect model. METHODS: Scaffolds were fabricated by pneumatic extrusion 3D printing and characterized for porosity, mechanics, hydrophilicity, and cytocompatibility with human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). A rabbit tarsal defect model was used to evaluate ocular safety, inflammation, angiogenesis, and tissue integration at 4 and 8 weeks via corneal staining, hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), qPCR, and immunohistochemistry (IHC). lens.title: Sex, Age, and Skull Morphology Effects on Eye Size and Refractive Errors in Reindeer.
lens.summary: Eye size influences captured light and visual resolution and is used as an indicator of the relative importance of vision. Although vision-related sexual dimorphism is subtle among vertebrates, Cervids exhibit pronounced sexual dimorphism in body size, antler development, and reproductive strategies. …
lens.abstract: Eye size influences captured light and visual resolution and is used as an indicator of the relative importance of vision. Although vision-related sexual dimorphism is subtle among vertebrates, Cervids exhibit pronounced sexual dimorphism in body size, antler development, and reproductive strategies. We tested the hypothesis that male reindeer (Rangifer tarandus tarandus) with larger skeletal dimensions would have larger eyes and narrower binocular overlap but similar refractive errors compared to females. We collected skull morphological, ocular biometric, and refractive error data from 69 semi-domesticated reindeer (0.5-12.5-year-old; 27 females, 42 males) living year-round under extreme high-latitude seasonal variation in photoperiod in south-central Norway. lens.title: Artificial intelligence for ophthalmic vessel segmentation: from multimodal imaging to clinical translation.
lens.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based vessel segmentation converts color fundus photographs, scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO), optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), structural OCT, and anterior-segment images into quantitative vascular biomarkers. …
lens.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based vessel segmentation converts color fundus photographs, scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO), optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), structural OCT, and anterior-segment images into quantitative vascular biomarkers. Strong performance within individual datasets has not consistently yielded reliable clinical measurements because errors can arise during acquisition, anatomical preprocessing, vessel extraction, biomarker calculation, and deployment. This structured narrative review compares segmentation tasks involving retinal vascular trees, OCTA capillary plexuses, the structural choroid and choriocapillaris, macular neovascularization, corneal neovascularization, and conjunctival microvasculature. lens.title: Foveal Crowding and Reduced Binocular Advantage In Myopic Anisometropia Under Brief Stimulus Presentation.
lens.summary: In optically corrected MA patients, brief stimulus presentation revealed abnormal foveal crowding in response time and a reduced binocular advantage, suggesting decreased efficiency in processing visual information under high perceptual demand.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To examine whether myopic anisometropia (MA) influences foveal crowding, binocular advantage, and the balance of monocular contributions to binocular vision under brief stimulus presentation. METHODS: Twenty-two participants were recruited, including 5 with high MA (HMA; mean age 23.20 ± 3.03 years), 9 with low MA (LMA; mean age 24.00 ± 2.78 years), and 8 with non-MA (NMA; mean age 26.88 ± 2.23 years). All participants completed a letter orientation discrimination task under crowded and uncrowded conditions. Sensitivity (D-prime, d'), response time (RT), binocular summation, and the monocular contributions to binocular performance were measured. RESULTS: Foveal crowding was present in all groups under brief stimulus presentation, with no interocular differences within any group. lens.title: Early detection of cataract in type 1 diabetes: A cross-sectional study using Scheimpflug imaging.
lens.journal: Biomed Pap Med Fac Univ Palacky Olomouc Czech Repub
lens.summary: Scheimpflug-based lens densitometry identified lower lens transparency in adults with T1DM than in healthy controls. The method appears useful as an objective quantitative adjunct for detecting early lenticular changes, but the findings should be interpreted with consideration of age and other potential confounding factors.
lens.abstract: AIM: To compare lens densitometry measured by Scheimpflug imaging in adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus, T1DM, and healthy controls, and to assess the associations of lens density with age, diabetes duration, and glycated haemoglobin, HbA1c. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 52 adults with T1DM and 53 healthy controls examined at St Anne's University Hospital Brno between January and December 2021. All participants underwent history taking, slit-lamp examination under pharmacological mydriasis, and Scheimpflug-based lens densitometry using Pentacam HR (Oculus, Wetzlar, Germany). Statistical analysis included the Shapiro-Wilk test, the Mann-Whitney test, simple linear regression, and an exploratory multivariable linear regression model in the diabetic cohort. lens.title: Slow change blindness from serial dependence: slowly changing objects are perceived as biased toward the past.
lens.summary: Overall, we provide evidence that serial dependence actively biases perception during gradual changes, sometimes producing slow change blindness.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Slow change blindness, when attentive observers fail to notice large changes that happen gradually, raises questions about how visual information is combined across time. One plausible integration strategy is serial dependence: blending information from the recent past into current perception. We investigate serial dependencies in perception of a cartoon object that slowly changes hue. In a one-shot experiment, observers each viewed a single trial with a random degree of hue change and provided one hue judgment response. Across participants, the entire morph was probed. RESULTS: Observers' hue reports revealed an overall bias toward the past that increased in magnitude as more of the morph was experienced. lens.title: Making better use of patients' time: feasibility of performing self-administered vision assessments in waiting rooms.
lens.summary: This proof-of-concept study demonstrates that it is feasible for patients to self-administer portable vision tests in clinic waiting rooms. Using CS as a representative example, this approach may enable additional data collection, potentially improving patient management, clinic flow, and/or patient satisfaction.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients often spend significant time in clinic waiting rooms. This study assessed the feasibility of using this "wasted" time to perform self-administered vision assessments directly within the waiting area. METHODS: Glaucoma patients attending routine appointments were asked to complete either a pen-and-paper (SpotChecks) or digital (PopCSF) contrast sensitivity (CS) test. Ambient illuminance, background noise, and crowd levels were recorded to assess potential environmental confounds. Test durations and patient feedback were recorded. Visual-Functioning Index-7 (VF-7) and Pelli-Robson CS (reference) test results were collected for comparison. RESULTS: Of 173 patients approached, 155 (89.6%) agreed to participate, and 151(97.4%) participants completed testing before their appointment (77/78 pen-and-paper; 74/74 digital). lens.title: Association of Thyroid Autoimmunity With Age-Related Macular Degeneration in U.S. Adults.
lens.summary: TgAb positivity was associated with prevalent AMD. The cross-sectional design and the nonidentical exposures assessed in the observational and MR analyses preclude causal inference.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the associations of thyroid autoimmunity, assessed by thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb) and thyroglobulin antibody (TgAb), with prevalent age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in U.S. adults, and to explore whether genetic liabilities to Hashimoto thyroiditis (HT) and Graves' disease (GD) were associated with AMD risk using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 2967 adults aged 40 years or older from the 2007-2008 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Survey-weighted logistic regression models included TPOAb and TgAb positivity simultaneously. Two-sample MR analyses were exploratory. RESULTS: Among 2967 participants, 234 had AMD, corresponding to a weighted prevalence of 6.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 5.6%-7.9%). lens.title: Adherens Junctions and Spectrin-Associated Proteins Function Interdependently to Stabilize Fiber Cell Membranes and Preserve Lens Transparency.
lens.summary: Together, this data supports a novel role for Arvcf linking adherens junctions to the spectrin-associated cytoskeleton. This association is required to stabilize fiber cell membranes, limit cell fusion events, and maintain transparency in the cortical regions of the lens.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Cortical cataracts develop in mice in the absence of Arvcf, a protein that serves as a key component of the adherens junctional complex (AJC) in lens cells. This study aimed to mechanistically probe the proteomic complex associated with Arvcf to identify novel mechanisms underlying cortical cataract formation. METHODS: Arvcf associated proteins were identified by coimmunoprecipitation of P30 mouse lens lysates using liquid chromatography mass-spectroscopy/mass-spectroscopy, gene ontology analysis, and western blot. Immunofluorescent staining was also performed in Arvcf or ankyrin-B mutant mouse lenses to assess protein expression, association, and junctional localization. RESULTS: In addition to members of the AJC, proteomic analysis revealed that Arvcf associates with several spectrin-associated proteins. Ankyrin-B, NrCAM, and β-spectrin. lens.title: Targeting lncRNA Carmn alleviates scleral remodeling in high myopia via Myrf-mediated repression of YAP activity.
lens.summary: LncRNA Carmn as a conserved regulatory factor associated with scleral remodeling in high myopia. Through combined RNA-protein interaction and ceRNA-mediated mechanisms, Carmn is linked to Myrf-YAP signaling and ECM homeostasis in scleral fibroblasts. …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pathological remodeling of the sclera, characterized by extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation and biomechanical weakening, is a central feature of axial elongation in high myopia. Scleral fibroblasts are the major cell type responsible for ECM homeostasis, and mechanotransduction pathways such as YAP signaling have been implicated in regulating fibroblast behavior and matrix turnover. However, the upstream regulators that control fibroblast function and ECM remodeling in the myopic sclera remain incompletely understood. Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as important modulators of gene regulation, but their contribution to scleral fibroblast dysfunction and ECM remodeling in high myopia is largely unexplored. lens.title: Retinal detachment and posterior vitreous detachment following refractive lens exchange in myopic patients.
lens.summary: Refractive lens exchange has become established thanks to advances in phacoemulsification, the precise calculation of intraocular lenses, and the design of simultaneous vision lenses, which allow for the joint correction of ametropia and presbyopia. …
lens.abstract: Refractive lens exchange has become established thanks to advances in phacoemulsification, the precise calculation of intraocular lenses, and the design of simultaneous vision lenses, which allow for the joint correction of ametropia and presbyopia. In myopia, however, the risk of retinal detachment following surgery remains a significant concern due to its severity. This review gathers the most recent data on the incidence of retinal detachment after refractive lens exchange using current techniques, analyzes its relationship with posterior vitreous detachment, and reviews indication criteria in light of recent literature. Additionally, the available evidence regarding the use of phakic lenses in patients with presbyopia is examined. Finally, the impact that vitreous and retinal detachment may have on the visual performance of simultaneous vision lenses is addressed. Clinical implicatio

lens.title: Short-term visual and ocular responses to a myopia control contact lens: influence of optical zones and hydration techniques.
lens.summary: The evaluated contact lenses showed good short-term performance and tolerance. A smaller central optical zone was associated with modest reductions in contrast sensitivity and perceived visual quality, without clear advantages in other outcomes. Hydration modality did not influence performance.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the short-term visual performance, subjective acceptance, tear film stability, and ocular physiological response after 1 h of wear of a monthly replacement soft contact lens for myopia control with different central optical zone diameters and hydration modalities. METHODS: Thirty myopic young adults (21 ± 1 years) were fitted monocularly with three centre-distance multifocal designs: 3.9 mm optical zone with bulk hydration, 3.9 mm with blister hydration, and 3.6 mm with bulk hydration. A no-contact lens condition served as baseline. High-contrast visual acuity (CDVA) and contrast sensitivity function (CSF) under photopic and mesopic conditions, tear film parameters (tear meniscus heigh, non-invasive tear break-up time), and Likert scales (visual quality, comfort, satisfaction) were assessed using a repeated-measures design. lens.title: Assessing Near Vision in the Rapid Assessment of Avoidable Blindness Survey Methodology: Results of Validation and Feasibility Studies in India and Togo.
lens.summary: The validity and feasibility of measuring near vision in RAAB surveys was confirmed. This new test will give eye care providers important information on the need for presbyopic correction in their population and start to build up the global evidence base for near eREC.
lens.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Half a billion people worldwide have near vision impairment from unaddressed presbyopia. To address this, the 2021 World Health Assembly endorsed a global target for increasing effective refractive error coverage (eREC) for near vision. However, there is a global population data gap on near vision. This study tested the validity and feasibility of including a Peek Vision smartphone-based near vision screening test in the Rapid Assessment of Avoidable Blindness (RAAB) survey to allow more epidemiological data to be collected on this important global health issue. METHODS: The study was done across four RAABs, two in India and two in Togo. In the first, the sensitivity and specificity of the Peek test was assessed to detect near vision impairment (cannot see N6 at 40 cm, binocularly) when compared to a printed near chart. lens.title: Evaluating the transfer effects of skill acquisition principles on performance in academy soccer players.
lens.summary: Despite growing evidence for the benefits of skill acquisition principles (SAPs), their effects in real-world settings remain understudied. This study examined the transfer effects of SAPs on soccer players' performance. …
lens.abstract: Despite growing evidence for the benefits of skill acquisition principles (SAPs), their effects in real-world settings remain understudied. This study examined the transfer effects of SAPs on soccer players' performance. Fifty male youth players (16.54 ± 1.01 years) and eight professional coaches from an elite soccer academy participated in a within-subject design including a control phase followed by an experimental phase where coaches applied seven SAPs. Performance was assessed at four time points (T0-T3) using match statistics and a video-based test of declarative knowledge. SAP implementation and training load were monitored during all training sessions, and changes over time were analyzed with generalized linear models and t-tests. lens.title: Iridocorneal Endothelial Syndrome after Implantation Collamer Lens: A Case Report.
lens.summary: Our report is the first to document the occurrence of ICE syndrome in pseudophakic eyes, with no preoperative abnormalities noted.
lens.abstract: INTRODUCTION: We describe a case of iridocorneal endothelial (ICE) syndrome 13 years after a bilateral insertion of implantable Collamer lenses in a patient to rectify severe myopia. CASE PRESENTATION: A 31-year-old woman presented to our hospital with elevated intraocular pressure detected during a routine physical examination. She had undergone bilateral implantable Collamer lens implantation 13 years ago to correct her high myopia. Slit lamp examination revealed appropriate vaulting of the lenses in both eyes. The right eye was structurally normal, but the left eye showed peripheral corneal opacity and edema, slight pigmented keratic precipitates, pupil displacement, sluggish response to light, iris atrophy, and peripheral anterior iris adhesions. lens.title: Design and experimental evaluation of a rotationally symmetric zonal aspheric lens for early presbyopia correction.
lens.summary: Progressive addition lenses (PALs) are inherently associated with peripheral astigmatism arising from their progressive optical architecture. We developed a rotationally symmetric zonal aspheric lens (ZAL) as an alternative approach for early presbyopia correction. …
lens.abstract: Progressive addition lenses (PALs) are inherently associated with peripheral astigmatism arising from their progressive optical architecture. We developed a rotationally symmetric zonal aspheric lens (ZAL) as an alternative approach for early presbyopia correction. The ZAL was designed using an eye model adapted to the participant's refractive prescription, fabricated, and experimentally characterized. Compared with a commercial PAL, the ZAL reproduced the intended power distribution and exhibited reduced peripheral astigmatism. A preliminary 14-day binocular wear evaluation was conducted in a single participant. Visual acuity and recognition accuracy were comparable between the ZALs and PALs, whereas median reaction time was longer with the ZALs (956.94 vs. 907.47 ms, p < 0.001). lens.title: Vision screening programmes for school-aged children in select high-income countries: a scoping review protocol.
lens.summary: OBJECTIVE: The proposed scoping review aims to summarise current vision screening programmes in school-aged children from selected high-income nations, incorporating both peer-reviewed and grey literature for an accurate depiction of current practices. …
lens.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The proposed scoping review aims to summarise current vision screening programmes in school-aged children from selected high-income nations, incorporating both peer-reviewed and grey literature for an accurate depiction of current practices. INTRODUCTION: Paediatric visual impairment is largely caused by uncorrected refractive error (UER). While preschool screening programmes focus on amblyopia detection, school-aged children face a higher and rising burden of refractive error in the crucial period of literacy skill development, which adversely impacts their education. A scoping review into the current state of care can be used to inform local implementation research. lens.title: Twelve-Month Efficacy and Visual Tolerability of MyoPi Spectacle Lenses in Childhood Myopia: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
lens.summary: In children with myopia, MyoPi continuous free-form defocus spectacle lenses slowed 12-month axial elongation and cycloplegic refractive progression compared with single-vision spectacles, with acceptable overall safety and visual tolerability.
lens.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the 12-month efficacy, safety, and visual tolerability of MyoPi continuous free-form defocus spectacle lenses compared with conventional single-vision spectacle lenses (SVLs) in children with myopia. DESIGN: Prospective, multicenter, randomized, single-masked, parallel-group clinical trial. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 116 eligible children were randomized 1:1 to MyoPi or SVLs. Eligible participants were 8 to 13 years of age with bilateral cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction (SER) from -0.75 to -5.00 diopters (D). METHODS: Participants were randomized 1:1 to MyoPi or single-vision spectacle lenses and were followed at baseline, week 1, month 3, month 6, and month 12. lens.title: Corneal diameter distribution and its determinant factors in elderly population: Tehran Geriatric Eye Study.
lens.summary: The corneal diameter range measured by Pentacam AXL in the elderly population is greater than certain prior studies and lesser than others. The findings serve as a reference for clinicians assessing corneal diameter in the elderly for clinical application.
lens.abstract: AIM: To determine the distribution and normative range of corneal diameter in individuals aged over 60, and its association with demographic variables, certain comorbidities, anthropometric measurements, additional ocular biometric indices, and refractive errors. METHODS: This population-based cross-sectional study involved participants aged over 60 residing in Tehran, selected by a multi-stage cluster random sampling. Following the acquisition of informed consent, comprehensive ophthalmological and optometric evaluations, including slit lamp examination, visual acuity assessment, and refraction, were conducted. Ocular biometric parameters, including corneal diameter, were assessed using the Pentacam AXL. lens.title: Artificial intelligence innovations in low vision rehabilitation: a systematic review of emerging technologies.
lens.summary: AI assistive technologies for low vision demonstrate technical feasibility with promising performance. However, important evidence gaps limit clinical application: the absence of prospective validation, limited comparative effectiveness data, and minimal patient-centered outcomes. …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low vision is one of the major types of visual impairment worldwide and when diagnosed early can help with its management. Artificial intelligence (AI) has recently shown promising outcomes in all fields including health, with low vision rehabilitation being one of its significant applications. This systematic review aims to provide an up-to-date and comprehensive evaluation of the application of AI in the management of low vision. METHODS: The systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. All relevant published papers were retrieved through searches from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore, without date restrictions. lens.title: Clinical outcomes of scleral lenses in keratoconus: a systematic review and Meta-analysis.
lens.summary: SLs fitting leads to improved visual outcomes and patient satisfaction in patients with keratoconus.
lens.abstract: AIM: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of scleral lenses (SLs) in patients with keratoconus. METHODS: Electronic databases including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane Library were systematically searched to find the articles on visual function and patient satisfaction following SLs fitting. A random-effects model was applied to specify the pooled values. RESULTS: Of 833 studies, 19 articles (704 eyes) and 14 studies (475 eyes) were included in qualitative and quantitative synthesis, respectively. Pooled mean difference (PMD) of best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was -0.37 [95% confidence interval (CI), -0.48 to -0.26] logMAR in favor of SLs treatment. SLs markedly reduced ocular and corneal higher-order aberrations and increased the quality of vision. lens.title: Selective compartmental plication in small-angle convergence insufficiency exotropia: surgical outcomes and predictive model.
lens.summary: Unilateral LRc combined with CIMRP is an effective and safe approach for small angle CI-IXT (< 25 PD). Based on preliminary evidence from this exploratory analysis, we tentatively suggest CIMRP of ≥ 3.5 mm for preoperative NDD > 10 PD, pending prospective validation. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate a novel surgical approach combining unilateral lateral rectus recession (LRc) with compartmentalized inferior medial rectus plication (CIMRP) for treating small-angle (< 25 prism diopters, PD) convergence insufficiency intermittent exotropia (CI-IXT) in pediatric patients. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 69 pediatric CI-IXT patients (mean age: 8.13 ± 2.46 years; range: 4-14 years) who underwent unilateral LRc and CIMRP between September 2022 and January 2024 at Tianjin Eye Hospital. All patients completed a minimum 12-month follow-up (mean: 12.41 ± 1.42 months; range: 12-18 months). Outcomes including near and distance deviations, near-distance difference (NDD), control scores, stereopsis, and complications were assessed preoperatively and postoperatively at 1 day, 2 months, 6 months, and final follow-up (12-18 months). lens.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of refractive errors in Ghana with emphasis on myopia.
lens.summary: Prevalence of refractive errors, including myopia, in Ghana remain key public health concern, and vary substantially according to the refraction method employed, the age group studied, and the study setting. …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Refractive errors remain the leading cause of visual impairment globally, with myopia representing the most prevalent. In Ghana, reported prevalence estimates for refractive errors and myopia show considerable variability across studies, which complicates accurate quantification of their public burden and poses challenges for evidence-informed policy formulation and planning. The study aimed to estimate the prevalence of refractive errors in Ghana, with particular emphasis on myopia. METHOD: The systematic review followed the 2020 Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) guidelines and was prospectively registered with the Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; registration number CRD42022377958). A comprehensive and independent search of the literature was undertaken to identify peer-reviewed cross-sectional studies, using pr

lens.title: Constructing an Objective Defocus Curve from Pyramidal Wavefront Aberrometry: Mapping Objective-to-Subjective Through-Focus Response.
lens.summary: An objective defocus curve from one pyramidal wavefront acquisition estimated the subjective through-focus response with small bias and limits of agreement of about ±0.2 logMAR in a test set and an independent cohort of refractive IOLs; individual precision, diffractive designs, and pupil-specific curves need further work.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To construct an objective defocus curve from pyramidal wavefront aberrometry and map it onto the subjective through-focus response. DESIGN: Prospective multicenter case series with external validation. SUBJECTS, PARTICIPANTS, AND/OR CONTROLS: 98 eyes of 63 patients implanted with the RayOne Galaxy spiral refractive intraocular lens (IOL) at three centers (Italy, UK); 81 eyes with a wavefront pupil ≥ 4 mm were split by patient into training (56) and test (25) sets; 19 eyes with other refractive extended-depth-of-focus IOLs from a fourth center formed an external cohort. METHODS, INTERVENTION, OR TESTING: Pyramidal aberrometry (Osiris) with numerically introduced defocus from +1.00 to -4.00 diopters (D); the second-moment radius of the geometrical point spread function was mapped to acuity by a rational function and compared with monocular ETDRS defocus curves. lens.title: Improvement in acuity following motion adaptation: The role of information at different spatial frequencies.
lens.summary: Prolonged exposure (adaptation) to blur, flicker or motion can transiently enhance visual acuity (VA). Such improvement could be linked to decreased contrast sensitivity (CS) for low spatial frequency (SF) image structure. Here, we determine if and why low SFs are required for such acuity improvement following adaptation. …
lens.abstract: Prolonged exposure (adaptation) to blur, flicker or motion can transiently enhance visual acuity (VA). Such improvement could be linked to decreased contrast sensitivity (CS) for low spatial frequency (SF) image structure. Here, we determine if and why low SFs are required for such acuity improvement following adaptation. We measured CS using SF band-pass filtered optotypes with and without adaptation. We also measured CS for these stimuli in the presence of a SF low-pass fixed-contrast "pedestal". Adaptation to receding motion improves VA for conventional but not vanishing optotypes (which contain little low SF structure), indicating a crucial role for low SFs. lens.title: When to use the Bonferroni correction.
lens.summary: PURPOSE: The Bonferroni correction adjusts probability (p) values because of the increased risk of a type I error when making multiple statistical tests. The routine use of this test has been criticised as deleterious to sound statistical judgment, testing the wrong hypothesis, and reducing the chance of a type I error but at the expense  …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: The Bonferroni correction adjusts probability (p) values because of the increased risk of a type I error when making multiple statistical tests. The routine use of this test has been criticised as deleterious to sound statistical judgment, testing the wrong hypothesis, and reducing the chance of a type I error but at the expense of a type II error; yet it remains popular in ophthalmic research. The purpose of this article was to survey the use of the Bonferroni correction in research articles published in three optometric journals, viz. Ophthalmic & Physiological Optics, Optometry & Vision Science, and Clinical & Experimental Optometry, and to provide advice to authors contemplating multiple testing. RECENT FINDINGS: Some authors ignored the problem of multiple testing while others used the method uncritically with no rationale or discussion. A variety of methods of correcting p

lens.title: Presbyopia: Effectiveness of correction strategies.
lens.summary: Presbyopia is a global problem affecting over a billion people worldwide. The prevalence of unmanaged presbyopia is as high as 50% of those over 50 years of age in developing world populations, due to a lack of awareness and accessibility to affordable treatment, and is even as high as 34% in developed countries. …
lens.abstract: Presbyopia is a global problem affecting over a billion people worldwide. The prevalence of unmanaged presbyopia is as high as 50% of those over 50 years of age in developing world populations, due to a lack of awareness and accessibility to affordable treatment, and is even as high as 34% in developed countries. Definitions of presbyopia are inconsistent and varied, so we propose a redefinition that states "presbyopia occurs when the physiologically normal age-related reduction in the eye's focusing range reaches a point, when optimally corrected for distance vision, that the clarity of vision at near is insufficient to satisfy an individual's requirements". lens.title: Global Prevalence of Presbyopia and Vision Impairment from Uncorrected Presbyopia: Systematic Review, Meta-analysis, and Modelling.
lens.summary: There is a significant burden of VI from uncorrected presbyopia, with the greatest burden in rural areas of low-resource countries.
lens.abstract: TOPIC: Presbyopia prevalence and spectacle-correction coverage were estimated by systematic review and meta-analysis of epidemiologic evidence, then modeled to expand to country, region, and global estimates. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Understanding presbyopia epidemiologic factors and correction coverage is critical to overcoming the burden of vision impairment (VI) from uncorrected presbyopia. METHODS: We performed systematic reviews of presbyopia prevalence and spectacle-correction coverage. Accepted presbyopia prevalence data were gathered into 5-year age groups from 0 to 90 years or older and meta-analyzed within World Health Organization global burden of disease regions. We developed a model based on amplitude of accommodation adjusted for myopia rates to match the regionally meta-analyzed presbyopia prevalence. lens.title: Wavefront refraction and correction.
Corrective response times in a coordinated eye-head-arm countermanding task.
lens.summary: Inhibition of motor responses has been described as a race between two competing decision processes of motor initiation and inhibition, which manifest as the reaction time (RT) and the stop signal reaction time (SSRT); in the case where motor initiation wins out over inhibition, an erroneous movement occurs that usually needs to be correc …
lens.abstract: Inhibition of motor responses has been described as a race between two competing decision processes of motor initiation and inhibition, which manifest as the reaction time (RT) and the stop signal reaction time (SSRT); in the case where motor initiation wins out over inhibition, an erroneous movement occurs that usually needs to be corrected, leading to corrective response times (CRTs). Here we used a combined eye-head-arm movement countermanding task to investigate the mechanisms governing multiple effector coordination and the timing of corrective responses. We found a high degree of correlation between effector response times for RT, SSRT, and CRT, suggesting that decision processes are strongly dependent across effectors. lens.title: Lens-based surgical correction of presbyopia. Where are we in 2020?
lens.summary: It is necessary to know the variety of lenses available, and to have an in-depth understanding of their optical properties, as well as the impact that these will have later on their clinical performance and on the visual quality of the patients. This should help us to select the best alternative for each of them.
lens.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Presbyopia is the progressive and irreversible loss of accommodation due to aging. It is one of the main causes of loss of quality of life in people from 45 years of age, due to the, often novel, dependence on spectacles. The eagerness to correct it by ophthalmologists impulsed by the desire of millions of people who suffer from it, has become one of the main drivers for the development of intraocular lens (IOL) technology over the last twenty years. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This review briefly presents the different alternatives that have allowed us to improve the crystalline lens surgical approach of presbyopia; from monofocal lenses and monovision technique, accommodative, refractive, and diffractive multifocal lenses, and finally the most recent extended depth of focus/field lenses known as EDOFs. lens.title: How to Fix a Leaky Pipe.
Outcomes of presbyopia-correcting intraocular lenses after laser in situ keratomileusis.
lens.summary: In conclusion, in post-myopic LASIK eyes, AT LISA tri839MP provides a good visual outcome at both near and distance, but is more predictable at near than at distance. There is a myopic shift in the postoperative SE. Visual quality is satisfactory and has not been exacerbated. …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) is the most common refractive surgery in young patients, which aims at providing a clear distance vision without the use of spectacles. With time, these patients develop symptomatic cataract, which affects activities of daily living, and to improve visual acuity, intraocular lens (IOL) implantation can be considered. In post-myopic LASIK patients, to allow continuation of spectacle independence, the implantation of presbyopia-correcting IOLs is a suitable option. The purpose of this retrospective case series is to report the visual outcome and quality in post-myopic LASIK eyes after the implantation of AT LISA tri839MP IOL. METHOD: Twenty eyes of 13 patients with history of myopic LASIK within 20 years underwent phacoemulsification by one single surgeon. All eyes were implanted with AT LISA tri839PMP IOL, and their outcomes were evaluated

lens.title: Visual and Physiological Optics: where will the journey lead us in 10 years?
The measurement of visual acuity in children: an evidence-based update.
lens.summary: Over the past decade, a number of large clinical trials have provided important information relating to the reliability and repeatability of commonly used paediatric tests of vision and their role in the diagnosis and management of paediatric ocular diseases. …
lens.abstract: Over the past decade, a number of large clinical trials have provided important information relating to the reliability and repeatability of commonly used paediatric tests of vision and their role in the diagnosis and management of paediatric ocular diseases. The aim of this review is to summarise recent findings on the use of paediatric visual acuity tests in clinical practice and to discuss the validity and accuracy of visual acuity measurements in infants and young children. We provide a broad overview of the benefits and challenges of measuring visual acuity in children and then discuss age-appropriate tests for measuring visual acuity in infants through to school-age children. We also discuss normative values for visual acuity in each age group and, where possible, provide comparisons of results between tests with a particular focus on the importance of optotype design.

lens.title: Regional differences in vision health: findings from Mwanza, Tanzania.
lens.summary: Due to regional differences in visual functioning in Mwanza, a national effort for vision health cannot be entirely successful without addressing the individualized needs of local communities. Reducing the cost of vision care appointments may expand vision health care utilization in Mwanza.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Visual impairment in developing countries has both social and economic impact on individuals and communities. Understanding the subjective visual functioning of populations will allow for local policymakers to identify the need for optometric or ophthalmic services in their communities. METHODS: The authors surveyed 644 adult patients in Mwanza, Tanzania at three clinics (Buzuruga, Mwananchi and Kisesa) using a modified Visual Functioning Questionnaire 25. Responses were categorized into General health, General vision, Ocular pain, Near activities, Distance activities, Social function, Mental health, Role difficulties, Color vision, Peripheral vision and Dependency. RESULTS: Patients at Buzuruga reported the lowest scores on most subscales. Of 100 employed patients, 37% claimed to have at least some difficulty in performing job duties due to their eyesight. lens.title: Optometry Research Agenda for the Next Decade: 20/20 by 2030.
Quality indicators in a community optometrist led cataract shared care scheme.
lens.summary: Direct cataract referrals from accredited community optometrists led to a majority of patients receiving a definitive clinical decision during first consultation. Postoperative community follow up reduced hospital visits and allowed for convenient consultation closer to home following uncomplicated cataract surgery. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Cataract shared care schemes involving community optometrists show wide variation in practice. We report on defined key performance indicators (KPIs) which improve accountability between stakeholders. METHODS: In this prospective study over nine months at a UK public hospital, we evaluated the outcomes of consecutive direct cataract referrals from community optometrists against two KPIs agreed under a service-level agreement between the Hospital Eye Service and community optometrists: (1) 85% of patients listed for cataract listing at first consultation; and (2) 90% postoperative feedback return rate on patients discharged to community optometrists. A detailed analysis on referral triage, surgical listing and postoperative form return rate is reported in this study. lens.title: Bifocal and Multifocal Contact Lenses for Presbyopia and Myopia Control.
lens.summary: Bifocal and multifocal optical devices are intended to get images into focus from objects placed at different distances from the observer. Spectacles, contact lenses, and intraocular lenses can meet the requirements to provide such a solution. …
lens.abstract: Bifocal and multifocal optical devices are intended to get images into focus from objects placed at different distances from the observer. Spectacles, contact lenses, and intraocular lenses can meet the requirements to provide such a solution. Contact lenses provide unique characteristics as a platform for implementing bifocality and multifocality. Compared to spectacles, they are closer to the eye, providing a wider field of view, less distortion, and their use is more consistent as they are not so easily removed along the day. In addition, contact lenses are also minimally invasive, can be easily exchangeable, and, therefore, suitable for conditions in which surgical procedures are not indicated. lens.title: Correction of presbyopia: old problems with old (and new) solutions.
lens.summary: We live in a three-dimensional world and the human eye can focus images from a wide range of distances by adjusting the power of the eye's lens (accommodation). Progressive senescent changes in the lens ultimately lead to a complete loss of this ability by about age 50, which then requires alternative strategies to generate high-quality r …
lens.abstract: We live in a three-dimensional world and the human eye can focus images from a wide range of distances by adjusting the power of the eye's lens (accommodation). Progressive senescent changes in the lens ultimately lead to a complete loss of this ability by about age 50, which then requires alternative strategies to generate high-quality retinal images for far and close viewing distances. This review paper highlights the biomimetic properties and underlying optical mechanisms of induced anisometropia, small apertures, dynamic lenses, and multi-optic lenses in ameliorating the visual consequences of presbyopia. Specifically, the advantages and consequences of non-liner neural summation leveraged in monovision treatments are reviewed. lens.title: "I can see fine": patient knowledge of eye care.
lens.summary: This study found notable gaps in knowledge of eye care and sight risks. If these gaps result in fewer eye examinations, they potentially contribute to increased risk of vision loss due to later stage detection. The results provide motivation for further study and development of effective public health education strategies.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To learn more about the perceptions and attitudes toward eye care of members of the public - in particular, their knowledge of the purpose, components and providers of eye examinations, their ability to self-monitor ocular status and their awareness of major sight threatening eye conditions. METHODS: This study used the qualitative research strategy, grounded theory. Participants were recruited via poster and social media. Two researchers, one with optometric knowledge and one without, moderated seven 60- to 90-min, semi-structured focus group discussions, which were audiotaped and transcribed. Participants also completed a short demographic questionnaire. Three researchers employed constant comparative coding strategies to identify common themes within the focus group transcripts. lens.title: Marketing and anecdotal evidence should not guide the delivery of optometric interventions.
The challenges of providing eye care for adults with intellectual disabilities.
lens.summary: This review is intended to raise awareness of the importance of providing high-quality eye care for people with intellectual disabilities and the increasing need for this eye care to be community-based. …
lens.abstract: This review is intended to raise awareness of the importance of providing high-quality eye care for people with intellectual disabilities and the increasing need for this eye care to be community-based. We describe the challenges to the provision of high-quality community-based eye care for people with intellectual disabilities and ideas, evidence and methods for overcoming them. The prevalence of visual impairment in people with intellectual disabilities has been reported to be at least 40 per cent, rising to as high as 100 per cent in those with profound and severe disabilities. A progressive move toward deinstitutionalisation has shifted the provision of care for people with intellectual disabilities. Individuals can have the freedom to access health-care services of their choice. This has posed challenges to the health-care system, including how to deliver high-quality community-base

lens.title: Macroeconomic landscape of refractive surgery in the United States.
lens.summary: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review examines the economic history of refractive surgery and the decline of laser-assisted in-situ keratomileusis (LASIK) in the USA, and the emergence of refractive cataract surgery as an area of growth. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review examines the economic history of refractive surgery and the decline of laser-assisted in-situ keratomileusis (LASIK) in the USA, and the emergence of refractive cataract surgery as an area of growth. RECENT FINDINGS: Since it peaked in 2007 at 1.4 million procedures per year, LASIK has declined 50% in the USA, whereas refractive cataract surgery, including presbyopia-correcting intraocular lenses (IOLs), astigmatism-correcting IOLs, and femtosecond laser-assisted cataract surgery, has grown to 350 000 procedures per year, beginning in 2003. SUMMARY: Patients are price-sensitive and responsive to publicity (good or bad) about refractive surgery and refractive cataract surgery. lens.title: Impact of monovision on dynamic accommodation of early presbyopes.
lens.summary: As the stimulus was abruptly changed from the retinal conjugate plane of the distance corrected eye to that of the near corrected eye, most early presbyopes fit with monovision accommodated, which resulted in a decline, not an increase in image quality in the near corrected eye. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To examine the impact of monovision on dynamic changes in accommodation, pupil responses, spherical aberration and resultant image quality in early presbyopes. METHODS: Refractive state, pupil size and spherical aberration levels were monitored in nine early presbyopes who exhibited some accommodation (40-50 years, mean = 42 ± 2.37 years) using a Shack-Hartmann aberrometer as a binocularly viewed stimulus stepped closer (from 2 m to 40 cm), or farther (from 40 cm to 2 m). Comparison data from two fully presbyopic (i.e. non-accommodating) subjects (ages 46 and 61 years) and two young adults (ages 26 and 29 years) were also collected. Each subject was fit with four different refractive strategies: (1) both eyes corrected for 2 m, (2) both eyes corrected for 40 cm, (3) monovision with the measured right eye corrected for 2 m and, (4) monovision with the right eye corrected for 40 c

lens.title: A novel rat head gaze determination system based on optomotor responses.
lens.summary: The optomotor response of animals is commonly used to measure their visual performance, e.g., rats of different genetically altered strains or various drug tests. With the presentation of stimuli using computer screens or projectors, the common idea focuses on measuring the eye movement or head and/or body movement to characterize changes …
lens.abstract: The optomotor response of animals is commonly used to measure their visual performance, e.g., rats of different genetically altered strains or various drug tests. With the presentation of stimuli using computer screens or projectors, the common idea focuses on measuring the eye movement or head and/or body movement to characterize changes of the head gaze. However, traditional methods rely on either the invasive fixation of animals, or the judgment of a human observer who reports the stimulus-tracking movements. In this paper, we propose a novel head gaze determination system to automatically track the head movement of rats without artificial markers. The experiments were done to demonstrate the process of optimizing parameters in image processing. lens.title: Modern spectacle lens design.
lens.summary: Ophthalmic lens design concerns the control of spectacle lens aberrations which occur when the eye rotates away from the optical centre of the lens. The most significant aberrations are oblique astigmatism and mean oblique error (power error). …
lens.abstract: Ophthalmic lens design concerns the control of spectacle lens aberrations which occur when the eye rotates away from the optical centre of the lens. The most significant aberrations are oblique astigmatism and mean oblique error (power error). A brief review of these aberrations is given, explaining how the lens designer can control them using just the bending of the lens, and what results can be achieved using simple spherical and toroidal surfaces. Before 1985, aspherical surfaces were used only for post-cataract spectacle lenses and high-power magnifiers. Today, aspherical surfaces are used by all major lens manufacturers to produce thinner, lighter and more attractive best-form lenses in the normal power range. lens.title: Visual system disorders and musculoskeletal neck complaints: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
lens.summary: Accommodation disorders and nonstrabismic binocular dysfunctions affect patients' binocular system and visual performance. These visual disorders could be associated with musculoskeletal discomfort in the neck and shoulder area. …
lens.abstract: Accommodation disorders and nonstrabismic binocular dysfunctions affect patients' binocular system and visual performance. These visual disorders could be associated with musculoskeletal discomfort in the neck and shoulder area. The purpose of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to ascertain the relationship between visual system disorders and the musculoskeletal system of the neck. The review protocol is available in PROSPERO (CRD42018112771). All articles selected examined the relationship between neck conditions (chronic neck pain and whiplash) and the visual system in adult populations. Studies with optometric or physiotherapeutic measurements were included. Bias risk was evaluated with the modified Cochrane Collaboration Tool and Study Quality Assessment Tool. lens.title: Impact of supervised student optometry consultations on the patient experience.
lens.summary: The findings of this study suggest that most patients view supervised student involvement in their optometric care as an important and highly positive experience. However, efforts should be made to avoid excessively long consultations and prolonged testing. …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Understanding patient perceptions of having students involved in their clinical care is important as we strive to develop optimal models of care that integrate teaching with the best possible experience for the patient. The aim was to ascertain the impact of supervised optometry student consultations on the patient experience. METHODS: A survey comprising 45 questions was mailed to consecutive adult patients who had undergone a comprehensive eye examination at the Australian College of Optometry over a four-week period. RESULTS: Responses were received from 193 patients who had a student involved in their care (44 per cent response rate; 156 completed correctly) and 177 who did not have a student involved (32 per cent response rate; 105 completed correctly). lens.title: Stereoscopic Viewing Can Induce Changes in the CA/C Ratio.
lens.summary: These findings demonstrated that the CA/C ratio can exhibit adaptive adjustments. The observed nature and amount of the oculomotor modification failed to compensate for the stereoscopic constraint.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Stereoscopic displays challenge the neural cross-coupling between accommodation and vergence by inducing a constant accommodative demand and a varying vergence demand. Stereoscopic viewing calls for a decrease in the gain of vergence accommodation, which is the accommodation caused by vergence, quantified by using the convergence-accommodation to convergence (CA/C) ratio. However, its adaptability is still a subject of debate. METHODS: Cross-coupling (CA/C and AC/A ratios) and tonic components of vergence and accommodation were assessed in 12 participants (27.5 ± 5 years, stereoacuity better than 60 arc seconds, 6/6 acuity with corrected refractive error) before and after a 20-minute exposure to stereoscopic viewing. lens.title: Measuring visual acuity is not as simple as it seems.
Vision screening for children 36 to <72 months: recommended practices.
lens.summary: The National Expert Panel recommends that children aged 36 to younger than 72 months be screened annually (best practice) or at least once (accepted minimum standard) using one of the best practice approaches. Technological updates will be maintained at http://nationalcenter.preventblindness.org.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: This article provides recommendations for screening children aged 36 to younger than 72 months for eye and visual system disorders. The recommendations were developed by the National Expert Panel to the National Center for Children's Vision and Eye Health, sponsored by Prevent Blindness, and funded by the Maternal and Child Health Bureau of the Health Resources and Services Administration, United States Department of Health and Human Services. The recommendations describe both best and acceptable practice standards. Targeted vision disorders for screening are primarily amblyopia, strabismus, significant refractive error, and associated risk factors. The recommended screening tests are intended for use by lay screeners, nurses, and other personnel who screen children in educational, community, public health, or primary health care settings. lens.title: A Review of Pharmacological Presbyopia Treatment.
lens.summary: Presbyopia reduces an individual's ability to perform visual tasks at near distances. It is a global problem, affecting over a billion people worldwide. Contact lenses, glasses, refractive surgery, and intraocular lens surgery are the main modalities in presbyopia treatment, although they all have some disadvantages. …
lens.abstract: Presbyopia reduces an individual's ability to perform visual tasks at near distances. It is a global problem, affecting over a billion people worldwide. Contact lenses, glasses, refractive surgery, and intraocular lens surgery are the main modalities in presbyopia treatment, although they all have some disadvantages. Thus, there is an increasing need for effective, easy-to-use, and noninvasive approaches for treating presbyopia while not limiting patients' daily activities. Pharmacological presbyopia treatment as an alternative method has been under investigation in recent years. We reviewed all relevant articles using the keywords "presbyopia," "presbyopia treatment," "pharmacological presbyopia treatment," and "presbyopic corrections" from 2010 to February 9, 2020, and summarized the main results of clinical trials, investigating the drops used for presbyopia treatment.

lens.title: Paediatric vision screening by non-healthcare volunteers: evidence based practices.
lens.summary: Non-healthcare professionals can be trained to an acceptable degree of accuracy to perform vision screening tests on children, which may assist in mitigating existing gaps in paediatric eye care.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: The purpose of this study was to test the sensitivity and specificity of eight undergraduate volunteer examiners conducting vision screening tests in a community setting, in order to determine if non-eye care professionals were able to be trained to an appropriate level of skill. METHODS: Eight undergraduate volunteer examiners were trained to conduct vision screening tests to address a gap in pediatric community eye care. Phase I of the study was implemented in the pediatric ophthalmology clinic, and phase II was conducted in nine local schools. lens.title: Monovision and the Misperception of Motion.
lens.summary: Monovision is a common prescription lens correction for presbyopia [1]. Each eye is corrected for a different distance, causing one image to be blurrier than the other. Millions of people have monovision corrections, but little is known about how interocular blur differences affect motion perception. …
lens.abstract: Monovision is a common prescription lens correction for presbyopia [1]. Each eye is corrected for a different distance, causing one image to be blurrier than the other. Millions of people have monovision corrections, but little is known about how interocular blur differences affect motion perception. Here, we report that blur differences cause a previously unknown motion illusion that makes people dramatically misperceive the distance and three-dimensional direction of moving objects. The effect occurs because the blurry and sharp images are processed at different speeds. For moving objects, the mismatch in processing speed causes a neural disparity, which results in the misperceptions. lens.abstract: Optometry is an independent profession which is specialised for providing comprehensive eye care including refraction and dispensing services, diagnosis and management of eye diseases and visual rehabilitation. In clinical settings of Nepal, optometrists are primarily recognised as refractionists and are provided with working opportunities in the same area. This report highlights other optometric services such as binocular vision, multifocal lenses, contact lenses and occupational lens design which can be provided by optometrists besides performing refraction and prescribing spectacles. Considering large proportion of optometrists with further education and being working outside the country, new specialised services can be introduced through training and workshop to the fellow optometrists so that specialised services can reach up to the public level. lens.abstract: Visual factors in specific learning difficulties (SpLD) are reviewed. People with SpLD fail to achieve at a level that is commensurate with their intelligence. The commonest SpLD is dyslexia, which usually results from phonological processing/decoding deficits. Additionally, there are several optometric correlates of SpLD which may, in some cases, contribute to the learning difficulty. These correlates include binocular instability and a low amplitude of accommodation. Some people with reading difficulties and perceptual distortions/eyestrain can be helped by individually prescribed coloured filters. A visual processing anomaly is also often present in the form of a deficit of the transient visual system. The role of the optometrist is discussed.
