lens.abstract: Hyperopia is the most common refractive error of children. Children with mild (or even moderate) levels of hyperopia usually do not experience visual problems resulting from this hyperopia. However, children with moderate-to-high degrees of hyperopia are at significantly increased risk for the development of amblyopia and strabismus. It is this association with these visually threatening disorders that makes hyperopia in children an important public health problem. lens.abstract: The field of aberrations of the human eye is moving rapidly, being driven by the desire to monitor and optimise vision following refractive surgery. It is important for ophthalmologists and optometrists to have an understanding of the magnitude of various aberrations and how these are likely to be affected by refractive surgery and other corrections. In this paper, I consider methods used to measure aberrations, the magnitude of aberrations in general populations and how these are affected by various factors (for example, age, refractive error, accommodation and refractive surgery) and how aberrations and their correction affect spatial visual performance.

However, with 133 million people blind or vision impaired due to the lack of an eye examination and provision of an appropriate pair of spectacles, it is imperative to establish a cadre of eye care professionals to work in conjunction with ophthalmologists to deliver comprehensive eye care. The integration of highly educated four year trained optometrists into primary health services is a practical means of correcting refractive error and detecting ocular disease, enabling co-managed care between ophthalmologists and optometrists. lens.summary: The results suggest that the instrument is capable of detecting large amounts of defocus but needs individual calibration for detailed studies of accommodative accuracy and absolute levels of defocus, as has been recommended previously for adult subjects.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Eccentric photorefraction provides an opportunity to gather rapid and remote estimates of refraction and gaze position from infants. The technique has the potential for extensive use in vision screenings and studies of visual development. The goal of this study was to assess the refraction calibration of the PowerRefractor (Multichannel Systems) for use with uncyclopleged infants. METHODS: The defocus measurements from the instrument were compared with the results of simultaneous retinoscopy in one analysis and with known amounts of defocus induced with trial lenses in another. Data were collected from infants 1 to 6 months of age and adults. RESULTS: The PowerRefractor typically read < 1 D of myopia when the retinoscopy reflex was judged to be neutral at the same working distance in both infants and adults. lens.abstract: Background The Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2017 (GBD 2017) includes a comprehensive assessment of incidence, prevalence, and years lived with disability (YLDs) for 354 causes in 195 countries and territories from 1990 to 2017. Previous GBD studies have shown how the decline of mortality rates from 1990 to 2016 has led to an increase in life expectancy, an ageing global population, and an expansion of the non-fatal burden of disease and injury. These studies have also shown how a substantial portion of the world's population experiences non-fatal health loss with considerable heterogeneity among different causes, locations, ages, and sexes. Ongoing objectives of the GBD study include increasing the level of estimation detail, improving analytical strategies, and increasing the amount of high-quality data. lens.abstract: Background As mortality rates decline, life expectancy increases, and populations age, non-fatal outcomes of diseases and injuries are becoming a larger component of the global burden of disease. The Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2016 (GBD 2016) provides a comprehensive assessment of prevalence, incidence, and years lived with disability (YLDs) for 328 causes in 195 countries and territories from 1990 to 2016. Methods We estimated prevalence and incidence for 328 diseases and injuries and 2982 sequelae, their non-fatal consequences. We used DisMod-MR 2.1, a Bayesian meta-regression tool, as the main method of estimation, ensuring consistency between incidence, prevalence, remission, and cause of death rates for each condition. lens.abstract: Background Non-fatal outcomes of disease and injury increasingly detract from the ability of the world's population to live in full health, a trend largely attributable to an epidemiological transition in many countries from causes affecting children, to non-communicable diseases (NCDs) more common in adults. For the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2015 (GBD 2015), we estimated the incidence, prevalence, and years lived with disability for diseases and injuries at the global, regional, and national scale over the period of 1990 to 2015. Methods We estimated incidence and prevalence by age, sex, cause, year, and geography with a wide range of updated and standardised analytical procedures. lens.abstract: Background Improving survival and extending the longevity of life for all populations requires timely, robust evidence on local mortality levels and trends. The Global Burden of Disease 2015 Study (GBD 2015) provides a comprehensive assessment of all-cause and cause-specific mortality for 249 causes in 195 countries and territories from 1980 to 2015. These results informed an in-depth investigation of observed and expected mortality patterns based on sociodemographic measures. Methods We estimated all-cause mortality by age, sex, geography, and year using an improved analytical approach originally developed for GBD 2013 and GBD 2010. Improvements included refinements to the estimation of child and adult mortality and corresponding uncertainty, parameter selection for under-5 mortality synthesis by spatiotemporal Gaussian process regression, and sibling history data processing. lens.abstract: Background Up-to-date evidence about levels and trends in disease and injury incidence, prevalence, and years lived with disability (YLDs) is an essential input into global, regional, and national health policies. In the Global Burden of Disease Study 2013 (GBD 2013), we estimated these quantities for acute and chronic diseases and injuries for 188 countries between 1990 and 2013. Methods Estimates were calculated for disease and injury incidence, prevalence, and YLDs using GBD 2010 methods with some important refinements. Results for incidence of acute disorders and prevalence of chronic disorders are new additions to the analysis. Key improvements include expansion to the cause and sequelae list, updated systematic reviews, use of detailed injury codes, improvements to the Bayesian meta-regression method (DisMod-MR), and use of severity splits for various causes. lens.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs), through their complex cargo, can reflect the state of their cell of origin and change the functions and phenotypes of other cells. These features indicate strong biomarker and therapeutic potential and have generated broad interest, as evidenced by the steady year-on-year increase in the numbers of scientific publications about EVs. Important advances have been made in EV metrology and in understanding and applying EV biology. However, hurdles remain to realising the potential of EVs in domains ranging from basic biology to clinical applications due to challenges in EV nomenclature, separation from non-vesicular extracellular particles, characterisation and functional studies. lens.title: Global Prevalence of Myopia and High Myopia and Temporal Trends from 2000 through 2050
lens.summary: Purpose Myopia is a common cause of vision loss, with uncorrected myopia the leading cause of distance vision impairment globally. Individual studies show variations in the prevalence of myopia and high myopia between regions and ethnic groups, and there continues to be uncertainty regarding increasing prevalence of myopia. …
lens.abstract: Purpose Myopia is a common cause of vision loss, with uncorrected myopia the leading cause of distance vision impairment globally. Individual studies show variations in the prevalence of myopia and high myopia between regions and ethnic groups, and there continues to be uncertainty regarding increasing prevalence of myopia. Design Systematic review and meta-analysis. Methods We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of the prevalence of myopia and high myopia and estimated temporal trends from 2000 to 2050 using data published since 1995. The primary data were gathered into 5-year age groups from 0 to ≥100, in urban or rural populations in each country, standardized to definitions of myopia of -0.50 diopter (D) or less and of high myopia of -5.00 D or less, projected to the year 2010, then meta-analyzed within Global Burden of Disease (GBD) regions. lens.abstract: Background The Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2015 provides an up-to-date synthesis of the evidence for risk factor exposure and the attributable burden of disease. By providing national and subnational assessments spanning the past 25 years, this study can inform debates on the importance of addressing risks in context. Methods We used the comparative risk assessment framework developed for previous iterations of the Global Burden of Disease Study to estimate attributable deaths, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and trends in exposure by age group, sex, year, and geography for 79 behavioural, environmental and occupational, and metabolic risks or clusters of risks from 1990 to 2015. lens.title: A standard procedure for creating a frailty index
lens.summary: Background Frailty can be measured in relation to the accumulation of deficits using a frailty index. A frailty index can be developed from most ageing databases. Our objective is to systematically describe a standard procedure for constructing a frailty index. …
lens.abstract: Background Frailty can be measured in relation to the accumulation of deficits using a frailty index. A frailty index can be developed from most ageing databases. Our objective is to systematically describe a standard procedure for constructing a frailty index. Methods This is a secondary analysis of the Yale Precipitating Events Project cohort study, based in New Haven CT. Non-disabled people aged 70 years or older (n = 754) were enrolled and re-contacted every 18 months. The database includes variables on function, cognition, co-morbidity, health attitudes and practices and physical performance measures. Data came from the baseline cohort and those available at the first 18-month follow-up assessment. refractive.summary: No clinically meaningful differences in stromal haze profiles or visual, tomographic, and aberrometric outcomes were detected between the combined and sequential cohorts at 12 months under the studied protocols.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To objectively evaluate stromal haze and refractive and tomographic results in eyes undergoing combined versus sequential customized transepithelial photorefractive keratectomy (TransPRK) with accelerated corneal cross-linking (A-CXL). METHODS: A prospective observational study of 119 eyes undergoing customized TransPRK either with combined A-CXL (n = 91) or after (median: 36 months) prior A-CXL (n = 28) between 2018 and 2025. All surgeries were performed by the same surgeon using the same laser platform (SCHWIND Amaris; SCHWIND eye-tech-solutions). No mitomycin C (MMC) was used in the combined group, whereas the sequential cohort had 0.02% MMC applied for 20 seconds. Customized ablation targeted mainly higher order aberrations (HOAs). refractive.summary: This case demonstrates a rare but visually significant complication of traumatic FS-LASIK flap avulsion. Despite the precision and stability of femtosecond laser-created flaps, the corneal interface remains biomechanically vulnerable even months postoperatively. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe a rare case of traumatic avulsion of a femtosecond laser-assisted laser in situ keratomileusis (FSLASIK) flap following direct corneal trauma caused by a pet bird. METHODS: A 34-year-old woman presented with pain and visual loss in her left eye after a bird-related corneal injury that occurred 10 months following uneventful FS-LASIK for myopia. Clinical evaluation included slit-lamp examination, anterior segment optical coherence tomography, corneal tomography, and follow-up of visual and structural outcomes. RESULTS: Examination revealed complete absence of the LASIK flap with a sharply demarcated circular epithelial defect corresponding to the flap borders. The avulsed flap was not identified on the ocular surface or within the fornices. The patient was treated with a bandage contact lens and intensive fortified topical antibiotics. refractive.title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence Model for Automated Measurement of the Anterior Segment by Ultrasound Biomicroscopy in ICL Calculation.
refractive.summary: The artificial intelligence model demonstrated good agreement with manual measurements for most anterior segment parameters, with variable performance across parameters. These findings support the potential role of automated UBM-based measurements as an adjunctive tool for anatomical assessment in ICL planning. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the agreement between an artificial intelligence-based automated system and manual ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM) measurements of anterior segment parameters relevant to Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL; STAAR Surgical) planning. METHODS: This cross-sectional, observational, and analytical study was conducted at a tertiary referral ophthalmology center in Mexico City, Mexico. A total of 400 ultrasound biomicroscopy images of the anterior segment corresponding to one image per patient were used to generate segmentation masks and train a U-Net-based automated measurement model. An independent test dataset consisting of 40 UBM images from 40 different patients, not included in the training dataset, was used for model evaluation. refractive.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Transport Properties in Amorphous Polymer Electrolytes Using Chemically Informed Structural Descriptors.
refractive.summary: Amorphous polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for next-generation lithium batteries. They offer improved safety and mechanical stability compared to conventional liquid electrolytes. However, predicting their transport performance remains challenging. …
refractive.abstract: Amorphous polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for next-generation lithium batteries. They offer improved safety and mechanical stability compared to conventional liquid electrolytes. However, predicting their transport performance remains challenging. Ionic conductivity and diffusivity depend on complex, coupled interactions between polymer structure, chemistry, and ion dynamics. This work leverages machine learning to predict four key transport properties in amorphous polymer electrolytes using a molecular dynamics data set of more than 6,000 polymer electrolyte systems. These are ionic conductivity, bis-(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)-imide (TFSI) diffusivity, lithium-ion diffusivity, and polymer diffusivity. refractive.title: Six-month efficacy and safety of toric implantable collamer lens implantation in myopic eyes with asymmetric bow-tie corneal astigmatism: a prospective comparative study.
refractive.summary: At 6 months, TICL implantation provides an effective and safe method for correcting asymmetric bow-tie corneal astigmatism, yielding refractive and visual outcomes that are comparable to those achieved in symmetric bow-tie astigmatism.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the 6-month efficacy and safety of toric implantable collamer lens (TICL) implantation in myopic patients with asymmetric bow-tie corneal astigmatism. METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 25 eyes from 16 patients with asymmetric bow-tie astigmatism and 41 eyes from 24 patients with symmetric bow-tie astigmatism, all undergoing TICL implantation. Corneal topography was assessed using Pentacam high-resolution. Uncorrected and corrected distance visual acuities (UDVA and CDVA), refraction, and higher-order aberrations (HOAs) were evaluated preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively. Vector analysis was employed to assess astigmatic changes. RESULTS: Postoperatively, 100% of eyes in both groups achieved UDVA ≥ 20/20, and UDVA was equal to or higher than preoperative CDVA. refractive.summary: Vitiligo is an autoimmune disease characterized by progressive depigmentation of the skin due to T cell-mediated destruction of melanocytes. Disease onset varies but usually initiates during adolescence. Sex differences in disease development and therapeutic outcomes have not been explored. …
refractive.abstract: Vitiligo is an autoimmune disease characterized by progressive depigmentation of the skin due to T cell-mediated destruction of melanocytes. Disease onset varies but usually initiates during adolescence. Sex differences in disease development and therapeutic outcomes have not been explored. We previously associated stress induced HSP70i with immune activation in depigmentation and showed that HSP70iQ435A can tolerize dendritic cells (DCs) to prevent cutaneous recruitment and activation of T cells. Among male and female vitiligo-prone mice, we investigated the long-term efficacy of HSP70iQ435A plasmid DNA treatment introduced by biolistic administration at varying stages of vitiligo development. refractive.title: Three-Month Ocular Surface and Dry-Eye Outcomes After Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL) Implantation versus Small-Incision Lenticule Extraction (SMILE): A Prospective Non-Randomized Comparative Cohort Study.
refractive.summary: In this non-randomized comparison of patients with clinically normal preoperative ocular surface who received standardized postoperative lubrication, no statistically significant between-group differences were detected for the primary tear-film outcome NIBUT or for NITMH, ORI or OSDI at 3 months. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare ocular surface and dry-eye parameters 3 months after implantable collamer lens (ICL) implantation vs small-incision lenticule extraction (SMILE). PATIENTS AND METHODS: Right eyes of 98 patients with complete data (SMILE, n = 49; ICL, n = 49) were analyzed. Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), non-invasive tear meniscus height (NITMH), non-invasive tear-film break-up time (NIBUT), ocular redness index (ORI), corneal fluorescein staining (CFS), refraction and visual acuity were measured before and 3 months after surgery. Between-group comparisons of change from baseline were the primary analysis. refractive.title: Machine-learning prediction of high implantable collamer lens vault using angle-to-angle anatomy: a patient-grouped internal validation study.
refractive.summary: ATA-based models improved prediction of both high and continuous 1-week ICL vault compared with otherwise matched WTW-based models. When an ICL size has already been selected, ATA-based prediction may help identify eyes that warrant closer review of biometric measurements and the proposed sizing plan.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Machine learning has increasingly been applied to implantable collamer lens (ICL) vault prediction, but the value of anatomically informed feature representation remains uncertain. We evaluated whether angle-to-angle (ATA)-centered anatomy improves prediction of high and continuous postoperative vault compared with white-to-white (WTW)-centered anatomy. METHODS: This retrospective study included 279 eyes from 152 patients with 1-week postoperative vault measurements. Matched regularized supervised machine-learning models were constructed using either ICL size minus WTW or ICL size minus ATA; an expanded ATA model additionally included crystalline lens rise and nasal and temporal anterior chamber angles. refractive.title: 25 Years of Laser Vision Correction Research in the U.S. Army: Advancing Readiness, Safety, and Vision.
refractive.summary: Established in 2000, the Warfighter Refractive Eye Surgery Program (WRESP) positioned refractive surgery at the forefront of enhancing operational readiness. With 25 years of evidence, the WRESP treats the right procedure for the right patient. …
refractive.abstract: Established in 2000, the Warfighter Refractive Eye Surgery Program (WRESP) positioned refractive surgery at the forefront of enhancing operational readiness. With 25 years of evidence, the WRESP treats the right procedure for the right patient. Its lasting contribution is its method: testing new technology against the demands of the mission.

refractive.title: A Volatilomics Approach for the Identification of Volatile Organic Compounds as Biomarkers of Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia Using GC-MS.
refractive.summary: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a common and serious complication of patients at intensive care units (ICUs), contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Current diagnostic approaches for VAP rely on clinical, radiological, and invasive methods, which are time-consuming, carry risks, and may result in delayed or inconclusi …
refractive.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a common and serious complication of patients at intensive care units (ICUs), contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Current diagnostic approaches for VAP rely on clinical, radiological, and invasive methods, which are time-consuming, carry risks, and may result in delayed or inconclusive findings. The need for rapid, reliable, and non-invasive diagnostic tools is critical. Biomarkers and specifically volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled breath have emerged as promising candidates for this purpose. In this study, we applied gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) with solid-phase microextraction (SPME) to analyze breath VOC profiles in critically ill children and explore their potential as early indicators of VAP. refractive.title: Two Strategies in Transepithelial PRK: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
refractive.summary: No significant differences were detected between StreamLight and SmartSurfACE in efficacy, refractive predictability, or safety for myopic TransPRK. The observed epithelial-healing advantage with StreamLight was based on indirect evidence and should be interpreted cautiously.
refractive.abstract: TOPIC: To compare efficacy, refractive predictability, safety, and early recovery after single-step transepithelial photorefractive keratectomy (TransPRK) using StreamLight and SmartSurfACE in myopic eyes through network meta-analysis. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: TransPRK is a flap-free surface ablation option for myopic patients. Direct comparative evidence between TransPRK technologies remains limited. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central, and Web of Science were searched from inception to October 31, 2025. Randomized trials, cohort studies, and case series evaluating single-step TransPRK using StreamLight or SmartSurfACE were included. Alcohol-assisted photorefractive keratectomy (aaPRK) served as the common comparator. Random-effects network meta-analysis was performed. refractive.title: Incomplete Corneal Epithelialization at the One-Week Visit After PRK: Incidence and the Dominance of Examination Timing.
refractive.summary: At one week, incomplete epithelialization is uncommon, is concentrated at day 5, and resolves gradually to a stable baseline by day 7, consistent with assessment timing rather than a distinct entity, and supporting a day-7 review default. It is predominantly patient-level, and no surgical parameter was consistently associated with it.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine the incidence and independent predictors of incomplete corneal epithelialization at the one-week visit after photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), accounting for correlation between fellow eyes. SETTING: A high-volume refractive-surgery network, Israel. DESIGN: Retrospective registry-based cohort study. METHODS: 37,982 eyes of 18,991 patients who underwent bilateral same-session PRK (January 2013-June 2024), examined on postoperative days 5-9. The outcome was modeled by generalized estimating equations (logistic; exchangeable correlation, robust standard errors) clustered on patient. Visit day and optical zone were also modeled categorically; surgeon was examined as a covariate and a clustering level. refractive.title: The Ghana Surgical Dialogue: A Whole-of-Society Innovation for Advancing Safe Surgery, Obstetric, Trauma, and Anesthesia Care in Ghana.
refractive.summary: Ghana continues to face major gaps in access to safe surgery, obstetric, trauma, and anesthesia (SOTA) care, especially at district level, where workforce shortages, infrastructure deficits, weak referral systems, and limited data constrain service delivery. …
refractive.abstract: Ghana continues to face major gaps in access to safe surgery, obstetric, trauma, and anesthesia (SOTA) care, especially at district level, where workforce shortages, infrastructure deficits, weak referral systems, and limited data constrain service delivery. To support implementation of the Ghana National Surgical, Obstetric and Anesthesia Plan (NSOAP) 2025-2029, the Ministry of Health convened the inaugural Ghana Surgical Dialogue in Koforidua in August 2025. The Dialogue brought together government, professional associations, clinicians, nurses, biomedical engineers, laboratory professionals, health managers, financiers, civil society, and international partners to identify practical solutions for strengthening SOTA care. Key innovations included alignment of SOTA priorities with national budgeting, exploration of public-private partnership models such as build-operate-transfer schemes

refractive.title: Efficacy of the Nefertiti Lift for Jawline Contour: A Split-Face Study.
refractive.summary: The Nefertiti lift reliably improves platysmal banding but does not provide meaningful short-term jawline contour improvement.
refractive.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine whether the Nefertiti lift produces a measurable improvement in jawline contour and jowl severity compared with untreated control, and to assess its effect on platysmal banding and patient-reported outcomes. METHODS: This prospective, single-center, split-face study included 20 adult female participants with early lower face and neck aging. One side was randomized to receive onabotulinumtoxinA using the Nefertiti technique, with the contralateral side serving as control. Standardized photographs were obtained at baseline and 2-week follow-up. Two blinded facial plastic surgeons graded jowl contour and platysmal banding using validated scales. Patient-reported outcomes included global esthetic improvement, willingness to pursue or recommend the procedure for jawline contouring. refractive.title: Non-Metric Dental Traits, Dental Caries Experience, Parental Perceptions, and Oral Hygiene Status of Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder-A Step Towards Sustainable Smiles.
refractive.summary: Parents' perceptions regarding oral health among children with ASD are neutral with both behavioral limitations and oral hygiene practices affecting oral health. This study recommends early NMDTs identification and a multidisciplinary approach involving dental professionals, along with targeted parental education and regular follow-up, th …
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is accompanied by poor oral health outcomes for children with ASD. AIM: To assess the occurrence of non-metric dental traits (NMDTs), dental caries experience, parents' perception, and oral hygiene status of children with ASD. METHODOLOGY: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 150 children with ASD and their biological parents. Children with severe sensory or behavioural difficulties who were unable to cooperate for oral examination were excluded. A pre-validated questionnaire was used to assess parental perception. Oral hygiene index-Simplified (OHI-S), Decayed, Missing and Filled Teeth index (DMFT) for permanent and primary dentition was used to assess oral hygiene status and dental caries in children with ASD. refractive.title: Recipient Vessel Utilization in Gracilis Free Functional Muscle Transfer for Facial Reanimation: A 12-Year Single-Center Experience.
refractive.summary: Facial vessels remain the preferred recipients for gracilis FFMT, with the superficial temporal system providing a suitable alternative. Recipient vessel selection was not associated with significant differences in overall complications, flap survival, or muscle activation. …
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Free functional muscle transfer (FFMT) using the gracilis muscle is a well-established technique for smile restoration in long-standing facial paralysis. However, recipient vessel selection remains poorly standardized, particularly when facial vessels are unavailable. This study evaluated recipient vessel utilization, associated clinical outcomes, and potential predictors of alternative vessel selection to propose a practical surgical algorithm. METHODS: A retrospective review of patients undergoing gracilis FFMT for facial reanimation between 2011 and 2022 was performed. Demographic, clinical, and operative characteristics were compared between facial and non-facial recipient vessel groups using Fisher's exact test and Welch's t-test. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression analyses evaluated factors associated with alternative vessel utilization and complications. RES

refractive.title: Different vault outcomes following implantable collamer lens implantation in eyes with ciliary body cysts: a case report.
refractive.summary: These two cases suggest that cyst morphology may be one of several factors associated with postoperative ICL vault in eyes with sulcus-involved ciliary body cysts. Detailed preoperative UBM assessment of cyst structure and sulcus anatomy may be useful for individualized surgical planning and postoperative follow-up. …
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ciliary body cysts are common incidental findings during preoperative screening for implantable collamer lens (ICL) implantation. Although their presence is generally not considered a contraindication to surgery, cysts extending into the ciliary sulcus may influence haptic seating. The potential contribution of cyst morphology to postoperative ICL behavior remains insufficiently described. CASE PRESENTATION: We report two myopic patients with ciliary body cysts protruding into the ciliary sulcus who underwent posterior chamber ICL implantation. Preoperative ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM) was used to evaluate cyst anatomy. Case 1 had a single, qualitatively thin-walled, unilocular cyst and achieved an adequate postoperative vault of 445 μm at 3 months. refractive.title: Prevalence of self-reported dry eye symptoms after refractive surgery among Saudi adults: A cross-sectional survey.
refractive.summary: Refractive surgery corrects vision using different corneal techniques; however, dry eye disease (DED) is one of its commonest side effects. This descriptive survey questionnaire-based study aimed to evaluate prevalence and factors associated with dry eye symptoms after refractive surgery among survey respondents using ocular surface disea …
refractive.abstract: Refractive surgery corrects vision using different corneal techniques; however, dry eye disease (DED) is one of its commonest side effects. This descriptive survey questionnaire-based study aimed to evaluate prevalence and factors associated with dry eye symptoms after refractive surgery among survey respondents using ocular surface disease index (OSDI) questionnaire in Saudi Arabia. Four hundred and thirty nine participants were included. Dry eye OSDI scores compared across different epidemiological risk factors, focusing on refractive surgery type and postoperative duration. refractive.title: Methyl aminolevulinate-PpIX mediated fluorescence-guided mapping of high-grade vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia: a pilot prospective clinical trial (PhotoDiVin).
refractive.summary: The worldwide prevalence of vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia is increasing and is characterized by the high risk of recurrence and evolution towards vulvar cancer. Positive margins following surgical excision are the most important criteria of recurrence risk. …
refractive.abstract: The worldwide prevalence of vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia is increasing and is characterized by the high risk of recurrence and evolution towards vulvar cancer. Positive margins following surgical excision are the most important criteria of recurrence risk. We conducted a pilot clinical study to assess the fluorescence-based cartography of VIN lesions using methyl aminolevulinate (m-ALA), which is a prodrug of the fluorophore protoporphyrin IX (PpIX). A prospective, single-center, single-arm clinical trial included 17 women with histologically confirmed high-grade vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (dVIN or vHSIL). Following topical methyl aminolevulinate application, fluorescence-guided examination under 405-nm light was performed. refractive.title: Total Lower Eyelid Reconstruction With Auricular Cartilage-Perichondrium Graft and Upper Eyelid Rotation Flap.
refractive.summary: Reconstruction of large full-thickness lower eyelid defects remains a complex challenge in oculoplastic surgery because restoration of both functional integrity and aesthetic appearance is required. …
refractive.abstract: Reconstruction of large full-thickness lower eyelid defects remains a complex challenge in oculoplastic surgery because restoration of both functional integrity and aesthetic appearance is required. Successful reconstruction depends on adequate replacement of the posterior lamella to provide structural support and reconstruction of the anterior lamella to ensure appropriate coverage and mobility. The study presents a sample of 10 patients who presented with a basocellular carcinoma of the lower lid. A full-thickness resection with wide margins was performed and medial, lateral, and deep margins were subjected to extemporaneous histologic examination. In all 10 patients, to attain complete resection with 3 mm negative margins, following NCCN recommendations, a full-thickness total lower eyelid resection was performed. refractive.title: Comparative Refractive and Vector Outcomes of PRK in Moderate and High Astigmatism: A 12-Month Retrospective Study.
refractive.summary: PRK is an effective and predictable method for the correction of moderate to high astigmatism.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate the photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) results in patients with moderate to high astigmatism. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: One hundred twelve eyes of 71 patients with a cylindrical component of greater than 3 diopters (D) (moderate: 3.00 to 3.99 D; high: ≥4.00 D) undergone PRK were reviewed. UDVA, CDVA, and subjective refraction before and after surgery (1, 3, 6, 12 months) were extracted. RESULTS: The preoperative mean spherical equivalent (SE) was -3.39 ± 1.82 D (range -9.00 to 2.50 D), and the mean cylinder was -3.76 ± 0.78 D (range -3.00 to -6.00 D). refractive.summary: This series highlights early recognition of extensively drug-resistant infections after PRK surgery, source identification, and prompt, microbiology-guided therapy, resulting in favorable outcomes.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aims to report the clinico-microbiological characteristics of cases of infectious keratitis caused by extensively drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa after photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) and to identify the source of infection. METHODS: Retrospective review of 7 eyes from 4 patients presenting with infectious keratitis after bilateral PRK performed at different centers and time points, evaluated at a tertiary eye care center in India between March 2024 and August 2025. We analyzed demographic, clinical, microbiological, treatment, and outcome data. RESULTS: The study included 7 eyes from 4 patients. Patients presented, on average, after 2.5 days (range, 1-4 ), and visual acuity ranged from 20/50 to perception of light with inaccurate projection of rays. refractive.title: OPTIMIZ: A Constraint-Driven Tool for Decision-Making in Full- Arch Rehabilitation.
refractive.summary: OPTIMIZ is a practical tool developed to simplify decision-making and improve treatment predictability in full-arch rehabilitation while minimizing avoidable surgical intervention. The tool should be used in conjunction with comprehensive patient evaluation, individualized treatment planning, and professional clinical judgment.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To present OPTIMIZ, a clinical tool developed to simplify restorative decision-making in full-arch implant rehabilitation of the edentulous maxilla. OVERVIEW: Decision-making remains one of the most challenging aspects of full-arch implant rehabilitation. Implant-supported fixed complete prostheses (iFCPs) may provide highly favorable biologic, functional, and esthetic outcomes. However, their success depends on appropriate case selection and careful evaluation of esthetic, prosthetic, functional, soft tissue and bone-related factors. Inappropriate treatment selection may result in compromised esthetics, avoidable bone reduction, or overtreatment through extensive augmentation procedures. refractive.title: Surgical Treatment of Congenital Facial Palsy: A Retrospective Analysis of More than 20 Years' Experience in Smile Surgery.
refractive.summary: Background and Objectives: Congenital facial palsy, either isolated or associated with syndromic conditions such as Moebius syndrome, is a rare disorder that poses significant functional and psychological challenges for patients, families, and healthcare teams. …
refractive.abstract: Background and Objectives: Congenital facial palsy, either isolated or associated with syndromic conditions such as Moebius syndrome, is a rare disorder that poses significant functional and psychological challenges for patients, families, and healthcare teams. Dedicated care pathways and a multidisciplinary approach are essential for optimal management. This study presents our experience of more than 20 years in smile surgery, highlighting clinical outcomes with an objective analysis of facial symmetry and movement as well as a review of our progressive improvements of surgical techniques and patient management over time. Materials and Methods: Patients diagnosed with congenital facial palsy who were referred to our institution for rehabilitative treatment and surgical management between January 2003 and December 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. refractive.title: Parent-Reported Orofacial Health in Preterm- and Term-Born Children: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
refractive.summary: Longer reported pacifier use was associated with a broad parental perception of smile abnormality after FDR correction; causality and clinical significance cannot be established. The findings require confirmation using clinically verified perinatal data and standardized orofacial assessment.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Early feeding experiences and non-nutritive sucking habits coexist with the development of orofacial functions and occlusion. This study compared the duration of breastfeeding, bottle feeding, and mixed feeding, as well as parent-reported orofacial outcomes in preterm- and term-born children, and exploratorily assessed associations among these variables. METHODS: A cross-sectional parent/caregiver survey used open convenience recruitment in online prematurity-related groups. The main comparison included 108 children (88 preterm and 20 term). Unambiguous duration records for all three feeding modes were available for 92 children and were analyzed as separate quantitative variables. refractive.title: Anterior vault as a risk stratification marker for trabecular-iris angle reduction after implantable collamer lens implantation.
refractive.summary: This study identified AV, WTW/ACD ratio, and preoperative angle metrics as key markers associated with postoperative TIA500 ≤20° after ICL implantation. AV proved to be a simple, clinically valuable marker to enhance risk stratification.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate the clinical utility of the anterior vault (AV), as measured by anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT), as a risk stratification marker for a postoperative trabecular-iris angle (TIA) ≤ 20° following Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL) implantation. Additionally, this study investigated postoperative alterations in iridocorneal angle dynamics after ICL placement. METHODS: This retrospective, observational study was conducted at a single private hospital and included 185 eyes from 185 patients who underwent ICL implantation between January 2018 and December 2023. The primary endpoint was to evaluate the discriminative performance of AV for identifying eyes with postoperative TIA500 ≤20°. refractive.title: Comparison of toric implantable collamer lens and bioptics for correction of high myopia with astigmatism.
refractive.summary: Both TICL and Bioptics are excellent options for correction of high myopia with astigmatism, Both showing comparable refractive and visual results and satisfaction scores.
refractive.abstract: AIM OF THE WORK: This work aims to offer a comparison of toric implantable collamer lens and bioptics for correction of high myopia with astigmatism, focusing on their clinical efficacy, safety profiles, complications and patient satisfaction. BACKGROUND: High myopia with astigmatism poses significant challenges to visual correction, affecting not only the quality of life but also daily functioning. Toric Implantable Collamer Lenses (TICL) and Bioptic (implantation of spherical ICL followed by laser vision correction to the residual astigmatism) procedures, represent two effective surgical interventions for correction of high myopia with astigmatism. METHODS: This study was designed as a prospective interventional case study. refractive.title: The Stomatognathic System as an Expanding Frontier for Botulinum Toxin Therapy.
refractive.summary: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) therapy has expanded from focal chemodenervation to a versatile therapeutic modality used across multiple medical specialties. The stomatognathic system is particularly suited to BoNT therapy because motor, sensory, articular, secretory, and aesthetic functions converge within a compact anatomical region. …
refractive.abstract: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) therapy has expanded from focal chemodenervation to a versatile therapeutic modality used across multiple medical specialties. The stomatognathic system is particularly suited to BoNT therapy because motor, sensory, articular, secretory, and aesthetic functions converge within a compact anatomical region. Current and emerging applications include oromandibular dystonia, dyskinesia, bruxism, tremor, hemimasticatory spasm, embouchure dystonia, masticatory muscle and temporomandibular disorder-related pain, trigeminal neuralgia, recurrent temporomandibular joint dislocation, sialorrhea, Frey syndrome, masseter prominence, gummy smile, and perioral wrinkles. Evidence and regulatory status vary substantially among indications, and many applications remain off-label. Dentistry and oral and maxillofacial surgery have historically played a limited role in BoNT therapy

refractive.title: Short- and Long-Term Dynamics of Endothelial Cell Density and Vault Changes After Implantable Collamer Lens Implantation.
refractive.summary: Background/Objectives: Endothelial cell density (ECD) and vault height are essential safety metrics in implantable collamer lens (ICL) surgery, yet their reported decay rates vary. This study assessed short- and long-term changes in ECD and vault height. …
refractive.abstract: Background/Objectives: Endothelial cell density (ECD) and vault height are essential safety metrics in implantable collamer lens (ICL) surgery, yet their reported decay rates vary. This study assessed short- and long-term changes in ECD and vault height. Methods: Medical records of patients undergoing V4c ICL implantation between 2014 and 2024 were reviewed. ECD loss was evaluated across three periods: early (baseline to 6 months), late (6 months to last visit), and total (baseline to last visit). Vault was measured at day 1 and months 3, 6, 12, and the last visit and decay rate was calculated for the entire follow-up period. Results: A total of 631 eyes of 323 patients were analyzed. The early, late, and total ECD losses per year were 1.81 ± 8.56% (95% CI 0.43 to 3.19), 0.68 ± 2.11% (95% CI 0.34 to 1.03), and 1.21 ± 2.58% (95% CI 0.83 to 1.59), respectively. refractive.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of the eHealth-faciLitated SMILe-integrated care model on treatment burden, quality of life and graft-versus-host disease after allogeneic stem cell transplantation: results of two European randomized controlled implementation studies.
refractive.summary: The SMILe Integrated Care Model (SMILe-ICM) has previously demonstrated feasibility, successful implementation, and promising effects on survival, re-hospitalization, and cost-effectiveness following allogeneic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT). …
refractive.abstract: The SMILe Integrated Care Model (SMILe-ICM) has previously demonstrated feasibility, successful implementation, and promising effects on survival, re-hospitalization, and cost-effectiveness following allogeneic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT). To complement these findings and provide a more comprehensive evaluation of the intervention's effects, we evaluated patient-reported and clinical secondary outcomes from two RCTs. Data from two hybrid effectiveness-implementation RCTs conducted at two European alloSCT centers (Germany, Switzerland) were analyzed. Adult alloSCT recipients were randomized 1:1 to usual care (UCG) or the SMILe-ICM, a multicomponent intervention combining eHealth with advanced practice nurse-led self-management support. refractive.summary: Avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) is the cause of avian colibacillosis, which leads to huge economic losses in poultry production worldwide, and presents significant zoonotic antimicrobial resistance (AMR) risk. …
refractive.abstract: Avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) is the cause of avian colibacillosis, which leads to huge economic losses in poultry production worldwide, and presents significant zoonotic antimicrobial resistance (AMR) risk. Cell-permeable itaconate derivatives exhibit dual antibacterial and immunomodulatory properties; however, they have not been systematically evaluated against APEC, and their underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined for this pathogen. In the present study, we systematically explored the anti-APEC therapeutic potential and mechanism of action of 4-octyl itaconate (4-OI) using an integrated approach of in vitro phenotypic, ex vivo macrophage, biochemical genetic, and dual in vivo infection models. This prospective study aimed to compare stability and outcomes following two approaches for counterclockwise mandibular setback in bimaxillary rotational surgery to correct skeletal class III high-angle malocclusion. Fifty-six adult patients with skeletal class III high-angle malocclusion who underwent surgery-first bimaxillary surgery with counterclockwise mandibular setback were analyzed. Patients were grouped by different direction of mandibular distal segment: posterior-shortening (n = 25) and posterior-lengthening (n = 31). refractive.title: The Potential Role of Postbiotics in Periodontitis Treatment and Preventive Dentistry.
refractive.summary: Postbiotics, the bioactive molecules of probiotics and inactive microbial cells, have emerged as promising supplementary method in dental health treatment, specifically targeting disorders such as periodontitis. …
refractive.abstract: Postbiotics, the bioactive molecules of probiotics and inactive microbial cells, have emerged as promising supplementary method in dental health treatment, specifically targeting disorders such as periodontitis. The definition, mechanisms of action and therapeutic potential of postbiotics in periodontitis are discussed in detail in this review. The capacity of postbiotics to control pathogenic bacteria development, increase immune responses and restore microbial balance, demonstrates the many roles of postbiotics in antimicrobial activity and anti-inflammatory effects in controlling the oral microbiome. Importantly, postbiotics have potential advantages over live probiotics such as greater stability and safety, without the need for microbial colonization. refractive.title: Intermediate and near vision outcomes with an advanced monofocal aspheric Swiss Phob intraocular lens.
refractive.summary: The Swiss Phob advanced monofocal IOL provides good distance and intermediate visual acuity with functional near vision. The significant reciprocal association between uncorrected intermediate and near visual acuity suggests an extended range of functional vision across intermediate and near distances.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate postoperative visual outcomes at distance, intermediate, and near and determine correlation between intermediate and near vision following implantation of an advanced monofocal aspheric Swiss Phob intraocular lens (IOL). METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 60 eyes of 30 patients who underwent bilateral cataract surgery with Swiss Phob IOL implantation before May 2024. Postoperative evaluation at 6-12 months included uncorrected distance (UDVA), intermediate (UIVA), and near visual acuity (UNVA). refractive.title: Topical Losartan in the Management of Corneal Scarring from Trauma and Infection: A Case Series.
refractive.summary: Topical losartan may be an effective treatment for corneal scarring secondary to trauma or infection either following or in conjunction with corticosteroid therapy. Patients with such scarring should be considered for inclusion in future clinical trials which investigate the efficacy and safety of topical losartan treatment.
refractive.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Losartan inhibits ERK-mediated signaling in the noncanonical transforming growth factor β (TGFβ) pathway, which may play a role in corneal fibrosis. Rabbit studies have shown that topical losartan can reduce stromal scarring, fibrosis, and myofibroblast formation after corneal injuries and other clinical insults. Its use in humans has since been reported for corneal scarring and haze following LASIK, corneal cross-linking, and herpes simplex and varicella-zoster virus infections. Here, we present several additional clinical scenarios in which topical losartan has demonstrated potential efficacy in reducing corneal scarring. refractive.title: Keratorefractive Surgery in Patients with Systemic Isotretinoin Exposure: A Propensity-Score-Matched Analysis of LASIK and PRK.
refractive.summary: Outcomes of LASIK and PRK were comparable between eyes with documented preoperative isotretinoin exposure and matched unexposed eyes across all cessation intervals observed, including surgery within days of documented use. These preliminary findings warrant prospective confirmation with ocular-surface endpoints.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine whether documented preoperative systemic isotretinoin exposure affects LASIK and PRK outcomes and complications. SETTING: Care Vision Laser Center, Tel Aviv, Israel. DESIGN: Retrospective comparative cohort study. METHODS: Consecutive primary myopic LASIK and PRK procedures (January 2013 to June 2024), excluding retreated and monovision eyes, were reviewed. Exposure was ascertained from clinical notes and a preoperative medication questionnaire; patients whose exposure began after surgery were excluded. Exposed patients were propensity-score matched 1:4 to controls on age, sex, year of surgery, and preoperative spherical equivalent (SEQ), cylinder, and central corneal thickness. refractive.title: Facial esthetic medicine in dentistry: botulinum toxin and hyaluronic acid fillers for smile-face harmonization.
refractive.summary: Orofacial treatment planning is being redefined by the convergence of minimally invasive facial aesthetic medicine and aesthetic dentistry. Specifically, hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers and botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A) are being employed more frequently as adjuncts to maximize smile-lip-face harmony. …
refractive.abstract: Orofacial treatment planning is being redefined by the convergence of minimally invasive facial aesthetic medicine and aesthetic dentistry. Specifically, hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers and botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A) are being employed more frequently as adjuncts to maximize smile-lip-face harmony. The scope of non-invasive or minimally invasive facial aesthetic medicine for dentists has also been clarified by regulatory changes in Italy, underscoring the importance of competency-based training and organized risk management. The objective is to give a narrative summary of BoNT-A and HA fillers' indications, clinical procedures, integration into dental workflows, and safety concerns in dental practice, with a focus on perioral applications and complication management. refractive.abstract: Off-target polypharmacology across the conserved kinase ATP pocket can limit the safety and efficacy of kinase-directed compounds. HuKSA is a transparent ligand-based framework that predicts kinase targets and estimates measured-kinome selectivity from a SMILES string while exposing the reference activities behind each estimate. The method compares ECFP4 fingerprints by Tanimoto similarity and applies five-neighbour, similarity-weighted read-across to an atlas of 794 compounds with measurements spanning 464 kinases. Selectivity is summarized by the S-score, the fraction of measured kinases with pActivity above 6. refractive.title: Unilateral macrostomia repair using modified muscle reconstruction: Long-term anthropometric evaluation of static and smile symmetry.
refractive.summary: Long-term postoperative assessment results indicated that the modified muscle reconstruction technique was associated with favorable static and smile symmetry.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Macrostomia, or transverse facial cleft, substantially impairs facial esthetics and oral function. Although various repair techniques have been reported, achieving satisfactory bilateral symmetry, particularly during dynamic expressions such as smiling, continues to be a challenge. Here, we introduce our modified muscle reconstruction technique for unilateral macrostomia repair and evaluate long-term outcomes in static and smile symmetry using anthropometric measurements. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on all patients who underwent unilateral macrostomia repair at our institution between December 2008 and December 2019. refractive.title: Language of Toxicity: An eXplainable Artificial Intelligence Approach.
refractive.summary: Toxicity prediction in small molecules represents a fundamental challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment. Traditional approaches heavily rely on predefined molecular descriptors or fingerprints, potentially limiting the ability to capture complex and nonlinear structure-activity relationships. …
refractive.abstract: Toxicity prediction in small molecules represents a fundamental challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment. Traditional approaches heavily rely on predefined molecular descriptors or fingerprints, potentially limiting the ability to capture complex and nonlinear structure-activity relationships. Here, we present a descriptor-free, language-inspired framework that can be applied to different toxicity prediction tasks within a unified architecture. The model proposed combines a multiscale Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layer to capture chemical patterns at different scales and a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) layer to capture the sequential nature of these patterns. This architecture also exploits an attention mechanism that computes attention weights across the sequence, enabling the model to focus on the most relevant molecular substructures for toxicity prediction. refractive.summary: Within the limitations of this study, we did not detect evidence of statistical difference between SMILE and SMILE Pro surgical procedures when used for the treatment of myopia and astigmatism. SMILE Pro using VISUMAX 800 provided more accurate refractive cylinder outcomes. …

METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched up to February 2026 to identify relevant studies. The PRISMA guidelines were followed. Primary outcomes were postoperative efficacy, safety, and predictability at the end of follow-up. Secondary outcomes were the postoperative high-order aberrations (HOAs) parameters and the vector analysis parameters. refractive.summary: Trans-mastoid facial nerve decompression is safe and effective for persistent facial paralysis secondary to retroauricular HA injection, yielding significant functional improvement and high patient satisfaction.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Retroauricular hyaluronic acid (HA) injection for aesthetic enhancement can precipitate immediate-onset facial nerve palsy. The underlying mechanism remains unclear, and no consensus exists on the next step when prolonged conservative therapy fails. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the pathogenesis of persistent facial paralysis following retroauricular HA injection and to evaluate the functional and aesthetic outcomes of trans-mastoid facial nerve decompression in affected patients. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 17 patients (16 females, 1 male; mean age 33.65±7.91 years) who developed immediate-onset unilateral facial paralysis after retroauricular HA injection and showed no improvement after 4 weeks of conservative therapy. refractive.title: Health and economic benefits of air quality improvements in France through diverse net-zero transition scenarios by 2050.
refractive.summary: Net-Zero transition can deliver substantial health and economic co-benefits across diverse policy pathways. These findings support integrating co-benefits into climate policy frameworks to strengthen the evidence base for ambitious mitigation action.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Climate mitigation can deliver substantial air quality co-benefits, yet these remain poorly quantified across pathways ranging from sufficiency-to technology-driven transitions. This study compares four French energy-transition scenarios for 2030 and 2050 against a 2019 baseline under fixed meteorology, evaluating annual PM2.5 and NO2 concentration changes and health and economic co-benefits. refractive.title: Impact of Laser Vision Correction on Readiness and Operational Performance Among Active Duty Service Members.
refractive.summary: LVC is associated with substantial self-reported improvements in visual readiness and operational task performance, with exceptionally high, comparable satisfaction across PRK, LASIK, and SMILE cohorts. …
refractive.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Optimal visual performance is essential for modern military operations. Traditional forms of vision correction, including spectacles and contact lenses, may present operational limitations during deployment or field training. The Department of Defense established the Warfighter Refractive Eye Surgery Program (WRESP) to provide laser vision correction (LVC) to improve operational readiness by reducing reliance on corrective eyewear among active duty service members (ADSM). This study evaluated ADSMs' perceptions of overall satisfaction, visual outcomes, operational performance, and military readiness following LVC performed at the Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA)-Lackland, Joint Warfighter Refractive Surgery Center (JWRSC). refractive.title: Refractive surgery.
refractive.summary: Refractive surgery has evolved beyond laser refractive techniques over the past decade. refractive.abstract: Refractive surgery has evolved beyond laser refractive techniques over the past decade. Laser refractive surgery procedures (such as laser in-situ keratomileusis), surface ablation techniques (such as laser epithelial keratomileusis), and photorefractive keratectomy have now been established as fairly safe procedures that produce excellent visual outcomes for patients with low-to-moderate amounts of ametropia. Additionally, a broader selection of options are now available to treat a wider range of refractive errors. Small incision lenticule extraction uses a femtosecond laser to shape a refractive lenticule, which is removed through a small wound. The potential advantages of this procedure include greater tectonic strength and less dry eye. In the future, intracorneal implants could be used to treat hyperopia or presbyopia. refractive.abstract: UNLABELLED: This review looks at the benefits, limitations, complications, and future applications of the small-incision lenticule extraction procedure. Using the search terms small incision lenticule extraction and femtosecond lenticule extraction, we obtained data from 56 articles (omitting German and Chinese articles) from the PubMed database. Small-incision lenticule extraction has shown efficacy, predictability, and safety that are proportionate to those of laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK), with the additional benefit that it eliminates flap creation and the attendant risks. The potential advantages of the procedure related to improved biomechanical stability, postoperative inflammation, and dry-eye symptoms have not been fully established. Small-incision lenticule extraction-treated eyes have shown a reduced degree of postoperative corneal denervation and higher-order aberratio

refractive.title: Refractive surgery beyond 2020.
refractive.summary: Refractive surgery refers to any procedure that corrects or minimizes refractive errors. Today, refractive surgery has evolved beyond the traditional laser refractive surgery, embodied by the popular laser in situ keratomileusis or 'LASIK'. …
refractive.abstract: Refractive surgery refers to any procedure that corrects or minimizes refractive errors. Today, refractive surgery has evolved beyond the traditional laser refractive surgery, embodied by the popular laser in situ keratomileusis or 'LASIK'. New keratorefractive techniques such as small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) avoids corneal flap creation and uses a single laser device, while advances in surface ablation techniques have seen a resurgence in its popularity. Presbyopic treatment options have also expanded to include new ablation profiles, intracorneal implants, and phakic intraocular implants. With the improved safety and efficacy of refractive lens exchange, a wider variety of intraocular lens implants with advanced optics provide more options for refractive correction in carefully selected patients. Given that dry eye is a common complaint following keratorefractive surgery, evaluation, and treatment of periocular conditions that further predispose the patient to dry eye symptoms is an important part of the presurgical assessm …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Refractive surgery is one of the most popular elective procedures performed in the world. Given that dry eye is a common complaint following keratorefractive surgery, evaluation, and treatment of periocular conditions that further predispose the patient to dry eye symptoms is an important part of the presurgical assessment. Periocular conditions and surgeries can also affect the ocular surface and keratometry, and should be addressed. For example, ptosis, orbital fat herniation, ectropion, and eyelid masses have been shown to induce corneal topography changes and astigmatism. The oculoplastic considerations for refractive surgery include both the contribution of eyelid position on dry eye, ocular surface damage, refractive error, and outcomes, as well as the timing of oculoplastic surgery in relation to the refractive surgery. refractive.title: Astigmatism Correction Using SMILE.
refractive.summary: Small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) was introduced in the recent decade for the treatment of myopia and myopic astigmatism. This flap-free technique has a high efficacy and safety profile and also carries potential advantages over laser in situ keratomileusis such as a better corneal biomechanical stability, reduction in dry eyes  …
refractive.abstract: Small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) was introduced in the recent decade for the treatment of myopia and myopic astigmatism. This flap-free technique has a high efficacy and safety profile and also carries potential advantages over laser in situ keratomileusis such as a better corneal biomechanical stability, reduction in dry eyes rate, and the avoidance of flap complications. However, there have been concerns regarding the precision of astigmatism correction that undercorrection has been reported to be apparent. Various factors that affect astigmatism correction have been identified in the literature. The purpose of this review is to discuss the factors that affect astigmatism correction in SMILE and several techniques to improve the refractive outcomes.

refractive.title: Refractive Eye Surgery: Helping Patients Make Informed Decisions About LASIK.
refractive.summary: A variety of refractive surgery techniques, which reshape the corneal stroma using laser energy, have been marketed as simple and safe alternatives to glasses or contact lenses. Laser-assisted in-situ keratomileusis (LASIK) is the most common of these procedures. …
refractive.abstract: A variety of refractive surgery techniques, which reshape the corneal stroma using laser energy, have been marketed as simple and safe alternatives to glasses or contact lenses. Laser-assisted in-situ keratomileusis (LASIK) is the most common of these procedures. Although there are few high-quality prospective studies of long-term outcomes, complications, or stability for refractive surgery procedures, there is at least general agreement that more than 90% of appropriately selected patients achieve excellent uncorrected distance vision. In addition to well-recognized contraindications (e.g., unstable refraction, pregnancy and lactation, chronic eye disease, systemic illness, corneal abnormalities), there are other conditions that warrant caution (e.g., excessively dry eyes, contact lens intolerance, chronic pain syndromes). Postoperative dry eye, which may in part represent a corneal neu

refractive.title: TFOS DEWS II iatrogenic report.
refractive.summary: Dry eye can be caused by a variety of iatrogenic interventions. The increasing number of patients looking for eye care or cosmetic procedures involving the eyes, together with a better understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms of dry eye disease (DED), have led to the need for a specific report about iatrogenic dry eye within the …
refractive.abstract: Dry eye can be caused by a variety of iatrogenic interventions. The increasing number of patients looking for eye care or cosmetic procedures involving the eyes, together with a better understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms of dry eye disease (DED), have led to the need for a specific report about iatrogenic dry eye within the TFOS DEWS II. Topical medications can cause DED due to their allergic, toxic and immuno-inflammatory effects on the ocular surface. Preservatives, such as benzalkonium chloride, may further aggravate DED. A variety of systemic drugs can also induce DED secondary to multiple mechanisms. Moreover, the use of contact lens induces or is associated with DED. However, one of the most emblematic situations is DED caused by surgical procedures such as corneal refractive surgery as in laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) and keratoplasty due to mechanis

refractive.title: Dry Eye After LASIK.
refractive.summary: Post-LASIK dry eye is the most common postoperative dry eye after ophthalmic surgeries. The clinical signs of post-LASIK dry eye include positive vital staining of the ocular surface, decreased tear breakup time and Schirmer test values, reduced corneal sensitivity, and decreased functional visual acuity. …
refractive.abstract: Post-LASIK dry eye is the most common postoperative dry eye after ophthalmic surgeries. The clinical signs of post-LASIK dry eye include positive vital staining of the ocular surface, decreased tear breakup time and Schirmer test values, reduced corneal sensitivity, and decreased functional visual acuity. The symptoms and signs usually last for about 1 month after LASIK. A small number of patients continue to experience symptoms more than 1 year postoperatively. It has been suggested that the loss of corneal innervation caused by flap-making is the major cause, affecting the corneal-lacrimal gland, corneal-blinking, and blinking-meibomian gland reflexes, resulting in decreased aqueous and lipid tear secretion and mucin expression. A new type of corneal refractive surgery, SMILE, which has less impact on corneal nerves, induces less postoperative dry eye, supporting the association betwee

refractive.title: Excimer laser surface ablation: a review of recent literature.
refractive.summary: The aim was to review the recently published literature on excimer laser surface ablation procedures, including photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), laser sub-epithelial keratomileusis (LASEK), microkeratome-assisted PRK (epi-LASIK) and trans-epithelial (laser-assisted) PRK, to help elucidate where and how surface ablation may best fit into …
refractive.abstract: The aim was to review the recently published literature on excimer laser surface ablation procedures, including photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), laser sub-epithelial keratomileusis (LASEK), microkeratome-assisted PRK (epi-LASIK) and trans-epithelial (laser-assisted) PRK, to help elucidate where and how surface ablation may best fit into current refractive surgical practice. The emphasis was on publications within the last three years and included systemic reviews, meta-analyses and randomised controlled trials. Where such evidence did not exist, selective large series cohort studies, case-controlled studies and case series with follow-up preferably greater than six months were examined and included. refractive.title: Femtosecond laser refractive surgery: small-incision lenticule extraction vs. femtosecond laser-assisted LASIK.
refractive.summary: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Small-incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) is a novel technique devised to correct refractive errors. SMILE circumvents excimer laser photoablation of cornea, as the stromal lenticule cut by femtosecond laser is removed manually. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Small-incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) is a novel technique devised to correct refractive errors. SMILE circumvents excimer laser photoablation of cornea, as the stromal lenticule cut by femtosecond laser is removed manually. Smaller incisions and preservation of anterior corneal biomechanical strength have been suggested as some of the advantages of SMILE over femtosecond laser-assisted LASIK (FS-LASIK). In this review, we compared previous published results of SMILE and FS-LASIK. The advantage, efficacy and safety of SMILE are compared with FS-LASIK. RECENT FINDINGS: SMILE achieved similar efficacy, predictability and safety as FS-LASIK. Greater preservations of corneal biomechanical strength and corneal nerves were observed in SMILE when compared with LASIK or PRK. refractive.title: Dry Eye After Small Incision Lenticule Extraction and Femtosecond Laser-Assisted LASIK: Meta-Analysis.
refractive.summary: According to this meta-analysis, the SMILE procedure has fewer negative impacts on the ocular surface and corneal innervation than does FS-LASIK. Furthermore, SMILE shows superiority over FS-LASIK by a exhibiting a lower risk of postoperative dry eye.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare postoperative ocular surface integrity and innervation between small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) and femtosecond laser-assisted laser in situ keratomileusis (FS-LASIK). METHODS: The Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PubMED, and EMBASE were searched for prospective comparative studies. Trials meeting the selection criteria were quality appraised, and the data were extracted by 2 independent authors. The weighted mean differences (WMDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were used to compare dry eye examinations and corneal subbasal nerve density (SMILE-FS-LASIK). RESULTS: The study covered 5 trials. No significant difference was found in the Schirmer test score between both groups (WMD = -1.91 and 0.27; 95% CI, -5.02 to 1.20 and -0.99 to 1.54; P = 0.23 and 0.67 at 1- and 6-month follow-ups, respectively). refractive.title: Enhancement Options After Myopic Small-Incision Lenticule Extraction (SMILE): A Review.
refractive.summary: Refractive enhancement after SMILE is currently mostly performed by surface ablation, CIRCLE cap-to-flap conversion or thin-flap LASIK, which all offer safety and efficacy comparable to LASIK retreatments. In this review, a detailed overview over each method, its technical aspects, and specific advantages and disadvantages is given.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To provide an overview of the currently available retreatment methods after myopic small-incision lenticule extraction (SMILE). DESIGN: Systematic literature review. METHODS: The PubMed library was searched for articles containing the terms "small-incision lenticule extraction" and "enhancement" or "retreatment". The last search was performed on May 1, 2019. RESULTS: In contrast to laser in-situ keratomileusis (LASIK), which can be retreated by a flap relift, repeat SMILE retreatment is currently not approved and only seldomly performed. As substitutes, surface ablation, cap-to-flap conversion using the CIRCLE program in the VisuMax platform, and thin-flap LASIK have been recently established. refractive.title: Keratitis following laser refractive surgery: Clinical spectrum, prevention and management.
refractive.summary: Laser refractive surgery (LRS) is one of the most demanding areas of ophthalmic surgery and high level of precision is required to meet outcome expectations of patients. Post-operative recovery is of vital importance. Keratitis occurring after LRS can delay visual recovery. …
refractive.abstract: Laser refractive surgery (LRS) is one of the most demanding areas of ophthalmic surgery and high level of precision is required to meet outcome expectations of patients. Post-operative recovery is of vital importance. Keratitis occurring after LRS can delay visual recovery. Both surface ablations [Photorefractive keratectomy (PRK)] as well as flap procedures [Laser in-situ keratomileusis (LASIK)/Small incision lenticule extraction] are prone to this complication. Reported incidence of post-LRS infectious keratitis is between 0% and 1.5%. The rate of infections after PRK seems to be higher than that after LASIK. Staphylococci, streptococci, and mycobacteria are the common etiological organisms. About 50-60% of patients present within the first week of surgery. Of the non-infectious keratitis, diffuse lamellar keratitis (DLK) is the most common with reported rates between 0.4% and 4.38%. T

refractive.title: Biology of keratorefractive surgery- PRK, PTK, LASIK, SMILE, inlays and other refractive procedures.
refractive.summary: The outcomes of refractive surgical procedures to improve uncorrected vision in patients-including photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), laser in-situ keratomileusis (LASIK), Small Incision Lenticule Extraction (SMILE) and corneal inlay procedures-is in large part determined by the corneal wound healing response after surgery. …
refractive.abstract: The outcomes of refractive surgical procedures to improve uncorrected vision in patients-including photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), laser in-situ keratomileusis (LASIK), Small Incision Lenticule Extraction (SMILE) and corneal inlay procedures-is in large part determined by the corneal wound healing response after surgery. The wound healing response varies depending on the type of surgery, the level of intended correction of refractive error, the post-operative inflammatory response, generation of opacity producing myofibroblasts and likely poorly understood genetic factors.
