cataract.title: Bilateral electric cataracts: clinicopathologic report.
cataract.summary: We report a case with bilateral intumescent electric cataracts, outcomes of cataract surgery with a new technique, and a histopathologic study of the anterior capsule followed by a review of the literature on electric cataracts. …
cataract.abstract: We report a case with bilateral intumescent electric cataracts, outcomes of cataract surgery with a new technique, and a histopathologic study of the anterior capsule followed by a review of the literature on electric cataracts. The patient had bilateral cataract extraction and posterior chamber intraocular lens implantation, achieving a visual acuity of 20/20. Hematoxylin and eosin staining of the anterior capsule revealed significant scar tissue formation consisting of fibroblast proliferation and hyaloid production over the basement membrane of the anterior capsule. Electric injuries can cause bilateral intumescent cataracts; the outcomes after cataract surgery are excellent provided the fundus and optic nerve examinations are normal. Scar formation over the anterior capsule may disturb lens nutrition, leading to cataract formation.

cataract.title: A systematic overview of the incidence of posterior capsule opacification.
cataract.summary: Visually significant PCO develops in more than 25% of patients undergoing standard extracapsular cataract extraction or phacoemulsification with posterior chamber intraocular lens implantation over the first 5 years after surgery. …
cataract.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Reported rates of posterior capsule opacification (PCO) vary widely and are based on various definitions of PCO, varying lengths and intervals of follow-up, and the use of different surgical techniques, intraocular lens (i.o.l.) designs, and methods of IOL implantation. This study was designed to obtain a more precise overall estimate of the incidence of PCO and to explore factors that might influence the rate of PCO development. DESIGN: A meta-analysis. METHODS: Published articles were selected for study based on a computerized MEDLINE search of the literature and a manual search of the bibliographies of relevant articles. Articles meeting selected inclusion criteria were reviewed systematically, and the reported data were abstracted and synthesized using the statistical techniques of meta-analysis. cataract.title: Phacoemulsification and intraocular lens implantation combined with trabeculotomy for open-angle glaucoma and coexisting cataract.
cataract.summary: The outcome of the combined operation for open-angle glaucoma and coexisting cataract was promising.
cataract.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To study the outcome of phacoemulsification and intraocular lens implantation combined with trabeculotomy. METHODS: We performed trabeculotomy combined with phacoemulsification and foldable lens implantation in 25 eyes with open-angle glaucoma and coexisting cataract in 18 patients. The series comprised 9 males (13 eyes) and 9 females (12 eyes). Mean age of the patients was 73.4 +/- 10.9 years (45-87 years). Mean follow-up period was 14.3 +/- 6.0 months (6-24 months). RESULTS: The preoperative intraocular pressure was 21.4 +/- 3.7 mm Hg. The postoperative intraocular pressure 6 months after the surgery was 12.8 +/- 3.4 mm Hg. A postoperative tension spike (>30 mm Hg) was observed in 2 eyes. Six months after the operation, the intraocular pressure was controlled under 21 mm Hg in all eyes, and under 16 mm Hg in 18 eyes. cataract.title: Phacoemulsification and intraocular lens implantation for angle closure glaucoma after the relief of pupillary block.
cataract.summary: Phacoemulsification and IOL implantation is useful in IOP control for angle closure glaucoma after relief of pupillary block. However, we should take care of operative complications because of a shallow anterior chamber, poor mydriasis and zonular weakness.
cataract.abstract: PURPOSE: We studied the surgical outcomes of phacoemulsification and intraocular lens (IOL) implantation for cataract and/or uncontrolled intraocular pressure (IOP) in eyes with angle closure glaucoma. SETTING: Department of Ophthalmology, National Nagasaki Medical Center, Nagasaki, Japan. METHODS: Eighteen eyes from 15 patients after laser iridotomy (17 eyes) or peripheral iridectomy (1 eye) had undergone surgery and were studied. We used an iris retractor in 7 eyes due to insufficient mydriasis and a capsular tension ring in 2 eyes due to phacodonesis during the operation. The patients were followed up for at least 6 months (13.8 +/- 7.2 months; range: 6-36 months). RESULTS: The mean IOP significantly decreased from 17.4 +/- 8.1 to 13.5 +/- 3.3 mm Hg at 6 months after surgery. The IOP was below 21 mm Hg in all eyes. The visual acuity was not worsened in any eyes and became better than

cataract.title: Capsulorhexis in white cataracts.
The impact of cataract severity on measurement acquisition with the IOLMaster.
cataract.summary: The IOLMaster fails to acquire axial length measurement in approximately 20% of UK public hospital cataract patients. Failure is principally due to PSC, whereby the LOCS III score of p=3.5 defines the limit of PSC severity that the IOLMaster can measure.
cataract.abstract: PURPOSE: The Zeiss IOLMaster optical biometry system provides superior prediction of refractive outcome of cataract surgery compared to applanation ultrasound. However, measurement is not always possible in the presence of dense cataract. The purpose of this study was to elucidate the rate of measurement acquisition failure due to cataract and how this varies with morphology and severity. METHODS: A total of 149 subjects were prospectively enrolled and visual acuity, Lens Opacities Classification System III (LOCS III) scores, ultrasonic A-scan and IOLMaster axial lengths were measured. Chi-squared analysis was used to test the null hypothesis that cataract severity has no effect on measurement failure rate. cataract.title: Phacotrabeculectomy with mitomycin C in patients with uveitis.
cataract.summary: With adequate inflammation suppression, phacotrabeculectomy with mitomycin C is an effective and safe therapeutic option for the management of secondary cataract and glaucoma in uveitic eyes. A lower surgical success rate of the uveitic group might be attributable to the postoperative inflammation recurrence.
cataract.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of combined phacoemulsification, intraocular lens implantation, and trabeculectomy with mitomycin C for the management of uveitic complications. DESIGN: Retrospective case-control study. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective review of the records of 23 consecutive eyes with chronic noninfectious uveitis (uveitic group) and 43 nonuveitic eyes (control group) that had received primary phacotrabeculectomy. Mitomycin C was used in all the uveitic eyes. Considering the high preoperative intraocular pressure (IOP) of the uveitic group, nonuveitic eyes that had a preoperative IOP of >or=20 mm Hg or that had been given two or more medications were included in the control group. All patients were followed for at least one year. The main outcome measures were postoperative vision, IOP control, complications, and acute uveitis relapse rates. RESULTS: Vis

cataract.title: Two year results: sharp versus rounded optic edges on silicone lenses.
cataract.summary: To evaluate the role of optic edge design of 2 silicone intraocular lenses (IOLs) in 2 year clinical results. Department of Ophthalmology, University of Vienna, Medical School, Allgemeines Krankenhaus, Austria. …
cataract.abstract: To evaluate the role of optic edge design of 2 silicone intraocular lenses (IOLs) in 2 year clinical results. Department of Ophthalmology, University of Vienna, Medical School, Allgemeines Krankenhaus, Austria. In this comparative clinical study, 50 eyes had phacoemulsification and implantation of a high-refractive 3-piece silicone IOL with sharp optic edges (CeeOn model 911F) (n = 25) or a 3-piece silicone lens with rounded optic edges (CeeOn model 920) (n = 25). Biomicroscopic findings, including those of specular microscopic examination of the anterior lens surface, were documented and the results analyzed. After 2 years, a significant between-group difference in posterior capsule opacification (PCO) but not in anterior capsule alterations was observed. cataract.title: Cataract surgery combined with ocular surface reconstruction in patients with severe cicatricial keratoconjunctivitis.
cataract.summary: Small-incision phacoemulsification was performed safely in combination with ocular surface reconstruction in patients with cataract and end-stage cicatricial keratoconjunctivitis.
cataract.abstract: PURPOSE: To present the technique and outcome of cataract surgery combined with ocular surface reconstruction in patients with severe cicatricial keratoconjunctivitis. SETTING: Department of Ophthalmology, Tokyo Dental College, Chiba, Japan. METHODS: Phacoemulsification with transplantation of a limbal allograft and an amniotic membrane was performed in 4 eyes of 3 patients with cataract and end-stage cicatricial keratoconjunctivitis. The surgical technique and the improvements in visual acuity were reviewed. The follow-up ranged from 13 to 27 months. RESULTS: Phacoemulsification and intraocular lens implantation were performed in all cases without intraoperative complications. In 3 of the 4 eyes, the best corrected visual acuity improved from hand motions to 20/100, hand motions to 20/30, and counting fingers to 20/50. The visual acuity recovered to 20/60 postoperatively in 1 eye in whi

cataract.title: [Sutureless phacotrabeculectomy. Interim results].
cataract.summary: No-stitch phacotrabeculectomy appears to be a safe and (medium-term) effective procedure for combined surgery of cataract and glaucoma.
cataract.abstract: BACKGROUND: To study the medium-term success rate of a simple surgical technique for combined operation of cataract and glaucoma. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Of 50 patients with cataract and various types of glaucoma, 55 eyes underwent a combined operation for cataract and glaucoma and were followed up for at least 6.5 months. The phacoemulsification war performed through a scleral tunnel. After implantation of a foldable IOL an "inverse T" incision of the tunnel floor was performed to create a valve mechanism closure. RESULTS: In 45 eyes (83%) the intraocular pressure was controlled without medications during the follow-up time. In 10 cases (17%) a new glaucoma medication was introduced postoperatively. cataract.title: Phacoemulsification of white mature cataracts.
cataract.summary: If a CCC can be achieved, the results of white cataract phacoemulsification are comparable to those of routine cataract surgery. When using the two-stage technique, one should be prepared to deal with a hard cataract through a small capsulorhexis.
cataract.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the intraoperative difficulties associated with phacoemulsification of white mature cataracts and develop a strategy for consistently achieving continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis (CCC) in these cases. SETTING: Raghudeep Eye Clinic, Iladevi Cataract & IOL Research Centre, Ahmedabad, India. METHODS: This prospective study comprised 60 eyes of 60 patients with senile white mature cataract. Mean follow-up was 7 months. Detailed preoperative and intraoperative notes were made including intraoperative subjective assessment of the intracapsular pressure and cataract hardness. A small capsulorhexis was attempted initially. Endophacoemulsification was performed using the stop, chop, chop, and stuff technique. The capsulorhexis was enlarged before intraocular lens implantation. An initial cut in the capsulorhexis margin was made with a cystotome needle while a spatula suppor

cataract.title: Surgical techniques for difficult cataracts.
cataract.summary: This article reviews some of the advances that have taken place in the surgical techniques for difficult cataracts such as rock-hard, white, and posterior polar cataracts. Fashioning a central space, modified chopping maneuvers, and creation of multiple small fragments have enabled the surgeon to consistently achieve a successful outcome. …
cataract.abstract: This article reviews some of the advances that have taken place in the surgical techniques for difficult cataracts such as rock-hard, white, and posterior polar cataracts. Fashioning a central space, modified chopping maneuvers, and creation of multiple small fragments have enabled the surgeon to consistently achieve a successful outcome. A judicious combination of chop and separation movement in a step-by-step manner reduce the stress of the procedure and make it safer. Raised intracapsular pressure and poor visibility are dealt with through various innovative techniques. Use of high-viscosity sodium hyaluronate and double capsulorhexis allow the surgeon to achieve capsulorhexis with a high success rate. A controlled and gentle approach to phacoemulsification has proven to be the key factor for success in posterior polar cataracts.

cataract.title: Effect of phacoemulsification surgery on hypotony following trabeculectomy surgery.
cataract.summary: Phacoemulsification surgery may be associated with a statistically significant elevation in IOP in previously filtered eyes with hypotony, resulting in resolution of hypotony in some of these challenging cases. Arch Ophthalmol. 2000;118:763-765
cataract.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To review the effect of phacoemulsification surgery in eyes with chronic hypotony following trabeculectomy with mitomycin C. DESIGN: Retrospective analysis of all eyes that underwent phacoemulsification surgery for symptomatic cataracts and had a preoperative diagnosis of chronic hypotony (intraocular pressure [IOP] </=6 mm Hg) for at least 6 months following trabeculectomy with mitomycin C. Each case had at least 6 months' follow-up after the phacoemulsification surgery. SETTING: A tertiary care referral center. INTERVENTION: Clear cornea phacoemulsification surgery, with minimal perioperative anti-inflammatory medication and retention of viscoelastic in eyes at case conclusion. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Intraocular pressure, visual acuity, and complications. RESULTS: Nine eyes of 9 patients were identified. cataract.title: Technique and outcome of combined phacoemulsification and trabeculectomy.
cataract.summary: The efficacy of combined surgery for the treatment of concurrent glaucoma and cataract has long been under scrutiny. Comparisons between sequential surgery and combined procedures have shown mixed results, and current guidelines have been drawn for the indication of combined surgery. …
cataract.abstract: The efficacy of combined surgery for the treatment of concurrent glaucoma and cataract has long been under scrutiny. Comparisons between sequential surgery and combined procedures have shown mixed results, and current guidelines have been drawn for the indication of combined surgery. The evolution of combined triple surgery--cataract extraction, intraocular lens implantation, and filtering procedure--has evolved from planned extracapsular cataract extraction to small-incision phacoemulsification. The improvements of phacoemulsification over extracapsular surgery have naturally given rise to improvements in the results of combined procedures; good outcomes in both intraocular pressure control and visual acuity have been reported along with low complication rates. cataract.title: [Cataracts - trend and new developments].
cataract.summary: Cataract is the leading cause of blindness or severe visual handicap worldwide (20 Million people). The majority of cataracts are age-dependent. The only known treatment so far is surgery, which therefore has become the most frequent performed surgery in all industrialized countries. …
cataract.abstract: Cataract is the leading cause of blindness or severe visual handicap worldwide (20 Million people). The majority of cataracts are age-dependent. The only known treatment so far is surgery, which therefore has become the most frequent performed surgery in all industrialized countries. Indication for cataract surgery is when the vision falls below patients requirements. Today's surgical technique is phacoemulsification of the nucleus and implantation of a foldable intraocular lens via a small (< 3 mm) self-sealing incision. The majority of patients undergoes the surgery under topical anaesthesia and as outpatient procedure. Major complication are rare (< 1 %), may however lead to permanent visual disability (< 1 per thousand). New developments are nowadays mainly in the design and additional features of the artificial lens i.e. blueblocker, multifocal and toric lenses.

cataract.title: Phacoemulsification versus combined phacotrabeculectomy in medically uncontrolled chronic angle closure glaucoma with cataracts.
cataract.summary: Combined phacotrabeculectomy with adjunctive mitomycin C is more effective than phacoemulsification alone in controlling IOP in medically uncontrolled CACG eyes with coexisting cataract. Combined phacotrabeculectomy is associated with more postoperative complications.
cataract.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare phacoemulsification alone versus combined phacotrabeculectomy in medically uncontrolled chronic angle closure glaucoma (CACG) with coexisting cataract. DESIGN: Prospective randomized clinical trial. PARTICIPANTS: Fifty-one medically uncontrolled CACG eyes with coexisting cataract of 51 patients. INTERVENTION: Recruited patients were randomized into group 1 (phacoemulsification alone) or group 2 (combined phacotrabeculectomy with adjunctive mitomycin C). Postoperatively, patients were reviewed every 3 months for 2 years. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Intraocular pressure (IOP) and requirement for topical glaucoma drugs. RESULTS: Twenty-seven CACG eyes were randomized into group 1, and 24 CACG eyes were randomized into group 2. Combined phacotrabeculectomy resulted in lower mean postoperative IOP than phacoemulsification alone at 3 months (14.0 vs. 17.0 mmHg, P = 0.01), 15 m

cataract.title: Cool phaco--new option in cataract surgery.
cataract.summary: Phacoemulsification performed through two paracenteses can be the next step in cataract surgery development.
cataract.abstract: PURPOSE: The aim of this paper is to present an alternative method of phacoemulsification. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Bimanual phacoemulsification through two paracenteses was performed in 15 eyes. After cataract removal intraocular lenses were implanted into the capsular bag through a small paracentesis (less than 2 mm). RESULTS: Anatomical and functional results were good in all cases. After comparison with conventional phacoemulsification we concluded, that the bimanual technique shortens the time of ultrasounds usage and reduces postoperative astigmatism. CONCLUSIONS: Phacoemulsification performed through two paracenteses can be the next step in cataract surgery development.

cataract.title: Deep lamellar keratoplasty combined with cataract surgery.
cataract.summary: We used a surgical technique that combines deep lamellar keratoplasty, phacoemulsification, and intraocular lens implantation for treating patients with cataract and corneal stromal disease. …
cataract.abstract: We used a surgical technique that combines deep lamellar keratoplasty, phacoemulsification, and intraocular lens implantation for treating patients with cataract and corneal stromal disease. Deep lamellar dissection of the cornea was first performed with viscoelastic substances (hyaluronate sodium) until the highly transparent Descemet membrane solely remained. We then created a short corneal tunnel to perform phacoemulsification with low vacuum and intraocular lens implantation. The resilience of the Descemet membrane ensured excellent viewing of the whole anterior chamber as well as the surgical conditions of a closed system. At the end of surgery, a full-thickness donor button was sutured into the recipient bed after its Descemet membrane was stripped. This technique was effective in these 4 patients with cataract and dense corneal opacity.

cataract.title: A phacovitrectomy with a clear corneal incision for a full-thickness macular hole.
cataract.summary: Combining cataract surgery with vitrectomy can achieve visual rehabilitation in the early postoperative period without requiring post-vitrectomy cataract surgery. A sutureless clear corneal incision, used in this procedure, can minimize the SIA and promote postoperative wound healing. …
cataract.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the results of a pars plana vitrectomy, combined with phacoemulsification, using a sutureless, superotemporal, clear corneal incision for patients with a macular hole. METHODS: This study reviewed the records of 22 patients (22 eyes) who underwent a phacoemulsification with the insertion of an acrylic intraocular lens, using a 3.2 mm superotemporal clear corneal incision and a pars plana vitrectomy with an internal limiting membrane peeling in one session, for the treatment of a macular hole. RESULTS: All 22 patients had their macular holes closed using the combined surgical procedures. The mean preoperative visual acuity was 0.086, and the mean postoperative visual acuity was 0.173. This improvement was statistically significant (paired Student's t-test, p < 0.05). No patients developed posterior capsular opacity, retinal detachment, or a cystoid macular edema. The

cataract.title: Correction of astigmatism at the time of cataract surgery.
cataract.summary: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: There are several options for correcting astigmatism at the time of cataract surgery. They include incision placement on the steep axis of corneal astigmatism, single or paired peripheral corneal relaxing incisions, and toric intraocular lens implantation. …
cataract.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: There are several options for correcting astigmatism at the time of cataract surgery. They include incision placement on the steep axis of corneal astigmatism, single or paired peripheral corneal relaxing incisions, and toric intraocular lens implantation. The aim of this review is to update readers on advances reported during the last year. RECENT FINDINGS: Phacoemulsification incision placement on the steep corneal axis corrects small amounts of astigmatism and is sufficient for most eyes. Peripheral corneal relaxing incisions correct greater amounts of astigmatism. They may be necessary when implanting multifocal intraocular lenses in eyes with more than 1 diopter of astigmatism. Toric intraocular lenses are also safe and effective for treating more than 1 diopter of astigmatism, and they now have excellent rotational stability. SUMMARY: Good uncorrected postoperati

cataract.title: [Phacoemulsification combined with cyclophotocoagulation].
cataract.summary: The combination of cyclophotocoagulation and phacoemulsification is as successful as other combinations of cataract and glaucoma surgery with a similar or lower complication rates. Cyclophotocoagulation is cost efficient, can be repeated and is adaptable to the intraocular pressure.
cataract.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cyclophotocoagulation and phacoemulsification procedures may be combined to treat patients with glaucoma and cataract. cataract.abstract: The design and use of materials in the nanoscale size range for addressing medical and health-related issues continues to receive increasing interest. Research in nanomedicine spans a multitude of areas, including drug delivery, vaccine development, antibacterial, diagnosis and imaging tools, wearable devices, implants, high-throughput screening platforms, etc. using biological, nonbiological, biomimetic, or hybrid materials. Many of these developments are starting to be translated into viable clinical products. Here, we provide an overview of recent developments in nanomedicine and highlight the current challenges and upcoming opportunities for the field and translation to the clinic.

cataract.abstract: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is an inherited retinal dystrophy caused by the loss of photoreceptors and characterized by retinal pigment deposits visible on fundus examination. Prevalence of non syndromic RP is approximately 1/4,000. The most common form of RP is a rod-cone dystrophy, in which the first symptom is night blindness, followed by the progressive loss in the peripheral visual field in daylight, and eventually leading to blindness after several decades. Some extreme cases may have a rapid evolution over two decades or a slow progression that never leads to blindness. In some cases, the clinical presentation is a cone-rod dystrophy, in which the decrease in visual acuity predominates over the visual field loss. cataract.abstract: Corneal wound healing is a complex process involving cell death, migration, proliferation, differentiation, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Many similarities are observed in the healing processes of corneal epithelial, stromal and endothelial cells, as well as cell-specific differences. Corneal epithelial healing largely depends on limbal stem cells and remodeling of the basement membrane. During stromal healing, keratocytes get transformed to motile and contractile myofibroblasts largely due to activation of transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) system. Endothelial cells heal mostly by migration and spreading, with cell proliferation playing a secondary role. In the last decade, many aspects of wound healing process in different parts of the cornea have been elucidated, and some new therapeutic approaches have emerged. cataract.abstract: Summary Candida parapsilosis is an emerging major human pathogen that has dramatically increased in significance and prevalence over the past 2 decades, such that C. parapsilosis is now one of the leading causes of invasive candidal disease. Individuals at the highest risk for severe infection include neonates and patients in intensive care units. C. parapsilosis infections are especially associated with hyperalimentation solutions, prosthetic devices, and indwelling catheters, as well as the nosocomial spread of disease through the hands of health care workers. Factors involved in disease pathogenesis include the secretion of hydrolytic enzymes, adhesion to prosthetics, and biofilm formation. cataract.abstract: Scedosporium spp. are increasingly recognized as causes of resistant life-threatening infections in immunocompromised patients. Scedosporium spp. also cause a wide spectrum of conditions, including mycetoma, saprobic involvement and colonization of the airways, sinopulmonary infections, extrapulmonary localized infections, and disseminated infections. Invasive scedosporium infections are also associated with central nervous infection following near-drowning accidents. The most common sites of infection are the lungs, sinuses, bones, joints, eyes, and brain. Scedosporium apiospermum and Scedosporium prolificans are the two principal medically important species of this genus. These findings support the value of careful macular OCT assessment for identifying early glaucomatous structural damage.
glaucoma.abstract: PRCIS: Based upon a real-world data set, the prevalence of subtle glaucoma-like defects in the macula is underestimated. PURPOSE: To understand the prevalence and characteristics of glaucoma-like defects in a large real-world data set using optical coherence tomography (OCT) and an OCT-based Reading Center (OCT-RC) approach. METHODS: OCT scans were analyzed from 6184 individuals tested at optometric sites involved in refractive care. Based on commercial widefield OCT reports, foveal B-scans, and a previously published OCT-RC method, 361 individuals had evidence of optic neuropathy consistent with glaucoma in 1 or both eyes [ON-G (RC)]. Using the Columbia University (CU) OCT method, 2 experienced graders also labeled eyes as "ON-G (CU)" and "Not ON-G (CU)," based only upon the OCT report. glaucoma.title: Clinical and ocular factors associated with visual field progression following optic disc haemorrhage in glaucoma.
glaucoma.summary: Recurrent DH, longer axial length, thinner CCT, and greater IOP fluctuation were independently associated with VF progression following optic DH. These factors may help identify glaucomatous eyes at higher risk of progression and support closer clinical monitoring after the initial detection of DH.
glaucoma.abstract: BACKGROUND: To investigate the structural and clinical factors linked to visual field (VF) progression in glaucomatous eyes after the initial detection of optic disc haemorrhage (DH) in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). METHODS: This study included 92 eyes of 92 patients who presented with at least one optic DH on stereoscopic optic disc and red-free photography. The included patients had a minimum follow-up of 3 years after initial detection of DH and at least 5 reliable standard automated perimetry investigations. VF progression was assessed using event-based guided progression analysis (GPA). Baseline demographic, clinical, and ocular parameters were examined using Cox proportional hazards regression to identify the independent predictors of functional deterioration. glaucoma.title: Axon Content of the Circumpapillary Nerve Fiber Layer in Experimental Glaucoma.
glaucoma.summary: The axon size distribution and non-axonal area in the circumpapillary RNFL are similar between healthy and stable glaucomatous eyes. Building on this, a location-specific model is proposed that estimates axon content from the circumpapillary RNFL profile after accounting for regional variability in axonal and non-axonal components.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine axonal content from optical coherence tomography (OCT)-derived circumpapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) measures using histologically informed models in a non-human primate experimental glaucoma model. METHODS: Unilateral experimental glaucoma was induced in 22 animals (mean age, 6.1 ± 1.9 years; 10 females) who were monitored with OCT. At varying stages of neuropathy, animals were euthanized and perfusion fixed. For RNFL histology, circumpapillary tissue (∼0.75 × 0.75 mm) from six equally spaced regions was obtained and processed for serial block face scanning electron microscopy in five animals. A single high-resolution image of the block face was used to quantify axon size (cross-sectional area) and non-axonal tissue area within the RNFL. Using the 95% limits of the histological data as a starting point, models for estimating axon count from OCT RNFL area

glaucoma.title: Suprachoroidal hemorrhage and detachment in the non-laser photocoagulation posterior pole after intravitreal Anti-VEGF injection: A case report.
glaucoma.summary: Intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections are widely used for diabetic macular edema (DME) and neovascular ocular diseases. Suprachoroidal hemorrhage and detachment (SCHD) in the posterior pole non-laser photocoagulation area is an extremely rare complication after anti-VEGF injection, with no standardize …
glaucoma.abstract: Intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections are widely used for diabetic macular edema (DME) and neovascular ocular diseases. Suprachoroidal hemorrhage and detachment (SCHD) in the posterior pole non-laser photocoagulation area is an extremely rare complication after anti-VEGF injection, with no standardized management. We report a 56-year-old male with a 20-year history of type 2 diabetes, bilateral proliferative diabetic retinopathy (DR), neovascular glaucoma (NVG), and prior pars plana vitrectomy who developed SCHD in the right eye after intravitreal Conbercept injection. He was treated with retrobulbar triamcinolone acetonide injection. During follow-up, SCHD resolved completely with significant improvement in best-corrected visual acuity and stable intraocular pressure. glaucoma.title: Combined vitrectomy/glaucoma drainage device with posteriorly placed tubes compared to anterior chamber placed tubes in children.
glaucoma.summary: In children with glaucoma, concurrent Vit/GDD placement with posterior placement of the tube and aged-matched controls who underwent conventional anterior chamber GDD placement both obtained IOP control at final follow-up. Further, there was no difference in survival rates between the two groups.
glaucoma.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Compare combined vitrectomy/posterior tube placement in children to age-matched controls who underwent conventional anterior chamber glaucoma drainage device (GDD) placement. METHODS: Retrospective review of children (< 18 years of age) with at least 1-year of post-operative follow-up who underwent combined vitrectomy/GDD placement (Vit/GDD) between 2010 and 2024 and age-matched controls who had conventional anterior chamber GDD placement. Demographics, ocular diagnoses and surgeries, and exam findings were collected. Main outcome measures were BCVA, IOP, and glaucoma medications, success and survival of GDD (IOP 5-21 mmHg, no additional IOP-lowering surgeries, and no visually devastating complications). RESULTS: Children in the Vit/GDD (n = 45) and control (n = 73) groups showed no difference in age at surgery, GDD-type implanted, or follow-up length. The Vit/GDD group underw

glaucoma.title: Combined endoscope-assisted procedures (CEaP) for the management of neovascular glaucoma.
glaucoma.summary: This combined surgical technique appears safe and effective and may represent a promising early interventional strategy for NVG, significantly reducing IOP and treatment burden in a high-risk patient population.
glaucoma.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neovascular glaucoma (NVG) is a severe and vision-threatening form of secondary glaucoma characterized by both retinal ischemia and elevated intraocular pressure (IOP). Effective management requires simultaneous control of the ischemic stimulus and IOP. However conventional cyclodestructive techniques are associated with significant risks including severe inflammation, hypotony and phthisis bulbi. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a combined surgical approach-endoscopic cyclophotocoagulation (ECP), pars plana vitrectomy (PPV), and panretinal photocoagulation (PRP)-for treating neovascular glaucoma (NVG). METHODS: This retrospective, non-comparative interventional case series included 30 eyes from 30 patients treated at a tertiary referral care center in France. glaucoma.title: Efficacy and safety of XEN63 gel implant with open conjunctiva technique.
glaucoma.summary: Open-conjunctiva XEN63 Gel Stent implantation resulted in significant reductions in IOP and medication burden during a short-term follow-up, with a favorable safety profile and low postoperative intervention rates, in both stand-alone and combined procedures.
glaucoma.abstract: BACKGROUND: The XEN Gel Stent implantation using the traditional technique has demonstrated good efficacy and an acceptable safety profile. However, it is associated with intensive postoperative management due to high bleb needling and revision rates. The aim of this study is to assess the efficacy and safety of XEN63 Gel Stent implantation using a open-conjunctiva technique. METHODS: A multicentre retrospective chart review of consecutive patients who underwent XEN63 implantation using an open conjunctiva technique between 2023 and 2024 in the two University Eye centers was conducted. Only patients with at least 12 months of follow-up were included. Patient demographics, preoperative and postoperative clinical data were collected. Study variables were analyzed using Student's t-test and Mann-Whitney U test. All tests were two-tailed, and statistical significance was defined for p < 0.05

glaucoma.title: Defining the optimal duration of remote home tonometry for accurate characterization of intraocular pressure fluctuation.
glaucoma.summary: Remote tonometry provides clinically meaningful characterization of IOP metrics beyond traditional office-based measurements. Depending on the clinical context, seven to ten consecutive monitoring days consisting of measurements across each day are needed to represent a patient's true IOP pattern.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine the minimal duration of remote intraocular pressure (IOP) monitoring needed to yield accurate IOP fluctuation metrics in patients. DESIGN: Secondary modeling analysis of retrospective data, validated with a large national database. PARTICIPANTS: 397 patients from the Moran Eye Center and/or Wilmer Eye Institute and 1,579 patients from a MyEyes CorporationTM database who utilized an iCare HOME/HOME2 tonometer and recorded ≥3 measurements throughout each day over several consecutive days. METHODS: Bootstrapped progressive day-censorship analyses and exponential decay modeling were used to estimate the number of monitoring days required to achieve 95% of the maximal model-based reduction in error for IOP metrics, including mean, maximum, range, and standard deviation (SD). glaucoma.title: Feasibility and Early Outcomes of Gonioscopy-Assisted Transluminal Trabeculotomy for Neovascular Glaucoma.
glaucoma.summary: This retrospective observational case series evaluates the clinical outcomes of gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy (GATT) in 6 consecutive eyes with neovascular glaucoma (NVG) treated at a tertiary referral center. …
glaucoma.abstract: This retrospective observational case series evaluates the clinical outcomes of gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy (GATT) in 6 consecutive eyes with neovascular glaucoma (NVG) treated at a tertiary referral center. NVG was defined as secondary glaucoma associated with retinal ischemia, characterized by elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) and prior presence of iris and/or angle neovascularization. All patients had previously undergone pan-retinal photocoagulation and intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy and were receiving maximally tolerated medical treatment at presentation. Circumferential GATT was successfully completed in all cases. At final follow-up, IOP control was achieved in 3 eyes with topical therapy, while the remaining 3 eyes required subsequent Ahmed glaucoma valve implantation due to early surgical failure. glaucoma.title: Outcomes of the Paul Glaucoma Implant for Refractory Glaucoma in an Indonesian Population.
glaucoma.summary: The Paul Glaucoma Implant demonstrated favorable short- to mid-term outcomes, with substantial reductions in intraocular pressure and glaucoma medication use and a low rate of postoperative hypotony.
glaucoma.abstract: PRECIS: The Paul Glaucoma Implant demonstrated favorable short- to mid-term outcomes in patients with refractory glaucoma in the Indonesian population. Low rates of postoperative hypotony following implantation were observed with the use of intraluminal 6/0 prolene stent. PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of the Paul Glaucoma Implant in managing refractory glaucoma in the Indonesian population. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed patients who underwent implantation of the Paul Glaucoma Implant at the Kedoya and Menteng branches of the Jakarta Eye Center between September 2022 and January 2025. RESULTS: 121 implantations from 113 patients were included, with a median follow-up of 12.00 (12.00 - 24.00) months. glaucoma.title: Evaluation of Bruch's membrane opening minimum rim width and retinal nerve fiber layer in patients with glaucoma and comparison with normal population.
glaucoma.summary: BMO-MRW is a reliable and effective parameter for the early diagnosis of glaucoma, showing consistent global and sectoral diagnostic performance compared with APS-RNFL.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess and compare the diagnostic performance of Bruch's membrane opening-minimum rim width (BMO-MRW) and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness parameters in patients with early-stage glaucoma. MATERIAL AND METHOD: This observational cross-sectional study included 60 eyes with primary open-angle glaucoma, 44 eyes with ocular hypertension (OHT), and 41 healthy control eyes. One eye per participant was randomly selected. All subjects underwent comprehensive ophthalmologic evaluation, including Goldmann applanation tonometry, gonioscopy, standard automated perimetry, spectral-domain optical coherence tomography, and dilated fundus examination. Global and sectoral RNFL thickness measurements, including standard and Anatomical Positioning System-based RNFL (APS-RNFL), as well as BMO-MRW parameters, were obtained using the Glaucoma Module Premium Edition (GMPE). glaucoma.title: Seasonal intraocular pressure variation in patients with primary open-angle or exfoliation glaucoma: a bidirectional encoder representations from transformers -based natural language processing analysis.
glaucoma.summary: Intraocular pressure is higher in winter, regardless of glaucoma subtype or filtration surgery status. Filtration surgery lowers baseline intraocular pressure but does not eliminate season-related physiological influences.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: Seasonal variations in intraocular pressure (IOP) are reported in glaucoma, but differences between subtypes and the influence of filtration surgery remain unclear. This study examined seasonal IOP patterns in primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and exfoliation glaucoma (EXG) using electronic medical records analyzed with a Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT)-based natural language processing system. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective observational study. METHODS: We analyzed 1,679 visits from 352 patients (238 with POAG and 114 with EXG) at a Japanese university hospital between August 2020 and May 2023. Clinical parameters were extracted from electronic medical records using a validated BERT-based natural language processing model. glaucoma.title: Pediatric Endothelial Keratoplasty: A Modified Delphi Consensus by the EKLG Study Group on Indications, Surgical Techniques, and Postoperative Care.
glaucoma.summary: The consensus statements provide globally endorsed recommendations for the clinical management of pediatric EK. These guidelines are relevant for corneal specialists providing a practical framework to benchmark practice, reduce variability, and guide future multicenter investigations.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To identify areas of consensus among global experts on the clinical management of pediatric endothelial keratoplasty (EK), including patient selection, timing, preoperative evaluation, technique selection, intraoperative standards, and postoperative care, and to provide a practical framework for surgeons earlier in their pediatric EK learning curve. DESIGN: Modified Delphi-based global consensus study. PARTICIPANTS: International ophthalmologists with expertise in endothelial keratoplasty and pediatric corneal diseases. METHODS: A series of consensus statements on pediatric EK were developed from iterative rounds of structured questions and statements posed to a panel of experts. Two rounds of asynchronous electronic questionnaires were followed by a structured hybrid discussion of unresolved items. glaucoma.summary: A 7-year-old boy presented with progressive visual decline. On examination, visual acuity was no light perception in the left eye and 20/60 in the right eye. Examination showed bilateral microcornea, marked corneal flattening, shallow anterior chambers, abnormal iris configuration, and elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in both eyes. …
glaucoma.abstract: A 7-year-old boy presented with progressive visual decline. On examination, visual acuity was no light perception in the left eye and 20/60 in the right eye. Examination showed bilateral microcornea, marked corneal flattening, shallow anterior chambers, abnormal iris configuration, and elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in both eyes. The right eye had a slit-like pupil of 1 mm, and the left eye showed a closed pupil with very shallow anterior chamber and superior intercalary staphyloma. Keratometry values were significantly reduced, suggestive of cornea plana, which was subsequently confirmed by identification of a homozygous intronic variant in the KERA gene. These findings suggested pupillary block as the primary mechanism of glaucoma due to a functionally imperforate pupil. glaucoma.title: Bilateral same-day glaucoma surgery: a single-centre review of safety and outcomes of bilateral same-day minimally invasive glaucoma surgeries.
glaucoma.summary: this is the first study to report safety outcomes of BSDGS using MIGS procedures. The intervention appears safe and effective relative to both unilateral MIGS and immediately sequential bilateral cataract surgery.
glaucoma.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To report the efficacy and safety of bilateral same-day glaucoma surgery (BSDGS), specifically with minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) procedures. DESIGN: Single university centre longitudinal, consecutive case series. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 63 patients (126 eyes) were included. METHODS: This study reviewed all patients undergoing BSDGS between February 2022 and February 2025 at a university hospital in Montreal, Quebec. MIGS procedures included iStent trabecular microbypass, Hydrus Microstent, and bent ab interno needle goniotomy. All surgeries were performed by a single glaucoma specialist. Inclusion criteria included (i) bilateral glaucoma, (ii) need for intraocular pressure (IOP) or medication reduction, and (iii) minimum 1 month follow-up. glaucoma.title: Electrophysiological Changes Before and After Glaucoma Filtration Surgery in the Mid-Postoperative Period: A Retrospective Study.
glaucoma.summary: Introduction Changes in retinal function during the first days after glaucoma filtration surgery have been documented with electroretinography (ERG), but little is known about later time points, particularly in eyes operated on without concurrent cataract surgery and in eyes that develop choroidal detachment (CD). …
glaucoma.abstract: Introduction Changes in retinal function during the first days after glaucoma filtration surgery have been documented with electroretinography (ERG), but little is known about later time points, particularly in eyes operated on without concurrent cataract surgery and in eyes that develop choroidal detachment (CD). We examined ERG parameters before and after filtration surgery performed alone and explored, as a hypothesis-generating analysis, whether the responses differed between eyes with and without postoperative CD. Methods Thirty-two eyes of 32 patients who underwent filtration surgery alone at Chiba University Hospital were reviewed retrospectively. glaucoma.title: The 1-2-3 Rule: When to "Consider" Glaucoma Surgery and Discuss It With Patients.
glaucoma.summary: Earlier intervention is gaining momentum in glaucoma care, yet delayed referral and delayed consideration of surgery remain concerns in clinical practice. A simple clinical rule may help general ophthalmologists recognize when to discuss procedural options with patients. …
glaucoma.abstract: Earlier intervention is gaining momentum in glaucoma care, yet delayed referral and delayed consideration of surgery remain concerns in clinical practice. A simple clinical rule may help general ophthalmologists recognize when to discuss procedural options with patients. We propose the Shimane University 1-2-3 rule (SU1-2-3), comprising three prompts: intraocular pressure (IOP) >12 mmHg in progressive advanced glaucoma, with advanced glaucoma defined for this rule as visual field mean deviation ≤ -10 dB or glaucomatous visual field defects within the central 10°; IOP >20 mmHg despite topical treatment in perimetric glaucoma; or use of ≥3 bottles of IOP-lowering eye drops. Oral acetazolamide use is an additional, independent prompt. glaucoma.title: Glaucoma neurodegeneration: targeted modulation of intraocular immune pathways - a review of novel therapeutic advances.
glaucoma.summary: Glaucoma is the leading global cause of irreversible blindness, with its pathogenesis extending far beyond elevated intraocular pressure. Dysregulation of the intraocular immune system plays a central role in the progressive death of retinal ganglion cells. …
glaucoma.abstract: Glaucoma is the leading global cause of irreversible blindness, with its pathogenesis extending far beyond elevated intraocular pressure. Dysregulation of the intraocular immune system plays a central role in the progressive death of retinal ganglion cells. This review systematically examines the research progress on key intraocular immune pathways in glaucomatous neurodegeneration, with a primary focus on immune-inflammatory responses mediated by microglia, astrocytes, and T cells. It delves into the molecular mechanisms of various immunoregulatory networks, including the TLR4/nuclear factor kappa B (TLR4/NF-κB), Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), complement, and T-cell receptor signaling pathways. glaucoma.title: Compatibility of 24-2C central extra test points with OCT and OCTA parameters in early-stage glaucoma.
glaucoma.summary: It is known that specific regions of the macula may be sensitive to early-stage glaucomatous damage. This suggests that in early-stage glaucoma, attention should be paid to central points in addition to peripheral findings on VF. …
glaucoma.abstract: AIM: To facilitate structure-function analysis by evaluating the compatibility of newly added 10 extra test points in early-stage glaucoma cases with optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT-angiography (OCTA) glaucoma parameters in clinical practice. METHODS: Cases diagnosed with primary open angle glaucoma underwent Humphrey 24-2C visual field (VF) test, OCT, and OCTA tests on the same day. The arithmetic average of the central 10 extra points in the 24-2C VF was calculated, and its compatibility with OCT and OCTA parameters was assessed. Patients with low signal strength OCT and OCTA images, high fixation losses in VF, intraocular pressure of 25 mm Hg and above, systemic vascular diseases [diabetes mellitus (DM), hypertension (HT)] were excluded from the study. glaucoma.title: Transcriptomic profiling of normal and glaucomatous trabecular meshwork cells in a tissue-like soft ECM environment.
glaucoma.summary: These data define a transcriptomic signature of glaucomatous TM cells when cultured in a soft physiologic ECM microenvironment, independent of the originating laboratory, with three mechanistic axes (ECM/fibrosis, inflammation, hypoxia/metabolism), and nominate p300 (encoded by EP300) as a candidate upstream node integrating these program …
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: Trabecular meshwork (TM) dysfunction contributes to the elevated intraocular pressure in primary open-angle glaucoma. To better understand the "molecular signature" distinguishing glaucomatous from normal TM cells, we interrogated their genome-wide transcriptomic differences in a tissue-like soft extracellular matrix (ECM) microenvironment. METHODS: Primary human glaucomatous and normal TM cell strains (N = 5 each) from three independent laboratories were plated on bioengineered collagen type I/hyaluronic acid/elastin-like polypeptide ECM hydrogels in 10% FBS media for 4-5 days, then serum-free media for 2 days. glaucoma.title: Ultrasound cycloplasty: dynamic efficacy and long-term safety in glaucoma patients from northwest China.
glaucoma.summary: 1. In glaucoma patients in the Northwest population, UCP demonstrates significant long-term and dynamic efficacy-the higher the baseline IOP, the more pronounced the IOP-lowering effect, with outstanding performance in stabilizing IOP fluctuations. 2. UCP exhibits acceptable safety and controllable complications. …
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To comprehensively evaluate the dynamic efficacy of UCP in treating different types of glaucoma patients in Northwest China, systematically analyze treatment outcome variations across follow-up time points, and assess long-term safety profiles. METHODS: In a 1-year follow-up study, 24 patients (30 eyes) with various types of glaucoma were enrolled and underwent UCP treatment (10 sectors or 8 sectors). Follow-up visits were conducted at different postoperative time points (1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year). Follow-up assessments consisted of IOP measurements, IOP reduction from baseline, surgical success rate, 24-hour IOP fluctuation, pain score improvement, and complications. glaucoma.title: Congenital fibrovascular pupillary membrane with secondary glaucoma and associated fundus anomalies: a case report and literature review.
glaucoma.summary: We report a clinically rare case of CFPM-induced secondary glaucoma, with concurrent fundus anomalies. Comprehensive ophthalmic evaluation is essential for CFPM patients, with attention to the possibility of posterior segment involvement. …
glaucoma.abstract: BACKGROUND: Congenital fibrovascular pupillary membrane (CFPM) is a rare unilateral congenital anterior segment dysplasia, mainly characterized by the presence of fibrous vascular membrane-like tissue in the pupil area. This membrane can obstruct the pupil, impede aqueous humor circulation, and progress to severe secondary glaucoma. This report describes a rare case of CFPM-induced secondary glaucoma coexisting with fundus anomalies. CASE PRESENTATION: A 5-month-old female infant presented with right eye photophobia and epiphora, which had developed 20 days prior. Ophthalmological examination revealed the following: right eye intraocular pressure (IOP) 27.4 mmHg, corneal opacity and enlargement, near-complete absence of the anterior chamber, occluded pupillary membrane, and other intraocular structures were not visible. glaucoma.summary: In patients undergoing Susanna GDD implantation, adjunctive sub-Tenon triamcinolone provided no additional IOP-lowering benefit but was associated with a significantly increased risk of serious hypotony-related complications. …
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of Adjunct Triamcinolone (TA) with the Susanna drainage device for refractory primary open-angle glaucoma, to our knowledge, the first such evaluation with a non-valved glaucoma drainage device. METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind (patient and outcome assessor) trial included 39 eyes with refractory primary open-angle glaucoma, divided into a control (n = 20) and a triamcinolone group (n = 19). glaucoma.title: Interocular Asymmetry in Normal-Tension Glaucoma: Risk Factors for Unilateral Disease and Asymmetric Progression.
glaucoma.summary: Larger optic disc area and higher baseline IOP are associated with unilateral manifestation in NTG. Disc hemorrhage and less negative SE are correlated with high-risk progression in bilateral NTG.
glaucoma.abstract: PRCIS: This prospective cohort identifies clinical features linked to unilateral presentation and different progression risk in NTG. PURPOSE: This study aimed to identify determinants of asymmetric progression in bilateral normal-tension glaucoma (NTG) and compare interocular differences in patients with unilateral NTG. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This prospective cohort study enrolled 119 patients with NTG (238 eyes), including 48 bilateral (96 eyes) and 71 unilateral cases (142 eyes). Using a stratified grouping approach, eyes in the unilateral NTG group were categorized as affected eyes versus contralateral unaffected eyes based on diagnostic criteria. For the bilateral NTG group, eyes were stratified into high- and low-risk progression subgroups according to visual‑field progression rates. Interocular differences within each patient were compared. glaucoma.title: Development of a Corneal Biomechanical Risk Score for Visual Field Progression in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma.
glaucoma.summary: This internally validated, exploratory risk score based on four corneal biomechanical parameters stratified POAG patients by risk of VF progression. Further validation is needed to determine its clinical utility.
glaucoma.abstract: PRECIS: This study developed and internally validated an exploratory risk score model based on four Corvis-ST parameters to predict visual field progression in POAG. The model demonstrated acceptable predictive and risk-stratification performance. PURPOSE: To develop a risk score model based on corneal biomechanical properties for predicting visual field (VF) progression in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). METHODS: This prospective clinical cohort study included POAG patients with a follow-up period exceeding 18 months and at least six reliable visual field examinations. glaucoma.title: Endothelin 2-Mediated Neuroinflammation Drives Hypertensive Retinal Dysfunction.
glaucoma.summary: Our findings establish endothelin 2 as an important, intraocular pressure-independent contributing factor to hypertension-associated retinal neurodegeneration and identify the endothelin-endothelin receptor type A axis as a potential therapeutic target to prevent vision loss in patients with hypertension.
glaucoma.abstract: BACKGROUND: Systemic hypertension is a risk factor for glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, yet the mechanistic basis connecting the 2 conditions remains elusive. METHODS: A longitudinal assessment of blood pressure, intraocular pressure, retinal function, structure, and perfusion was conducted in spontaneously hypertensive rats and Wistar-Kyoto rats. Transcriptomic analyses and immunofluorescence staining were performed to investigate hypertension-associated retinal biochemical changes. AAV-mediated knockdown of endothelin 2 was used to investigate its mechanistic role. glaucoma.title: Modified Three-port Approach for Absolute Alcohol-induced Sclerosis of Iris Stromal Cyst: A Case Report.
glaucoma.summary: Iris stromal cysts are rare, progressive ocular lesions that can cause visual impairment and amblyopia due to visual axis obstruction, corneal endothelial damage, uveitis, and secondary angle-closure glaucoma. …
glaucoma.abstract: Iris stromal cysts are rare, progressive ocular lesions that can cause visual impairment and amblyopia due to visual axis obstruction, corneal endothelial damage, uveitis, and secondary angle-closure glaucoma. Management is challenging due to recurrence, and surgical resection carries severe risks such as epithelial downgrowth, glaucoma, blindness, and potential loss of the eye. glaucoma.abstract: Glaucoma is an irreversible progressive optic neuropathy, for which the major proven treatment is to lower the intraocular pressure (IOP). Five groups of IOP-lowering eye drops have varying mechanisms of action. Some drops, such as β-blockers and α-2 agonists, have potentially serious systemic side effects. Acetazolamide is the only available oral agent; it is effective at lowering IOP, but significant side effects relegate its use usually to refractory glaucoma. Two new eye drops, netarsudil and latanoprostene bunod, have recently been approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration. Both have novel IOP-lowering mechanisms and target the conventional aqueous outflow system. Selective laser trabeculoplasty is a gentle treatment that enhances conventional aqueous outflow. glaucoma.abstract: The goal of all glaucoma surgery is to lower eye pressure to prevent or reduce damage to the optic nerve. Standard glaucoma surgeries - trabeculectomy, ExPRESS shunts and external tube-shunts like the Ahmed and Baerveldt valves - are major surgeries. While they are very often effective at lowering eye pressure and preventing progression of glaucoma, they have a long list of potential complications. Minimal invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) is a group of operations that have been developed in recent years to reduce some of the complications of most standard glaucoma surgeries. MIGS procedures work by using microscopic-sized equipment and tiny incisions. The purpose of this study is to review the available MIGS currently in use, their benefits and limitations.

The mechanism by which SLT lowers IOP is not completely understood and is likely multifactorial. Published studies indicate that SLT is at least as effective as argon laser trabeculoplasty or medications at lowering IOP in many forms of glaucoma. glaucoma.abstract: Glaucoma is one of the most frequent causes of blindness in the world. Although there are several different subforms of glaucoma, their final common pathway is an atrophy of the optic disc leading to progressive visual field defects and finally total blindness. The loss of function in glaucoma is irreversible, i.e. early detection of the disease is the most important part of its therapy. Early detection, however, requires improved knowledge about the disease in the general population and the active help of all general practitioners, explaining their patients the insidious nature of the disease.

glaucoma.abstract: Glaucoma is a potentially blinding condition that cannot be easily defined. There are various types of glaucoma which may vary in symptoms from none at all to sudden pain and redness. There is a characteristic optic neuropathy, or damage to the optic nerve, which results in progressive loss of visual field. The most important risk factor is an increase in the intraocular pressure (IOP) secondary to a reduction in the drainage of aqueous fluid from the drainage pathways in the eye, the filtration angle (Kanski 2007, Allingham et al 2011).

glaucoma.abstract: The childhood glaucomas represent of variety of glaucoma subtypes that can cause serious and permanent visual damage. Early detection and treatment of infantile glaucoma is essential to preserve vision. The clinical signs and symptoms of infantile glaucoma are recognizable by nonophthalmologists but may be confused with other common clinical entities. Surgical and occasionally medical interventions can control raised intraocular pressure and thus prevent permanent glaucoma damage to the eye. Amblyopia is a common reason for permanent visual loss in this disease and needs to be treated aggressively as well.

glaucoma.abstract: Acute glaucoma crisis is an emergency in ophthalmology. Ocular and systemic clinical signs are typical and due to a paroxystic and severe increase of intraocular pressure. It is a biometric disease: little eye with a big lens. Main factors triggering the acute crisis are: stress, sympathicomimetics, parasympathicomimetics and parasympathicolytics drugs. Treatment is surgical: iridectomy, cataract extraction, trabeculectomy or combined surgery.

Nine blebs had typical clinical features of blebs after trabeculectomy with adjunctive MMC. We conclude that long-term-stored MMC may be beneficial as adjunctive treatment in initial trabeculectomy in this population.

In the 56 eyes where 5-fluorouracil was not used, the mean intraocular pressure (IOP) on diagnosis was 33.4 mmHg, the mean pre-operative IOP being 25.1 mmHg. glaucoma.abstract: Glaucoma represents a major cause of vision loss throughout the world. Primary open-angle glaucoma, the most common form of glaucoma, is a chronic, progressive disease often, though not always, accompanied by elevated intraocular pressure (IOP). In this disorder, retinal ganglion cell loss and excavation of the optic nerve head produce characteristic peripheral visual field deficits. Patients with normal-tension glaucoma present with typical visual field and optic nerve head changes, without a documented history of elevated IOP. A variety of secondary causes, such as pigment dispersion syndrome and ocular trauma, can result in glaucoma as well. Treatment of all forms of glaucoma consists of reducing IOP. This review was undertaken to address frequently raised issues pertinent to SLT in clinical practice. On the basis of the peer-reviewed medical literature, SLT demonstrates equivalent efficacy and comparable safety to argon laser trabeculoplasty, and is also equally as effective as topical medical therapy. SLT's safety profile includes mild and transient inflammation, ocular pain, and a small risk of moderate IOP elevations after the procedure. The mechanism of action of SLT is not known. glaucoma.abstract: A technique called optical coherence tomography (OCT) has been developed for noninvasive cross-sectional imaging in biological systems. OCT uses low-coherence interferometry to produce a two-dimensional image of optical scattering from internal tissue microstructures in a way that is analogous to ultrasonic pulse-echo imaging. OCT has longitudinal and lateral spatial resolutions of a few micrometers and can detect reflected signals as small as approximately 10(-10) of the incident optical power. Tomographic imaging is demonstrated in vitro in the peripapillary area of the retina and in the coronary artery, two clinically relevant examples that are representative of transparent and turbid media, respectively.

glaucoma.summary: Prostaglandins are lipid autacoids derived from arachidonic acid. They both sustain homeostatic functions and mediate pathogenic mechanisms, including the inflammatory response. …
glaucoma.abstract: Prostaglandins are lipid autacoids derived from arachidonic acid. They both sustain homeostatic functions and mediate pathogenic mechanisms, including the inflammatory response. They are generated from arachidonate by the action of cyclooxygenase isoenzymes, and their biosynthesis is blocked by nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs, including those selective for inhibition of cyclooxygenase-2. Despite the clinical efficacy of nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs, prostaglandins may function in both the promotion and resolution of inflammation. This review summarizes insights into the mechanisms of prostaglandin generation and the roles of individual mediators and their receptors in modulating the inflammatory response. Prostaglandin biology has potential clinical relevance for atherosclerosis, the response to vascular injury and aortic aneurysm.

retina.abstract: Wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD), a leading cause of irreversible vision loss, is driven by pathological choroidal neovascularization (CNV). Although anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapies remain the clinical standard, their utility is constrained by incomplete responses in nearly 50% of patients and off-target risks-such as geographic atrophy-stemming from non-specific VEGF blockade. Here, we identify a robust correlation between vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1) and VEGF/VEGF receptor (VEGFR) expression in aqueous humor from AMD patients and in murine CNV models. Thus, we engineered a tetravalent bispecific protein, RHV, by functionalizing an L-rhamnulose-1-phosphate aldolase scaffold with peptides that selectively bind VCAM-1 and the VEGFR on neovessels. The tetravalent design confers high apparent affinity, enhancing pathological endothelial

retina.title: Secondary Glaucoma Incidence Following Ischemic Retinal Disease and Anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Utilization.
retina.summary: The later era was associated with lower incidence of secondary glaucoma following ischemic retinal disease, concurrent with increased anti-vascular endothelial growth factor utilization and declining laser use. …
retina.abstract: PRECIS: This large real-world cohort study demonstrates reduced one-year secondary glaucoma incidence following ischemic retinal disease in the later anti-VEGF era, alongside increased anti-VEGF utilization and declining panretinal photocoagulation use. PURPOSE: Compare one-year incidence of secondary glaucoma following ischemic retinal disease between early and later anti-vascular endothelial growth factor treatment eras. METHODS: In this retrospective study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, adults with proliferative diabetic retinopathy, central retinal vein occlusion, or branch retinal vein occlusion were categorized into an early (2010-2014) or later (2015-2024) anti-vascular endothelial growth factor era based on index diagnosis date. retina.title: Three-Year Real-World Outcomes of Switching to Brolucizumab for Refractory Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
retina.summary: Switching to brolucizumab provided maintained visual and anatomical improvements with extended treatment intervals over 3 years. The safety profile was consistent with previous reports, and IOI events were manageable in a real-world setting.
retina.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the three-year long-term efficacy, treatment durability, and safety of switching to brolucizumab in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) who were refractory to previous anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents in a real-world setting. METHODS: This retrospective study included nAMD patients who switched to brolucizumab between July 2021 and November 2022. Clinical outcomes were evaluated based on changes in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), central macular thickness (CMT), and the presence of retinal fluid, as well as changes in annual injection frequency and treatment intervals. Safety outcomes, including intraocular inflammation (IOI), were also assessed. RESULTS: A total of 123 patients were initially reviewed. retina.title: Prognostic value of OCT biomarkers and systemic factors for early and long term anatomical treatment response in diabetic macular edema.
retina.summary: Baseline OCT biomarkers showed candidate associations with anatomical response, but several, including the hyperreflective-material association, were not reproduced when the outcome was redefined using continuous final CMT or an absolute CMT threshold, despite robustness within the primary model. …
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate the prognostic value of baseline optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarkers and systemic factors for early and long-term anatomical response to anti-VEGF therapy in diabetic macular edema (DME). METHODS: This retrospective study included 164 eyes from 105 patients with type 2 diabetes and DME who received three monthly loading doses of intravitreal bevacizumab (January 2013 to April 2024) and were subsequently managed with a pro re nata (PRN) regimen using standard retreatment criteria. Completion of the loading phase (minimum follow-up, 3 months) was required for inclusion. Anatomical response was assessed after the loading phase (early response) and at final follow-up (long-term response); eyes were classified as full, partial, or non-responders based on CMT and OCT morphology. retina.title: Suprachoroidal hemorrhage and detachment in the non-laser photocoagulation posterior pole after intravitreal Anti-VEGF injection: A case report.
retina.summary: Intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections are widely used for diabetic macular edema (DME) and neovascular ocular diseases. Suprachoroidal hemorrhage and detachment (SCHD) in the posterior pole non-laser photocoagulation area is an extremely rare complication after anti-VEGF injection, with no standardize …
retina.abstract: Intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections are widely used for diabetic macular edema (DME) and neovascular ocular diseases. Suprachoroidal hemorrhage and detachment (SCHD) in the posterior pole non-laser photocoagulation area is an extremely rare complication after anti-VEGF injection, with no standardized management. We report a 56-year-old male with a 20-year history of type 2 diabetes, bilateral proliferative diabetic retinopathy (DR), neovascular glaucoma (NVG), and prior pars plana vitrectomy who developed SCHD in the right eye after intravitreal Conbercept injection. He was treated with retrobulbar triamcinolone acetonide injection. During follow-up, SCHD resolved completely with significant improvement in best-corrected visual acuity and stable intraocular pressure. Pathogenesis may involve low intraocular pressure, anti-VEGF-related vascular effe

retina.title: Baseline Optical Coherence Tomography Features and Visual Outcomes After Anti-vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Therapy for Retinal Vein Occlusion-Associated Macular Edema: A Prospective Observational Study.
retina.summary: Background Macular edema is a major cause of visual loss in retinal vein occlusion (RVO). Although anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy reduces retinal thickening, visual recovery varies. …
retina.abstract: Background Macular edema is a major cause of visual loss in retinal vein occlusion (RVO). Although anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy reduces retinal thickening, visual recovery varies. The primary objective was to assess whether baseline optical coherence tomography (OCT) features were associated with visual acuity one month after the third anti-VEGF injection using a prespecified 6/18 threshold. Secondary objectives assessed demographic and clinical associations, while central macular thickness (CMT) reduction was evaluated exploratorily. Methodology This prospective observational study included 60 eyes of 60 patients with center-involving, RVO-associated macular edema treated between September 2022 and February 2024. Each eye received three intravitreal anti-VEGF injections, with assessment one month after each injection. A good outcome was defined as final vi

retina.title: Real-World Outcomes with Aflibercept 8 mg in Patients with Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration (nAMD) or Diabetic Macular Edema (DME) - Retrospective Single-Center Data Analysis.
retina.summary: The findings suggest that aflibercept 8 mg provides effective disease control with maintained visual outcomes and significant anatomical improvements in women and men with nAMD and DME, including a predominantly previously treated population, in routine clinical practice. …
retina.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This work aims to evaluate real-world functional and anatomical outcomes following intravitreal aflibercept 8 mg in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) and diabetic macular edema (DME) treated under routine clinical conditions. We assessed functional and anatomical outcomes, treatment intervals, and subgroup effects by prior treatment status and sex over 12 months. METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, non-interventional study included adult patients with nAMD or DME treated with aflibercept 8 mg in routine clinical practice between February 2024 and May 2026. Primary outcomes were changes in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA; logMAR) and central subfield retinal thickness (CST; µm) from baseline to 3-, 6-, and 12-month follow-up. Secondary analyses included subgroup comparisons according to treatment status (treatment-naïve vs. pretreat

retina.title: Outcomes of Diabetic Macular Edema After Switching From Faricimab-svoa to High-dose Aflibercept.
retina.summary: Anatomic and visual changes were not significant following switch to aflibercept 8 mg. Sustained injection interval improvements were present at the final aflibercept 8 mg injection.
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of high-dose aflibercept 8 mg in the treatment of diabetic macular edema (DME) refractory to faricimab-svoa treatment. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 82 eyes from 64 patients with DME previously treated with faricimab-svoa. Injection intervals, corrected or pinhole visual acuity (VA), and central foveal thickness (CFT) were recorded. RESULTS: Between the time of switch to the fifth injection, the average (SD) injection interval increased from 63 (45) days to 69 (23) days (P = .01). Mean VA decreased from 58.1 (23.1) to 52.9 (22.7) letters (P = .263), and average CFT decreased from 360 (145) µm to 348 (151) µm (P = .626). Intraretinal fluid incidence decreased from 50% to 33.3% (P = .066), while subretinal fluid incidence increased from 6.1% to 14.8% (P = .308). CONCLUSION: Anatomic a

retina.title: Submacular Hemorrhage Requiring Procedural Intervention During Anti-VEGF Therapy for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Japan: The JTY Three-Center Real-World Incidence Study.
retina.summary: SMH requiring procedural intervention during anti-VEGF therapy for nAMD was uncommon but visually severe; among affected eyes, PCV accounted for 72.2% of events. Exploratory drug-specific analyses did not demonstrate significant adjusted differences among anti-VEGF agents. …
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To estimate the incidence and clinical characteristics of submacular hemorrhage (SMH) requiring procedural intervention during anti-VEGF therapy for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) in a Japanese multicenter real-world setting, with exploratory comparison according to the preceding anti-VEGF agent. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective real-world incidence study reviewed surgical records from three Japanese centers to identify SMH requiring gas injection or vitrectomy during ongoing anti-VEGF treatment. The denominator was the total number of anti-VEGF injections for nAMD during the same period. Incidence per 1,000 injections and site-adjusted incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were estimated using quasi-Poisson regression. RESULTS: Among 47,358 injections, 54 SMH events requiring procedural intervention were identified (1.14 per 1,000 injections). Median final BC

retina.title: Impact of different treatment regimens on long-term prognosis in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy: a systematic review.
retina.summary: Anti-VEGF therapy and PRP may provide broadly comparable long-term visual acuity outcomes in selected PDR patients, though important differences exist in treatment burden, visual field preservation, and complication profiles. …
retina.abstract: AIM: To evaluate the long-term prognostic outcomes associated with different treatment regimens for PDR, including panretinal photocoagulation (PRP), anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy, vitrectomy, and combination approaches. METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from database inception through March 31, 2024, with manual supplementary screening extended to June 30, 2024. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and comparative observational studies that directly evaluated at least two treatment regimens with a minimum follow-up of 1y were included in the principal therapeutic synthesis; imaging, screening, epidemiologic, and disease-characterization studies were retained as contextual evidence.
