retina.title: Early outcomes of switching from bevacizumab to aflibercept-jbvf in exudative macular diseases: a real-world study.
retina.summary: Administration of aflibercept-jbvf following three monthly bevacizumab injections was temporally associated with a statistically significant but modest very early reduction in CST at 4 weeks in this heterogeneous cohort of exudative macular diseases. …
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate very early anatomical and functional outcomes following a switch from intravitreal bevacizumab to aflibercept-jbvf in patients with exudative macular diseases. METHODS: This prospective, single-center, single-arm interventional cohort study included 53 eyes of 41 patients with diabetic macular edema (DME), macular neovascularization (MNV) secondary to neovascular age-related macular degeneration, or retinal vein occlusion (RVO). This heterogeneous cohort comprised biologically distinct disease entities; therefore, diagnosis-specific analyses were considered exploratory. All eyes received three monthly intravitreal bevacizumab injections followed by a single aflibercept-jbvf injection. Primary outcomes were changes in BCVA and CST from the post-bevacizumab preswitch baseline, assessed immediately before aflibercept-jbvf administration, to 4 weeks after the injection.

retina.title: Microglia-targeted delivery of MCC950 suppresses NLRP3-IL-18-mediated neuroinflammation and retinal injury in retinal vein occlusion.
retina.summary: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) causes retinal ischemia, macular edema, and vision loss, yet current anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapies primarily limit vascular leakage and leave ischemia-driven neuroinflammation insufficiently controlled. …
retina.abstract: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) causes retinal ischemia, macular edema, and vision loss, yet current anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapies primarily limit vascular leakage and leave ischemia-driven neuroinflammation insufficiently controlled. Here, we reveal a critical role for microglia-associated NLRP3-IL-18 signaling in amplifying inflammation during early RVO. Bulk retinal RNA sequencing showed broad innate immune activation, whereas single-cell transcriptomic profiling and spatial protein analysis identified prominent inflammasome-related changes in retinal microglia. Constitutive global deletion of Nlrp3 or Il18 attenuated microglial activation and preserved retinal structure and electrophysiological function. To translate this mechanistic insight into a targeted anti-inflammatory strategy, we engineered MG1-functionalized, MCC950-loaded nanoliposomes for micro

retina.title: Occult Optic Disk Pit Maculopathy Masquerading as Exudative Age-Related Macular Degeneration in an Elderly Patient: A Case Report.
retina.summary: Occult ODPM can closely mimic exudative AMD and may go unrecognized for many months in elderly patients with coexisting retinal disease, resulting in repeated unnecessary anti-VEGF treatment.
retina.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Occult optic disk pit maculopathy (ODPM) is a rare cause of macular retinoschisis in which no pit is visible on funduscopic examination. Optic disk pits are congenital cavitary anomalies thought to arise from incomplete closure of the embryonic fissure during ocular development. CASE PRESENTATION: This report presents an 83-year-old woman with a history of exudative AMD of the left eye (OS) and low-tension glaucoma having received 11 intravitreal anti-VEGF injections over approximately 18 months without resolution of macular fluid. Fluorescein angiography demonstrated no macular leakage and no macular neovascularization. Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography revealed multilayered peripapillary retinoschisis with fluid extending from the optic disk to the fovea. Dedicated optic disk OCT confirmed a deep crater-like excavation consistent with an occult optic disk pit.

retina.title: Impact of Anti-VEGF treatment on retinal anatomy and electrophysiological function in diabetic macular edema.
retina.summary: Intravitreal bevacizumab therapy in treatment-naive DME patients produced significant anatomical improvement, accompanied by changes in selected electrophysiological parameters. …
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: The objective of this study is to evaluate changes in the foveal avascular zone (FAZ), vascular density (VD), and electrophysiological parameters in patients with diabetic macular edema (DME) following intravitreal bevacizumab therapy. METHODS: The study comprised 27 eyes of 22 patients with treatment-naive DME who received a loading phase of three consecutive monthly intravitreal bevacizumab injections, together with 30 eyes of 15 healthy controls. All participants underwent optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography (OCTA), pattern electroretinography (PERG) and visual evoked potentials (VEP) at baseline and at one and three months. As both eyes of some participants were included, all comparisons used generalized estimating equations clustered on subject, with cluster-robust variance estimation. retina.title: Time Course of Resolution of Diabetic Macular Edema by Sustained Suppression of VEGF-A with the Port Delivery Platform with Ranibizumab.
retina.summary: Sustained suppression of VEGF-A is sufficient to effectively treat DME in the vast majority of patients, but edema resolution may be slow in some patients giving the false impression of poor response to anti-VEGF-A treatment. In DME, the term unresponsive to anti-VEGF-A treatment should be replaced by slowly responsive.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine the incidence of poor responsiveness to VEGF-A suppression in eyes with diabetic macular edema (DME) by evaluating the effect of continuous delivery of ranibizumab via the Port Delivery Platform with ranibizumab (PDS) in individual patients enrolled in the Pagoda clinical trial. DESIGN: Retrospective analysis of prospective clinical trial data SUBJECTS: DME patients enrolled in Pagoda (NCT04108156). METHODS: Change in central subfield thickness (CST) and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) over time was evaluated for the adjusted intent-to-treat (aITT) population in the Pagoda trial. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) images obtained at each visit were analyzed for 56 PDS subjects from 8 sites to determine the time course of changes in intraretinal and subretinal fluid. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: CST, BCVA, and time to resolution of edema. RESULTS: In the aITT populatio

retina.title: Bridging Mechanism and Therapy in Ocular Disease: Mitochondrial, Vascular, and Immune Pathways in the Eye.
retina.summary: There is an increasing global burden of ocular disorders, with an estimated 43.3 million people worldwide currently blind and a further 295 million living with moderate-to-severe vision impairment, driven by a complex pathogenesis that involves multiple cascade failures ranging from mitochondrial dysfunction to chronic neuroinflammation a …
retina.abstract: There is an increasing global burden of ocular disorders, with an estimated 43.3 million people worldwide currently blind and a further 295 million living with moderate-to-severe vision impairment, driven by a complex pathogenesis that involves multiple cascade failures ranging from mitochondrial dysfunction to chronic neuroinflammation and blood-retinal barrier breakdown. This narrative review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature identified through targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, prioritizing publications from the last five years and supplemented by foundational studies where necessary, to examine molecular mechanisms underlying both anterior and posterior segment pathologies, including Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD), diabetic macular edema (DME), age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and antibody-mediated optic neuritis. retina.title: Generative Forecasting of Longitudinal 3D-OCT Under Anti-VEGF Therapy for Diabetic Macular Edema.
retina.summary: Background/Objectives: Forecasting the individual anatomical response to anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy from optical coherence tomography (OCT) could support the management of diabetic retinal disease. …
retina.abstract: Background/Objectives: Forecasting the individual anatomical response to anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy from optical coherence tomography (OCT) could support the management of diabetic retinal disease. Direct volumetric generation is difficult because treatment-associated change is local while most of the retina is stationary, so generative models regress to the mean and blur retinal layers. Methods: We propose a two-stage framework that decouples baseline anatomy from longitudinal change in 3D-OCT. A Retinal Response Tokenizer compresses the latent residual between baseline and follow-up volumes into discrete action tokens via Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ), and a conditional decoder renders the follow-up volume from baseline features and these tokens. retina.title: Changes in expression of DNA-methyltransferase in neovascular age-related macular degeneration: Anti-VEGF response or disease severity?
retina.summary: We hereby report varying DNMTs expression in nAMD patients with different disease manifestations giving new insights into the dynamic nature of epigenetic modifications in response to anti-VEGF treatment.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: Recent studies suggest distinct patterns of DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) expression across different stages of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). However, whether these variations can be modulated by conventional therapeutic approaches remains unexplored. This study investigates DNMT expression dynamics in two patients with exudative neovascular AMD (nAMD) during the initial months of anti-VEGF treatment. OBSERVATIONS: Case 1, a female in her 90s was seen for sudden loss of vision secondary to macular hemorrhage. retina.title: Longitudinal Quantitative Analysis of Ultra-Widefield Fluorescein Angiography Leakage Metrics: Analysis of the KINGFISHER Clinical Trial.
retina.summary: Both brolucizumab and aflibercept substantially reduced UWF-FA leakage in DME over 52 weeks. Brolucizumab achieved a more pronounced early reduction in leakage within the posterior pole, although the final residual leakage at week 52 was comparable between the 2 agents.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To longitudinally quantify changes in retinal vascular leakage in diabetic macular edema (DME) using ultra-widefield fluorescein angiography (UWF-FA) in patients receiving brolucizumab versus aflibercept. DESIGN: Retrospective post hoc analysis of the phase 3, randomized, masked KINGFISHER clinical trial. SUBJECTS: Eyes with center-involved DME enrolled in KINGFISHER with gradable late-phase UWF-FA images at baseline and follow-up (week 24 and/or week 52). METHODS: Two independent masked graders manually assessed late-phase UWF-FA images at baseline, week 24, and week 52 using OptosAdvance software. retina.title: Noninfectious intraocular inflammation with hypopyon after intravitreal aflibercept 8 mg injection for neovascular age-related macular degeneration: a case report.
retina.summary: Noninfectious IOI with hypopyon may occur after an intravitreal aflibercept 8 mg injection. Even when hypopyon is present after an anti-vascular endothelial growth factor injection, noninfectious IOI should be included as a differential diagnosis in addition to infectious IOI.
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: Herein, we report a case of noninfectious intraocular inflammation (IOI) with hypopyon after an intravitreal aflibercept 8 mg injection for neovascular age-related macular degeneration. CASE PRESENTATION: An 87-year-old Japanese man with neovascular age-related macular degeneration in the right eye was switched from intravitreal aflibercept 2 mg to aflibercept 8 mg to extend the treatment interval. Three days after the third aflibercept 8 mg injection, the patient presented with decreased vision without ocular pain. Slit-lamp examination revealed mild conjunctival injection and anterior chamber cells. Despite treatment with topical corticosteroids, the inflammation worsened the following day, with increased anterior chamber cells accompanied by a highly mobile hypopyon that shifted with head position. retina.title: Outcomes of Intravitreal Anti-VEGF Therapy for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Kazakhstan.
retina.summary: In this real-world cohort, anti-VEGF therapy was associated with significant anatomical improvement, as measured by CRT reduction, while functional outcomes were characterised by visual stabilisation rather than substantial gains.
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss among older adults. Although randomised controlled trials have demonstrated the robust efficacy of intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy, real-world outcomes often differ markedly from trial findings. This study aimed to evaluate the anatomical and functional outcomes of anti-VEGF therapy in a clinical cohort of nAMD patients, including a subgroup that received adjunctive rescue photodynamic therapy (PDT) with verteporfin. METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective observational cohort study included 568 patients (634 eyes) with nAMD treated with intravitreal anti-VEGF injections. Bevacizumab was used in 49% of eyes, ranibizumab in 44%, and aflibercept in 7%. Best recorded visual acuity (BRVA) and central retinal thickness (CRT) measured by opt

retina.title: Temporal, Phenotypic, and Treatment-Context Heterogeneity in Retinal Vasculitis Reporting with Pegcetacoplan: A United States Pharmacovigilance Study.
retina.summary: Background/Objectives: Pegcetacoplan slows geographic atrophy (GA) progression, but postmarketing retinal vasculitis remains an important safety concern. We evaluated whether retinal vasculitis reporting changed over time, whether the reported phenotype changed with respect to occlusive coding, and whether vasculitis was associated with i …
retina.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pegcetacoplan slows geographic atrophy (GA) progression, but postmarketing retinal vasculitis remains an important safety concern. We evaluated whether retinal vasculitis reporting changed over time, whether the reported phenotype changed with respect to occlusive coding, and whether vasculitis was associated with identifiable treatment contexts. Methods: We analyzed the United States (US) Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) data from 17 February 2023 through 31 December 2025. Strict retinal vasculitis reports required pegcetacoplan to be coded as the primary-suspect drug. Faricimab was used as a descriptive contemporaneous intravitreal comparator because US exposure estimates could be constructed over the same period; it was not treated as a safety-neutral control. Separately, within all US primary-suspect Syfovre reports, we examin

retina.title: AI-Based OCT Assessment of Anatomic Response During the Loading Phase of Anti-VEGF Therapy in Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
retina.summary: All agents improved functional and anatomic outcomes after the loading phase in treatment-naive nAMD. Baseline-adjusted analyses showed differences in anatomic response patterns across treatments. Exploratory AI-based OCT biomarkers may help characterize short-term anatomic response; however, these findings require external validation.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare functional and anatomic outcomes after the loading phase of intravitreal bevacizumab, aflibercept 2 mg, or faricimab in treatment-naive neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), using artificial intelligence (AI)-based optical coherence tomography (OCT) analysis. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 224 eyes. Patients received three monthly injections of bevacizumab (n = 80), aflibercept 2 mg (n = 78), or faricimab (n = 66). Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and spectral-domain OCT were assessed at baseline and week 12. AI-based segmentation quantified volumetric measurements of intraretinal fluid (IRFv), subretinal fluid (SRFv), and pigment epithelial detachment. The primary outcome was qualitative dry macula (absence of intraretinal fluid and subretinal fluid). An exploratory composite OCT biomarker (ΔCOMBO), defined as the less

retina.title: Outcomes of subthreshold diode micropulse laser and anti-VEGF vs anti-VEGF monotherapy for diabetic macular edema: a meta-analysis.
retina.summary: In patients with DME, SDMLP and anti-VEGF combination therapy appears comparable, and possibly modestly superior to anti-VEGF monotherapy, with a reduced injection burden over 12 months. BCVA and CMT differences were below clinically important thresholds and supported by low-certainty evidence.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare visual and anatomic outcomes in patients with diabetic macular edema treated with subthreshold diode micropulse laser photocoagulation (SDMLP) and anti-VEGF combination therapy versus anti-VEGF injection monotherapy. DESIGN: Meta-analysis. METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library between January 2005 and April 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies comparing best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and central macular thickness (CMT) after SDMLP and anti-VEGF combination therapy versus anti-VEGF monotherapy. The primary outcome was change in BCVA (∆BCVA). Secondary outcomes included absolute BCVA and CMT at all time points, change in CMT (∆CMT) from baseline to all time points, and the number of anti-VEGF injections over 12 months. Outcomes were reported as a weighted mean difference (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

retina.title: The potential of ruxolitinib as a senomorphic therapy in alleviating neovascular age-related macular degeneration : Ruxolitinib inhibits CNV.
retina.summary: Our study identifies the JAK1/2-STAT3 pathway as a key regulator of the SASP in senescent RPE and confirms its activation in nAMD and experimental CNV. Pharmacologic inhibition of this pathway with ruxolitinib effectively attenuates CNV progression with a favorable short-term safety profile, supporting its potential as a senomorphic thera …
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cellular senescence plays a key role in the pathogenesis of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). Senomorphic therapy, which targets the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), holds promise for treating age-related diseases; however, effective senomorphic treatments for nAMD remain lacking. METHODS: We screened a panel of senomorphic agents in bleomycin- and ionizing radiation (IR)-induced senescent ARPE-19 cells to identify a lead compound for nAMD. Bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data were analyzed to explore JAK-STAT signaling activation. Ruxolitinib and siRNA were used to validate the role of the JAK1/2-STAT3 pathway in senescent retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). retina.title: Development full-thickness macular hole and exudative retinal detachment in central retinal vein occlusion after intravitreal ranibizumab.
retina.summary: Although vitrectomy combined with removal of the inner limiting membrane can reclose macular hole caused by intravitreal injection of anti-VEGF drugs, these cases of FTMH differ from those of idiopathic FTMH in having a poorer visual prognosis. …
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravitreal injection of anti‑vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) has become a first-line treatment for macular oedema secondary to central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO). However, there have been recent reports of a surprising complication associated with intravitreal injection of anti-VEGF. We report a case of full-thickness macular hole (FTMH) and exudative retinal detachment (ERD) after intravitreal injection of ranibizumab for macular oedema. CASE PRESENTATION: A 21-year-old patient with macular oedema secondary to CRVO developed FTMH and ERD in her left eye after the first intravitreal injection of ranibizumab. A 25 G vitrectomy was performed, during which the internal limiting membrane was peeled off followed by filling with silicone oil tamponade. One week after the operation, optical coherence tomography showed closure of the macular hole. CONCLUSION: Although

retina.title: Choroidal structural changes following intravitreal injection of faricimab or aflibercept 8 mg in neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
retina.summary: Aflibercept 8 mg was associated with reduced overall choroidal thickness, whereas faricimab was associated with reduced luminal choroidal proportion. These findings may indicate differences in choroidal structural changes between the two agents during the first three injections, although further studies with larger sample sizes are needed …
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare choroidal structural changes following the initial three injections of faricimab or high-dose (8 mg) aflibercept in eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). METHODS: This retrospective study included 38 eyes (comprising both treatment-naïve and switch cases) that received three consecutive intravitreal injections of either faricimab (n = 24) or aflibercept 8 mg (n = 14). Subfoveal choroidal area was manually segmented on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography and binarized using Niblack's method. The evaluated parameters were central choroidal thickness (CCT) and the luminal-to-choroidal area ratio (L/C ratio). RESULTS: CCT significantly decreased in the aflibercept 8 mg group (P < 0.001), whereas the faricimab group showed no significant post-hoc pairwise differences. Conversely, faricimab was associated with a significant longitudinal red

retina.title: Recalcitrant Diabetic Macular Edema Case Report despite Anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Therapy during Pregnancy.
retina.summary: This report presents a severe case of DME that was recalcitrant to treatment with anti-VEGF treatment during pregnancy. The fetal loss is likely attributable to underlying medical conditions, including poorly controlled diabetes, hypertension, and congestive heart failure exacerbations requiring hospitalizations, rather than IVB. …
retina.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy is often the first-line treatment for diabetic macular edema (DME), but during pregnancy, focal laser photocoagulation is often preferred. We aim to report a case of anti-VEGF use during pregnancy for DME. CASE PRESENTATION: A 37-year-old pregnant female with a history of insulin-dependent, poorly controlled diabetes mellitus and proliferative diabetic retinopathy with macular edema presented with decreased vision. She had previously undergone focal laser therapy, but due to the appearance of symptomatic scotomas, had declined further focal laser treatment. Despite receiving intravitreal bevacizumab (IVB) injections, the patient's DME worsened during pregnancy. retina.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of preventable blindness in adults of working age. Anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy is the reference standard for diabetic macular edema (DME), yet in randomized cohorts, approximately 30-40% of DME eyes still show central macular thickening after six months of continuous treatment. In proliferative DR (PDR), the corresponding limitation is recurrence after treatment interruption rather than primary non-response, and these two patterns should not be conflated. This review examines translational research in DR across four domains. retina.title: Mapping the methodological framework of diabetic retinopathy interventional trials: a scoping review on trial design, execution, and reporting practices.
retina.summary: This review represents the first comprehensive assessment of current DR clinical research, exposing key design weaknesses in existing trials. Future meta-analyses and systematic evaluations, informed by the methodological gaps identified in this review, are urgently needed to generate robust evidence that can guide optimal treatment strat …
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a prevalent and sight-threatening ocular complication of diabetes, and one of the leading causes of vision loss and blindness among the working-age population worldwide. Driven by a growing understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying DR, treatment strategies have evolved from a sole focus on glycemic control to comprehensive, multi-targeted, and multimodal therapies. This study systematically summarizes the characteristics of current clinical trials focused on DR treatment and evaluates the employed research methodologies. The aim of this review is to explore methodological trends in specific domains, with the hope that such insights may inform future efforts to optimize trial design and improve trial quality. retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate real-world injection burden, treatment switching patterns, and visual outcomes in patients with diabetic macular edema (DME) receiving intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study included 563 eyes with DME treated with anti-VEGF agents and followed for at least 12 months. All eyes received an initial loading phase of three monthly bevacizumab injections followed by a pro re nata regimen. Primary outcomes were the number of injections and outpatient visits during the first year. Secondary outcomes included change in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), distribution of visual outcomes, and treatment switching patterns. Multivariable linear regression and generalized estimating equation (GEE) analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of visual outcomes.

retina.title: Predictive factors of functional and anatomical response to dexamethasone implant in refractory diabetic macular edema.

retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: To identify clinical and spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) biomarkers predictive of functional and anatomical response to intravitreal dexamethasone implant in refractory diabetic macular edema (DME). METHODS: This prospective longitudinal study included 185 eyes of 98 diabetic patients with center-involving DME refractory to a mean of 7.1±2.8 prior aflibercept (2mg) injections. All eyes received a 0.7mg intravitreal dexamethasone implant and were followed for at least 6 months, with a mean follow-up of 12.9±2.1 months. Functional outcome was assessed by best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA, logMAR) and anatomical outcome by central macular thickness (CMT) on SD-OCT. retina.abstract: Pathological neovascularization in the eye is a significant contributor to vision loss in diseases such as age-related macular degeneration and diabetic retinopathy. While anti-VEGF biologics are effective, they require repeated intravitreal injections. Here, we report a novel principle for designing photoactivatable VEGFR2 inhibitors, along with two examples, EYE1090 and EYE1118. Azido-functionalization in these molecules enables light-triggered receptor binding while preserving potent inhibition in the dark. Both compounds exhibit significantly enhanced activity upon exposure to green light that reaches the human retina, also in the elderly. In vitro, the compounds robustly inhibited angiogenesis and endothelial migration that was further potentiated by light. retina.abstract: INTRODUCTION: We sought to evaluate longitudinal visual and anatomical outcomes in treatment-naïve eyes with diabetic macular edema (DME) treated with aflibercept 8 mg in routine clinical practice. METHODS: Treatment-naïve eyes with DME receiving aflibercept 8 mg as first-line therapy under an observe-and-plan regimen were evaluated. Medical records were retrospectively reviewed, collecting data on best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), central retinal thickness (CRT), and follow-up visits. Longitudinal changes in BCVA and CRT were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with random effects to account for repeated measurements. Analyses were restricted to the first 300 days after baseline. RESULTS: A total of 95 eyes from 77 patients were eligible for evaluation. retina.abstract: Antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) intravitreal (IVT) therapy injections are routinely used to treat retinal diseases, including diabetic macular edema (DME), proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR), and neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD [nAMD]). Despite their robust efficacy, IVTs may not be effective for all patients and can impact patient quality of life due to the need for frequent injections, ocular adverse events (AEs), and challenges around the injection itself. Oral therapy enabling fewer injections may have a beneficial impact on patients' lives. Several are currently in development for retinal diseases, and existing data suggest that patients would prefer oral to injectable therapies. retina.summary: The three anti-VEGF treatments examined in this analysis demonstrated notable differences in systemic PKs. retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the systemic pharmacokinetics (PKs) of aflibercept, bevacizumab, and ranibizumab in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD), diabetic macular edema (DME), or retinal vein occlusion (RVO). METHODS: Prospective, open-label, nonrandomized clinical trial of patients with AMD, DME, or RVO who were antivascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) naïve or had not received anti-VEGF for ≥4 months. Patients received 3 monthly intravitreal injections of aflibercept 2.0 mg, bevacizumab 1.25 mg, or ranibizumab (0.5 mg for AMD/RVO, 0.3 mg for DME). The main outcome measures were serum PKs and plasma free-VEGF concentrations after the first and third injections. RESULTS: A total of 151 patients were included. Anti-VEGF treatment such as ranibizumab, bevacizumab, or aflibercept improved vision by 13.9-16.2 letters (best-corrected visual acuity) after 12 months versus baseline in patients with macular edema secondary to CRVO. A long-term study showed that reduced follow-up and fewer retreatments resulted in worsening visual acuity. Intravitreal therapy with anti-inflammatory agents stabilized visual acuity in CRVO. retina.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration is the most common cause of vision loss in elderly people in developed countries. Nowadays, in clinical practice, three anti-VEGF drugs are commonly used (bevacizumab, aflibercept and ranibizumab), requiring repeated intravitreal injections. In order to minimise the number of injections, research on intravitreal drug delivery systems (DDSs) is needed. In this review, the DDSs developed up to date regarding intravitreal anti-VEGF drugs have been summarised, which include systems as hydrogels, liposomes, microparticles, nanoparticles or implants. Most of the studies have focused on the extended in vitro release behaviour of the developed DDSs, but data as antibody bioactivity, biocompatibility or in vivo stability is sometimes scarce. retina.abstract: Polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (PCV) is an exudative age-related macular degeneration (AMD) subtype found more frequently among Asians than Caucasians. If untreated, it may lead to severe vision loss. PCV appears to be frequently underdiagnosed in Canada, although misdiagnosis of PCV as AMD carries the risk of inadequate treatment and unsatisfactory clinical outcomes. Diagnosis can be made on the basis of multimodal imaging, including optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography combined with colour fundus photography, or by other imaging techniques; the gold-standard indocyanine green angiography (ICGA) is not widely used in Canada. retina.summary: Women of childbearing age should be consulted regarding the potential adverse effects of anti-VEGF medications on fetal health and the risk of early pregnancy loss. However, the evidence for their effect on fetal and maternal health during pregnancy is very limited. The goal of this article is to accumulate evidence for the indications of anti-VEGF medications during pregnancy and their effects on maternal and fetal health. METHODS: Review of literature regarding anti-VEGF administration during pregnancy and using PubMed database without language or date limit. retina.summary: With the advent of anti-VEGF therapy, the prognosis of choroidal neovascularization has changed dramatically. Data from well-conducted clinical trials suggest that approved anti-VEGF drugs are effective and well tolerated.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of blindness, with an increasing incidence as the elderly population expands. Large, multi-center, randomized, clinical trials have been conducted exploring the safety and efficacy of anti-VEGF treatments. This paper aims to discuss the safety and efficacy of pegaptanib, ranibizumab, aflibercept and bevacizumab. New therapeutic agents and treatment strategies are also discussed. PROCEDURES: Evidence available from prospective, multicenter, clinical studies and from a selective literature search is utilized to present the results of VEGF inhibition in neovascular AMD and to generate evidence-based recommendations. retina.abstract: When evaluating the impact of vision-destroying diseases, pharmacologic therapies represent a significant cost to patients, insurance providers, and society. Currently, up to 11 million people in the United States have some form of age-related macular degeneration (AMD), which is one of the leading causes of vision loss in older Americans. Ophthalmologists have administered more than 6 million intravitreal injections of aflibercept, bevacizumab, pegaptanib, and ranibizumab last year. Comprehensive assessment requires managed care administrators and clinicians to understand the direct and indirect costs of vision loss as well as the comparative safety and efficacy profiles for each agent. In AMD, it is critical to understand the established and emerging treatment patterns.

retina.title: [Update from France Macula Federation: Treatment of Wet AMD].
retina.summary: The treatment of wet-AMD is more precisely codified than before. However, various strategies still coexist.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To update the recommendations of the France Macula Federation for treatment of wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD). METHODS: Analysis of literature and expert opinion. RESULTS: The FFM recommends initiating anti-VEGF therapy as soon as possible after diagnosis of exudative AMD. There has been no major change in the last several years concerning the procedure of intravitreal injection itself. However, the litigious points are discussed: simultaneous bilateral injection; antibiotic therapy; medico-legal aspects. All anti-VEGF strategies possess advantages and limitations. The strategy should be left to the ophthalmologists' preference. However, the chosen strategy should be explained to patients and strictly followed. CONCLUSION: The treatment of wet-AMD is more precisely codified than before. However, various strategies still coexist.

retina.abstract: Since their introduction in the late 2000s, anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) agents have become the first-line choice for center-involved diabetic macular edema (DME). Even with its proven effectiveness, there are still cases that do not respond satisfactorily. In those cases, a treatment option is to change to another anti-VEGF drug. In this paper, the authors review studies on switching between different anti-VEGF drugs in the treatment of persistent DME. An extensive bibliographic review was done using PubMed, Embase, and Scopus. Fourteen studies published from March 2010 to April 2017 reporting switching from anti-VEGF drugs in DME treatment were included. All reported good anatomical results after conversion; however, visual acuity outcomes showed great variability between publications. retina.summary: The duration of treatment-requiring nAMD was identified as primary risk factor for the onset of concomitant RPE atrophy after commencing therapy. Targeting concomitant atrophy in nAMD patients might improve the long-term prognosis of the disease.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to evaluate risk factors for the development of retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) atrophy in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). PROCEDURES: This post hoc analysis of the prospective RESPONSE study includes 52 therapy-naive nAMD patients without baseline RPE atrophy, who were treated with ≥9 anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) injections for ≥3 years. RPE atrophy was assessed via multimodal imaging. Baseline aqueous VEGF and serum complement levels (C3d/C3) were measured. Risk factors for atrophy development were evaluated via logistic regression analysis. RESULTS: Atrophy onset was significantly associated with the duration of nAMD (mean 5.34 years; odds ratio = 1.83, p = 0.012). retina.summary: Age-related macular degeneration and especially neovascular age-related macular degeneration is the leading cause of low vision in developed countries. Even though the introduction of anti-VEGF drugs in recent years completely changed the management of this condition, its cost, the need for repeated intravitreal injections, and loss of ef …
retina.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration and especially neovascular age-related macular degeneration is the leading cause of low vision in developed countries. Even though the introduction of anti-VEGF drugs in recent years completely changed the management of this condition, its cost, the need for repeated intravitreal injections, and loss of efficacy in the long term are still issues to deal with. Currently, a new generation of novel therapies under development is attempting to address some of these limitations. Some of the most prominent among them are new anti-VEGFs such as brolucizumab or abicipar, drugs against angiopoietin-2 receptor such as faricimab, sustained-release systems, or tyrosine kinase inhibitors. As regards dry age-related macular degeneration, neuroprotection, the complement pathway, and stem cell therapy are the most promising targets currently under investigation.

retina.abstract: The issue of macular retinal degeneration is one of the key areas of ophthalmology. Recent advances in the targeted delivery of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) suppressants have significantly impacted the patient's prognosis in the form of a significant deceleration in disease progression. Some of the drugs have gradually found their use in other indications (central retinal vein occlusion or diabetic macular edema). The following text gives a brief look at the physiology of VEGF, but not only in the eye, but throughout the human body, particularly in the context of adverse effects resulting from systemic inhibition of its effects.

retina.abstract: Diabetic macular edema (DME) represents the most common cause of vision loss in patients affected by diabetes mellitus. Although the pathophysiology of DME is not wholly understood, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) has been identified as a key contributor to the development of DME. In addition, latest information suggests that acute and chronic inflammatory changes occur, contributing to the DME pathogenesis. The current therapeutic approach for DME is mainly based on the administration of anti-VEGF molecules. In particular, VEGF-inhibitors that have been studied for diabetic retinopathy include pegaptanib, ranibizumab, bevacizumab, and aflibercept. The present review analyzes the main characteristics of each molecule, describing the most important results of clinical trails.

retina.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is one of the major complications of diabetes mellitus and a leading cause of visual loss. Diabetic macular edema (DME) is an ocular manifestation of the disease causing visual deterioration. The prevalence of visual impairment due to DME is estimated to be 5.4% in Europe. Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is overexpressed in diabetic eyes and plays a key role in the development of DME. VEGF levels were proven to be elevated in the vitreous and retina in patients with diabetic retinopathy. VEGF causes a breakdown of the blood-retinal barrier by influencing the tight junctions of retinal endothelial cells and leading to accumulation of fluid in the macula. Therefore, intravitreal VEGF inhibitors are ideal candidates to treat DME by counteracting VEGF overexpression. retina.abstract: A formulation of aflibercept for intravitreal injection (Eylea) is approved for the treatment of patients with exudative age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Aflibercept has a significantly higher affinity for Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-A compared with other monoclonal anti-VEGF antibodies. The VIEW 1 and 2 trials showed this drug achieves improved results in patients with exudative AMD similar to those obtained with monthly ranibizumab, using a bimonthly treatment regimen after a loading dose of three intravitreal injections, which translates to less use of healthcare resources. retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: The introduction of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) drugs to ophthalmology has revolutionized the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). Despite this significant progress, gaps and challenges persist in the diagnosis of nAMD, initiation of treatment, and management of frequent intravitreal injections. Thus, nAMD remains a leading cause of blindness in the United States. OBJECTIVE: To present current knowledge, evidence, and expert perspectives on anti-VEGF therapies in nAMD to support managed care professionals and providers in decision making and collaborative strategies to overcome barriers to optimize anti-VEGF treatment outcomes among nAMD patients. retina.title: Identifying Genetic Risk Factors for Diabetic Macular Edema and the Response to Treatment.
retina.summary: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the most common microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus (DM). DR is complex and the term encompasses several clinical subtypes of diabetic eye disease, including diabetic macular edema (DME), the most frequent cause of central vision loss in DR patients. …
retina.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the most common microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus (DM). DR is complex and the term encompasses several clinical subtypes of diabetic eye disease, including diabetic macular edema (DME), the most frequent cause of central vision loss in DR patients. Both genetic and environmental factors contribute to the pathophysiology of DR and its subtypes. While numerous studies have identified several susceptibility genes for DR, few have investigated the impact of genetics on DME susceptibility. This review will focus on the current literature surrounding genetic risk factors associated with DME. We will also highlight the small number of studies investigating the genetics of response to antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injection, which is used to treat DME.

retina.abstract: In this era of evidence-based medicine, significant progress has been made in the field of pharmacotherapeutics for the management of diabetic macular edema (DME). A. number of landmark clinical trials have provided strong evidence of the safety and efficacy of agents such as anti-vascular endothelial growth factors for the treatment of DME. Decades of clinical research, ranging from the early treatment of diabetic retinopathy study to the present-day randomized clinical trials (RCTs) testing novel agents, have shifted the goal of therapy from preventing vision loss to ensuring a maximum visual gain. Systematic study designs have provided robust data with an attempt to optimize the treatment regimens including the choice of the agent and timing of therapy. retina.title: Biological, preclinical and clinical characteristics of inhibitors of vascular endothelial growth factors.
retina.summary: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) plays an important role in the pathophysiology of several sight-threatening retinal disorders such as age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular edema and proliferative diabetic retinopathy. The discovery of anti-VEGF agents has revolutionized our treatment of these conditions. …
retina.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) plays an important role in the pathophysiology of several sight-threatening retinal disorders such as age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular edema and proliferative diabetic retinopathy. The discovery of anti-VEGF agents has revolutionized our treatment of these conditions. There are 4 anti-VEGF agents that are either approved or in common use in ophthalmology, namely pegaptanib (Macugen, Pfizer), ranibizumab (Lucentis, Novartis), aflibercept or VEGF Trap-Eye (EYLEA, Bayer) and bevacizumab (Avastin, Roche). There are differences between them. In this review, the differences are discussed in detail. Furthermore, an attempt is made to explain some of the clinical trial data based on their differences in ocular efficacy, duration of action, and local and systemic safety concerns.

These landmark clinical trials such as ANCHOR and MARINA and, more recently, the Comparison of AMD Treatment Trials and VIEW studies have revolutionized the management of neovascular AMD. While AMD continues to remain a leading cause of severe visual loss worldwide, advances in pharmacotherapeutics have led to substantial improvements in the outcome of these patients. The introduction of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor agents has resulted in improvement of visual outcomes and has had a positive impact on the quality of life among elderly population. retina.abstract: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and diabetic macular edema (DME) are major causes of visual impairment in the elderly population worldwide. With the aging population, the prevalence of neovascular AMD and DME has increased substantially over the recent years. Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) has been implicated as playing an important role in the pathogenesis of both neovascular AMD and DME. Since its introduction in 2006, ranibizumab, a recombinant, humanized, monoclonal antibody fragment against all isoforms of VEGF-A, has revolutionized the treatment of neovascular AMD and DME. The efficacy and safety of ranibizumab in neovascular AMD has been demonstrated in the ANCHOR and MARINA trials. Although initially used for the treatment of choroidal neovascularization in neovascular age-related macular degeneration, their application has spread rapidly for other indications as their outcomes have often outperformed previously existing treatments. retina.summary: With no difference in clinical effectiveness, longer treatment intervals for aflibercept should be investigated.
retina.abstract: AIM: A hospital-wide, unselected switch of ranibizumab to aflibercept in treatment of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) allowed us to compare the clinical effectiveness of these agents. METHOD: In a single-center before-after, observational study design new AMD-patients started with aflibercept treatment in 2013-2014 were compared with a control group of AMD-patients on ranibizumab before the switch. RESULTS: The mean difference in visual acuity (in logMAR units) after 1 year was comparable (+0.012 [aflibercept, n = 37] vs +0.17 [ranibizumab, n = 30], p = 0.154). However, the aflibercept-group did receive more intravitreal injections (5.8 vs 4.7 injections, p = 0.004) and were treated longer (265.7 vs 197.7 days; p = 0.011). CONCLUSION: With no difference in clinical effectiveness, longer treatment intervals for aflibercept should be investigated.

retina.abstract: The introduction of antivascular endothelial growth factor agents such as ranibizumab and aflibercept has revolutionized the management of neovascular age-related macular degeneration. A number of randomized clinical trials have shown that ranibizumab and aflibercept produce similar efficacy and safety outcomes. Most of the switching studies published to date show that efficacy benefits are uncontrolled, retrospective trials with limitations in terms of their selection, monitoring, numbers, and assessment criteria. Based on the published literature to date, we propose arguments for and against switching antivascular endothelial growth factor agents, provide our own perspective on this topic, and suggest a focus for future research.

retina.abstract: Diabetic macular edema (DME), defined as a retinal thickening involving or approaching the center of the macula, represents the most common cause of vision loss in patients affected by diabetes mellitus. In the last few years, many diagnostic tools have been proven useful in the detection and the monitoring of the features characterizing DME. On the other hand, several therapeutic approaches can now be proposed on the basis of the DME-specific characteristics. The aim of the present chapter is to thoroughly delineate the clinical and morpho functional characteristics of DME and its current treatment perspectives. The pathogenesis and the course of DME require a complex approach with multidisciplinary intervention both at the systemic and local levels.

retina.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF-A) is a key cytokine in the development of normal blood vessels as well as the development of vessels in tumors and other tissues undergoing abnormal angiogenesis. Here, we review the molecular engineering of two humanized antibodies derived from a common mouse anti-VEGF antibody--bevacizumab, a full-length IgG1 approved for the treatment of specified cancer indications, and ranibizumab, an affinity-matured antibody Fab domain approved for use in age-related macular degeneration (AMD). retina.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of blindness in patients over 50 years in the developed world. The wet form of AMD is responsible for the majority of severe vision loss. VEGF-A is a key component in the development of wet AMD. Ranibizumab is an anti-VEGF agent that has established itself as the gold standard in the treatment of neovascular AMD. Herein, we review the pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, efficacy and safety of ranibizumab. AREAS COVERED: Since its approval in 2006, ranibizumab has revolutionized the treatment of wet AMD. In two pivotal Phase III trials, MARINA and ANCHOR, ranibizumab (0.5 mg) prevented moderate visual loss in 90 and 96% of patients, respectively, and improved vision by 15 letters or more in 33 and 40% of patients, respectively. retina.abstract: Blood vessels deliver oxygen and nutrients to every part of the body, but also nourish diseases such as cancer. Over the past decade, our understanding of the molecular mechanisms of angiogenesis (blood vessel growth) has increased at an explosive rate and has led to the approval of anti-angiogenic drugs for cancer and eye diseases. So far, hundreds of thousands of patients have benefited from blockers of the angiogenic protein vascular endothelial growth factor, but limited efficacy and resistance remain outstanding problems. Recent preclinical and clinical studies have shown new molecular targets and principles, which may provide avenues for improving the therapeutic benefit from anti-angiogenic strategies.

retina.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is an endothelial cell-specific mitogen in vitro and an angiogenic inducer in a variety of in vivo models. Hypoxia has been shown to be a major inducer of VEGF gene transcription. The tyrosine kinases Flt-1 (VEGFR-1) and Flk-1/KDR (VEGFR-2) are high-affinity VEGF receptors. retina.abstract: In 2008, we published the first set of guidelines for standardizing research in autophagy. Since then, this topic has received increasing attention, and many scientists have entered the field. Our knowledge base and relevant new technologies have also been expanding. Thus, it is important to formulate on a regular basis updated guidelines for monitoring autophagy in different organisms. Despite numerous reviews, there continues to be confusion regarding acceptable methods to evaluate autophagy, especially in multicellular eukaryotes. Here, we present a set of guidelines for investigators to select and interpret methods to examine autophagy and related processes, and for reviewers to provide realistic and reasonable critiques of reports that are focused on these processes. Today, there are promising data from ongoing clinical trials for the treatment of age-related macular degeneration and respiratory syncytial virus. retina.summary: Active resolution of acute inflammation is a previously unrecognized interface between innate and adaptive immunity. Once thought to be a passive process, the resolution of inflammation is now shown to involve active biochemical programmes that enable inflamed tissues to return to homeostasis. …
retina.abstract: Active resolution of acute inflammation is a previously unrecognized interface between innate and adaptive immunity. Once thought to be a passive process, the resolution of inflammation is now shown to involve active biochemical programmes that enable inflamed tissues to return to homeostasis. This Review presents new cellular and molecular mechanisms for the resolution of inflammation, revealing key roles for eicosanoids, such as lipoxins, and recently discovered families of endogenous chemical mediators, termed resolvins and protectins. These mediators have anti-inflammatory and pro-resolution properties, thereby protecting organs from collateral damage, stimulating the clearance of inflammatory debris and promoting mucosal antimicrobial defence.

Elucidation of the molecular regulation of VEGF and the transformative development of multiple therapeutic pathways targeting VEGF directly or indirectly is a powerful case study of how fundamental research can guide innovation and translation. retina.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors are the leading platform for gene delivery for the treatment of a variety of human diseases. Recent advances in developing clinically desirable AAV capsids, optimizing genome designs and harnessing revolutionary biotechnologies have contributed substantially to the growth of the gene therapy field. Preclinical and clinical successes in AAV-mediated gene replacement, gene silencing and gene editing have helped AAV gain popularity as the ideal therapeutic vector, with two AAV-based therapeutics gaining regulatory approval in Europe or the United States. Continued study of AAV biology and increased understanding of the associated therapeutic challenges and limitations will build the foundation for future clinical success.

dryeye.abstract: On 15 July 2026, the Secretary of War announced that the Department of War will begin annual testosterone deficiency screening for male Active Duty and Reserve Component personnel aged 30 and older as part of the periodic health assessment, with screening available on request to younger servicemembers. This policy will increase testosterone testing and may increase testosterone replacement therapy (TRT). Primary care, flight, and operational medicine providers will be on the front line of a hormonal intervention with possible ocular implications. This Commentary summarizes the ophthalmic manifestations of low and elevated testosterone states relevant to a military population and proposes pragmatic recommendations for providers implementing this initiative. dryeye.title: Ocular Abnormalities in Multi-transfused Patients with Beta-thalassemia: A Cross-sectional Study from South India.
dryeye.summary: Ocular abnormalities are common among beta-thalassemia major patients, with some correlating with serum ferritin levels. Regular ophthalmic screening should be integrated into multidisciplinary care to facilitate early detection and management. …
dryeye.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate ocular findings in transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia patients and determine whether they exhibit a higher incidence of ocular abnormalities compared to healthy controls owing to effects of iron overload and chelation therapy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted in the Departments of Ophthalmology and Pediatrics at a tertiary care center in South India. Patients aged 10-18 years with transfusion-dependent thalassemia, receiving regular blood transfusions (every 2-4 weeks for at least 2 years), were included as cases. Age- and sex-matched healthy individuals without ocular complaints served as controls. dryeye.title: Dry eye disease in thyroid eye disease: A narrative review of pathogenic mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
dryeye.summary: Dry eye disease (DED) is a common and persistent manifestation of thyroid eye disease (TED), often remaining symptomatic despite apparent control of orbital inflammation or systemic thyroid dysfunction. …
dryeye.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a common and persistent manifestation of thyroid eye disease (TED), often remaining symptomatic despite apparent control of orbital inflammation or systemic thyroid dysfunction. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence within an integrated mechanistic framework relating the overlapping contributors to TED-associated DED to disease phenotype, therapeutic limitations, and opportunities for more targeted management. A literature review was conducted using PubMed and Scopus through March 2026, using broad MeSH and free-text terms related to TED, DED, ocular surface disease, and treatment, with manual screening of relevant references. dryeye.title: Topical Cyclosporine in Ophthalmology: Current Formulations, Clinical Applications, Advantages, and Limitations.
dryeye.summary: Cyclosporine A (CsA) is a calcineurin-inhibiting immunomodulator that suppresses T cell-mediated inflammation, a central mechanism in the pathogenesis of many ocular surface diseases. …
dryeye.abstract: Cyclosporine A (CsA) is a calcineurin-inhibiting immunomodulator that suppresses T cell-mediated inflammation, a central mechanism in the pathogenesis of many ocular surface diseases. Following the systemic use of CsA in ophthalmology, topical formulations were developed to provide local immunomodulation at the ocular surface while keeping systemic absorption negligible. Since the approval of the first commercial ophthalmic emulsion in 2002, topical CsA has become a cornerstone disease-modifying therapy. Unlike corticosteroids, topical CsA provides sustained anti-inflammatory control without the long-term risks of glaucoma and cataract. dryeye.title: Changing Patterns of Dry Eye Disease Management in Korea: A Nationwide 10-Year Analysis.
dryeye.summary: Over the past decade, DED management in Korea shifted toward the anti-inflammatory cyclosporine, the mucin and water secretagogue diquafosol, and preservative-free single-use formulations. …
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate long-term trends in treated dry eye disease (DED) prevalence and medication prescribing patterns in Korea using a nationwide mandatory insurance claims database. DESIGN: Retrospective nationwide clinical cohort study. PARTICIPANTS: Patients identified from the Korean NHIS mandatory claims database (2014-2023). METHODS: DED was defined by at least one relevant ICD-10 diagnosis code together with at least one prescription for a DED-related topical medication within the same calendar year. Annual overall, sex-specific, and age-specific prevalence was calculated using the corresponding mid-year resident population. Medication classes and single-use versus multi-use formulations were evaluated. dryeye.title: Fatty Acids for the Treatment of Ocular Diseases and Ocular Drug Delivery.
dryeye.summary: The intricate anatomical and physiological barriers of the eye severely limit the bioavailability of conventional topical therapies, necessitating innovative strategies. In this review, fatty acids are presented as versatile agents functioning in two distinct roles. …
dryeye.abstract: The intricate anatomical and physiological barriers of the eye severely limit the bioavailability of conventional topical therapies, necessitating innovative strategies. In this review, fatty acids are presented as versatile agents functioning in two distinct roles. As bioactive lipids, specific fatty acids exert disease-modifying effects, offering novel pharmacological interventions for ocular surface and posterior segment disorders, including dry eye syndrome, uveitis, and retinal degeneration. Concurrently, beyond their biological activity, fatty acids serve as structural components in formulation design; their physicochemical properties, particularly varying chain lengths and degrees of unsaturation, enable the construction of advanced ocular drug delivery systems with substantially enhanced ocular bioavailability. dryeye.title: Proteomics Identifies TRAP5 as a Candidate Marker of Residual Inflammation After Optimal Pulse Technology in Experimental Meibomian Gland Dysfunction.
dryeye.summary: OPT produced partial but incomplete recovery in experimental MGD. Proteomics identified a residual post-treatment molecular signature and highlighted TRAP5 as a candidate molecule for future tissue-level validation and mechanistic investigation.
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine whether residual clinical, tissue-level, and molecular abnormalities persist after optimal pulse technology (OPT) in experimental meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD), and to identify candidate proteins associated with the post-treatment state. METHODS: MGD was induced in rabbits by complete Freund's adjuvant injection into the eyelid margin and palpebral conjunctiva. Animals were assigned to control, MGD, and MGD + OPT groups. Eyelid margin abnormalities were scored from standardized photographs. Histopathologic changes were assessed by hematoxylin and eosin staining, and lipid-related abnormalities were evaluated by oil red O staining. Remaining eyelid tissues were analyzed by label-free quantitative proteomics and pathway enrichment. TRAP5 was further assessed in RAW264.7 macrophages as an exploratory in vitro model. dryeye.title: Three-Times-Daily 5% Diquafosol Versus Six-Times-Daily 3% Diquafosol for Dry Eye Disease: A Randomized, Double-Masked, Multicenter Phase 3 Noninferiority Trial.
dryeye.summary: This study found that 5% diquafosol demonstrated clinical efficacy and AE rates equivalent to those of 3% diquafosol, despite a halved dosing frequency. Therefore, 5% diquafosol may offer a more convenient treatment option for DED patients by reducing frequency.
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the safety and effectiveness of 5% diquafosol eye drops for treating dry eye disease (DED) in a double-blind, multicenter, phase 3 noninferiority clinical trial. METHODS: Of the 271 participants randomized to receive either 5% diquafosol (TJO-083) 3 times per day or an active control [3% sodium diquafosol; Diquas-S (DQS)] 6 times per day for 12 weeks, 268 were included in the full analysis set. The outcome measures included corneal fluorescein staining score (CFS), conjunctival staining score, tear break-up time (TBUT), the Schirmer test, Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), and adverse events (AEs). RESULTS: Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics related to DED did not differ significantly between the 2 groups. dryeye.title: Implementation of pharmaceutical interviews with patients treated with autologous serum eye drops.
dryeye.summary: Pharmaceutical interviews are feasible and well accepted in this population. They improve patient knowledge, support adherence to a complex care pathway and may reduce treatment interruptions. The tools developed could be implemented in other hospitals to improve safety and continuity of care.
dryeye.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Autologous serum eye drops are sterile compounded hospital preparations indicated for severe dry eye syndrome and require a complex manufacturing and dispensing process. This organisational complexity may expose patients to misuse and treatment interruption. Although pharmaceutical interviews have demonstrated benefits in chronic diseases, their implementation in patients treated with autologous serum eye drops has not been reported. This study aimed to evaluate the implementation of personalised pharmaceutical interviews in this setting. METHODS: A multidisciplinary collaboration between the hospital pharmacy and the ophthalmology department was established in a university hospital to structure the care pathway and implement pharmaceutical interviews. This descriptive survey questionnaire-based study aimed to evaluate prevalence and factors associated with dry eye symptoms after refractive surgery among survey respondents using ocular surface disea …
dryeye.abstract: Refractive surgery corrects vision using different corneal techniques; however, dry eye disease (DED) is one of its commonest side effects. This descriptive survey questionnaire-based study aimed to evaluate prevalence and factors associated with dry eye symptoms after refractive surgery among survey respondents using ocular surface disease index (OSDI) questionnaire in Saudi Arabia. Four hundred and thirty nine participants were included. Dry eye OSDI scores compared across different epidemiological risk factors, focusing on refractive surgery type and postoperative duration. Photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) or Femtosecond (FS)-LASIK, and small incision lenticule extraction procedures were performed on 201 (45.79%), 222 (50.56%), and 16 (3.65%) participants, respectively. dryeye.title: Spectrum of ocular adverse events associated with first-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors: real-world experience and a proposed management algorithm from a tertiary cancer centre in India.
dryeye.summary: First-generation EGFR-TKIs are associated with a characteristic spectrum of ocular surface and adnexal toxicities, occurring more commonly with erlotinib. Most events are manageable with timely ophthalmologic intervention, underscoring the importance of early recognition and multidisciplinary care to minimise morbidity and maintain treatm …
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the incidence, clinical spectrum, and outcomes of clinically significant ocular toxicities associated with first-generation epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) in a real-world tertiary cancer centre in India. METHODS: This retrospective observational study included adult patients treated with first-generation EGFR-TKIs between March 2023 and October 2025 for EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer or recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Patients who developed Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5.0 grade ≥ 2 ocular toxicity with complete oncologic and ophthalmologic records were analysed. dryeye.title: A Prospective Cohort Study of Clinical Outcomes, Tear Cytokines and Proteomic Profiles Following Insular Infraorbital Neurovascular Pedicle Labial Salivary Gland Transplantation for Severe Dry Eye Disease.
dryeye.summary: IINPLSGT was associated with improvements in symptoms and clinical signs of severe DED, accompanied by reductions in tear osmolarity and inflammatory cytokine levels during follow-up. …
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: Insular infraorbital neurovascular pedicle labial salivary gland transplantation (IINPLSGT) is an innovative procedure for the treatment of severe dry eye disease (DED). We aim to evaluate changes in clinical parameters, tear osmolarity, inflammatory cytokine levels, and proteomic profiles following IINPLSGT for severe dry eye patients. METHODS: A single-center, prospective exploratory study was conducted in 10 patients diagnosed with severe DED who underwent IINPLSGT surgery. The Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), tear break-up time (TBUT), Schirmer I test (SIt), corneal fluorescein staining (CFS), ocular manifestations and tear osmolarity were assessed before and after treatment. dryeye.title: Pathological remodeling and functional evolution of the corneal nervous system in ocular surface dyshomeostasis.
dryeye.summary: The corneal nerve plexus is essential to ocular surface homeostasis through sensory detection, trophic support, epithelial repair, blinking, and lacrimal reflexes. In dry eye disease (DED), chronic hyperosmolar, inflammatory, mechanical, and age-related stressors alter nerve morphology and function, contributing to reduced nerve density,  …
dryeye.abstract: The corneal nerve plexus is essential to ocular surface homeostasis through sensory detection, trophic support, epithelial repair, blinking, and lacrimal reflexes. In dry eye disease (DED), chronic hyperosmolar, inflammatory, mechanical, and age-related stressors alter nerve morphology and function, contributing to reduced nerve density, aberrant regeneration, microneuroma formation, sensory loss, and peripheral or central sensitization. This review summarizes the ultrastructure of corneal innervation and the molecular basis of corneal sensory transduction, with emphasis on TRPM8, TRPV1, TRPA1, Piezo2, and acid-sensing ion channels. It then examines bidirectional neuroimmune signaling involving dendritic cells, cytokines, neuropeptides, and diminished neurotrophic support. dryeye.title: Unraveling neuro-immune crosstalk in dry eye disease: Corneal neuropathy, lacrimal dysfunction, and therapeutic horizons.
dryeye.summary: Dry eye disease (DED) is a heterogeneous, multifactorial disorder characterized by loss of tear-film and/or ocular-surface homeostasis, with epithelial stress, inflammation, and neurosensory abnormalities contributing to varying degrees across clinical phenotypes. …
dryeye.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a heterogeneous, multifactorial disorder characterized by loss of tear-film and/or ocular-surface homeostasis, with epithelial stress, inflammation, and neurosensory abnormalities contributing to varying degrees across clinical phenotypes. This review synthesizes current evidence within a circuit-based sensory-autonomic-immune framework linking corneal sensory dysfunction to lacrimal dysfunction. We emphasize two anatomically and functionally distinct adrenergic checkpoints: norepinephrine (NE)-Adra1a-Ucp2 signaling in lacrimal acinar and myoepithelial cells, which restrains tear secretion, and epithelial NE-ADRB2 signaling, which reduces NGF/GDNF support and limits sensory nerve regeneration. dryeye.title: NanoMiLens (Nano-Micelle Loaded Hydrogel Contact Lenses) of Tofacitinib Citrate: Amalgamation, Development, Optimization and Characterization.
dryeye.summary: Dry eye disease (DED) is a multifactorial inflammatory eye disease caused mainly by immune dysregulation through JAK/STAT, which leads to a turbulent tear film, damage to the corneal epithelia, and poor visualization. Topical therapies of the conventional type show less ocular bioavailability with quick precorneal excretion. …
dryeye.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a multifactorial inflammatory eye disease caused mainly by immune dysregulation through JAK/STAT, which leads to a turbulent tear film, damage to the corneal epithelia, and poor visualization. Topical therapies of the conventional type show less ocular bioavailability with quick precorneal excretion. This research was done to design and test a new NanoMiLens system loaded with Tofacitinib Citrate (TFC), which is a selective JAK inhibitor, in order to have a controlled and prolonged contact lens delivery manageable with DED. TFC Polymeric Nano-Micelles (PoT-PNMs) were prepared using a thin-film hydration method employing Poloxamer 407 as the amphiphilic polymer and Tween 80 as the stabilizing surfactant in acetone, then rehydrated with simulated tear fluid. dryeye.summary: The BCMA×CD3 bispecific T cell engager (TCE) transforms targeted immunotherapy but remains constrained by ex vivo manufacturing and systemic delivery, limiting its application in autoimmune disorders. …
dryeye.abstract: The BCMA×CD3 bispecific T cell engager (TCE) transforms targeted immunotherapy but remains constrained by ex vivo manufacturing and systemic delivery, limiting its application in autoimmune disorders. Here, we use a T cell-targeted integration-deficient lentiviral vector (T-IDLE) to program endogenous T cells to secrete BCMA×CD3 TCEs directly in vivo. In a murine model of Sjögren's syndrome-associated dry eye, a single intravenous administration of T-IDLESTCE achieves deep but time-limited depletion of plasmablasts and plasma cells, reverses lacrimal gland inflammation, and restores tear production without detectable off-target transduction. Longitudinal studies in cynomolgus monkeys demonstrate plasma cell clearance and a favorable safety profile. dryeye.title: Recombinant Human Lysozyme Attenuates Hyperosmolarity-Induced Dry Eye Disease by Suppressing Oxidative Stress and Modulating NLRP3 Inflammasome Signaling.
dryeye.summary: Given the escalating global prevalence of dry eye disease (DED) and the inadequacy of current palliative management, this study was to evaluate thetherapeutic potential of recombinant lysozyme (rlysozyme) and investigate underlying mechanisms. …
dryeye.abstract: Given the escalating global prevalence of dry eye disease (DED) and the inadequacy of current palliative management, this study was to evaluate thetherapeutic potential of recombinant lysozyme (rlysozyme) and investigate underlying mechanisms. Human corneal epithelial cells (HCEC) were subjected to hyperosmotic stress and treated with graded rlysozyme. Cell viability, wound healing, barrier integrity, oxidative stress, cytokines, and mitochondrial function were evaluated by MTS and scratch assays, immunofluorescent staining, ELISA, qRT-PCR, and flow cytometry. dryeye.title: Optimizing Dry Eye Disease Management with Topical Anti-Inflammatory or Immunomodulatory Drugs Combined with Artificial Tears: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Trials.
dryeye.summary: Background/Objectives: Dry eye disease (DED) is an ocular condition that significantly impairs quality of life. In mild cases, it is commonly treated with artificial tears (ATs), while more advanced cases are managed with immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory drugs. …
dryeye.abstract: Background/Objectives: Dry eye disease (DED) is an ocular condition that significantly impairs quality of life. In mild cases, it is commonly treated with artificial tears (ATs), while more advanced cases are managed with immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory drugs. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of topical anti-inflammatory drugs, immunomodulatory drugs, AT, and their combination in adults with DED. Methods: The protocol was registered in the PROSPERO database (CRD420251245079). Intervention studies were searched in MEDLINE and Scopus databases. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed with the R software (version 4.5.2). Results: A total of 42 studies were included in the meta-analysis of efficacy and 46 in the analysis of safety. dryeye.title: Documented Dry Eye Disease in Patients Receiving Topical Antiglaucoma Therapy: Associations with Treatment Characteristics.
dryeye.summary: Background/Objectives: Chronic topical antiglaucoma therapy may affect the ocular surface. We assessed documented dry eye disease (DED) and its associations with active-ingredient burden, treatment duration, and preservative exposure. …
dryeye.abstract: Background/Objectives: Chronic topical antiglaucoma therapy may affect the ocular surface. We assessed documented dry eye disease (DED) and its associations with active-ingredient burden, treatment duration, and preservative exposure. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 357 adults receiving topical antiglaucoma therapy at a tertiary center who had complete treatment and ocular-surface data. Ocular-surface testing was prompted by symptoms or clinical judgment. The first eligible visit identified during chronological record review was analyzed for each patient. DED was based on the treating ophthalmologist's documented diagnosis. Logistic regression evaluated treatment-related factors. dryeye.summary: Background/Objectives: Sjögren's syndrome (SS) is a systemic autoimmune disease characterized by lacrimal and salivary gland dysfunction, leading to dry eye and dry mouth. This study aimed to explore the potential associations between oxidative stress-mediated immune and apoptotic responses in Sjögren's syndrome dry eye (SSDE) and to comp …
dryeye.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sjögren's syndrome (SS) is a systemic autoimmune disease characterized by lacrimal and salivary gland dysfunction, leading to dry eye and dry mouth. This study aimed to explore the potential associations between oxidative stress-mediated immune and apoptotic responses in Sjögren's syndrome dry eye (SSDE) and to computationally predict theoretical interacting candidates. Methods: We enrolled 16 SSDE patients and 15 healthy controls to assess key clinical parameters. The study utilized conjunctival impression cytology, RNA-seq, and bioinformatics to identify exploratory transcriptomic signatures. Gene expression levels were then assessed using real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). dryeye.title: Frequency and Spectrum of Ocular Manifestations Among Patients With Systemic Autoimmune Rheumatic Diseases: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
dryeye.summary: A total of 210 unique eligible patients were included. The mean age was 37.6 ± 12.8 years, and 164 (78.1%) were female. Rheumatoid arthritis was the most common rheumatic disease (82, 39.0%), followed by systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) (57, 27.1%) and spondyloarthritis (26, 12.4%). …
dryeye.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases may cause a wide range of ocular manifestations, ranging from dry eye disease to potentially vision-threatening inflammatory and vascular complications. Data regarding the frequency and spectrum of ocular involvement among patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases in Pakistan remain limited. This study aimed to determine the frequency and spectrum of documented ocular manifestations among patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases. METHODS: A retrospective, hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted at Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan, using medical records from May 2026 to August 2026.
